text: The family of Michael Brown, the black teenager shot dead by a policeman, say they are crushed by the grand jury's decision not to charge Darren Wilson. Widespread protests erupted across 13 American cities Tuesday evening following the controversial grand jury decision, with Ferguson experiencing renewed unrest as demonstrators clashed with law enforcement and set a police vehicle ablaze near the town hall.The deployment of approximately 2,000 National Guard troops in Ferguson on Tuesday—nearly triple Monday's 700-person contingent—helped contain the violence compared to the previous night's widespread rioting and looting that saw over a dozen buildings torched. Forty-four arrests were made during Tuesday's confrontations.Missouri Governor Jay Nixon credited the ramped up presence of National Guard forces as helpful while indicating he would assess whether additional resources might be necessary.Wednesday brought continued demonstrations as roughly 200 protesters assembled outside St. Louis City Hall for a mock trial targeting Mr. Wilson. Several demonstrators breached the building while chanting shame, shame, prompting police to implement lockdown procedures, according to AP reports. Two individuals were reportedly detained.The outrage extended far beyond Missouri's borders, with Tuesday night protests documented in Philadelphia, Seattle, Albuquerque, New York, Cleveland, Los Angeles, Oakland, Minneapolis, Atlanta, Portland, Chicago and Boston. While most demonstrations remained peaceful, Oakland, California, witnessed rioting as protesters ignited street fires. Los Angeles authorities arrested 130 demonstrators for disorderly conduct, the LA Times reported, while police in Boston, Atlanta and New York also made several arrests, Reuters confirmed.The controversy stems from the August 9 shooting of Michael Brown by white police officer Darren Wilson in Ferguson, Missouri, which initially sparked widespread protests.Following Monday's verdict, Mr. Wilson defended his actions to ABC broadcaster, stating he maintained a clean conscience. Wilson described how Mr. Brown allegedly forced him back into his patrol car, struck him, and attempted to grab his weapon, comparing the struggle to feeling like a five-year-old holding on to [US wrestler] Hulk Hogan.However, Mr. Brown's parents rejected Wilson's version of events during Wednesday interviews. His mother, Lesley McSpadden, characterized Wilson's statements to NBC as adding insult after injury and being disrespectful.I don't believe a word of it. I know my son far too well... Our son doesn't have a history of violence, McSpadden told CBS in a separate interview.Michael Brown Sr. expressed feeling hurt and crushed by the verdict during his own interview. The grieving father accused prosecutors of having crucified his character through terrible statements about his son.Despite his anguish, Brown Sr. appealed for peaceful demonstrations: My son was a good guy, a quiet guy. So in his name, I want to keep it on a positive note.Brown's supporters maintain he was attempting to surrender when Wilson fatally shot him. However, state prosecutors argued that physical evidence contradicted several witness testimonies.Ferguson's predominantly African-American community had demanded murder charges against Wilson, but the grand jury—comprising nine white and three black members—declined to indict the officer. While this decision eliminates potential state criminal charges, the US Justice Department continues its federal investigation into possible civil rights violations.From Chicago Tuesday, President Barack Obama condemned the destructive behaviour and criminal acts of rioting, declaring there was no excuse for such actions. Nevertheless, Obama acknowledged that many communities of colour perceive laws as not being enforced uniformly or fairly, announcing he had directed Attorney General Eric Holder to examine measures for rebuilding community trust.

text: Peterhead boss Jim McInally hailed his League Two side after they stunned Hearts in the League Cup. McInally expressed his satisfaction with the outcome, declaring I thought we deserved it following Rory McAllister's decisive late penalty that eliminated the Premiership side 2-1 at Balmoor Stadium.Speaking to BBC's Sportsound, McInally elaborated: For 70 minutes we were probably the better side and we got the break at the end.The Group B clash saw Jason Brown's early header give the League Two side the advantage, before Kyle Lafferty restored parity with his fourth strike across three matches. As the League Cup tie seemed headed for penalties and the pursuit of a bonus point, McAllister's spot-kick delivered a memorable victory.McInally reflected on the timing of their winner: Ironically, we scored or got our penalty when we had really tired in the last 10 minutes and (were) hanging on.The manager praised his squad's performance, stating: I'm so happy for the players because they concentrated for the whole game and passed it well when they needed to.He highlighted the logistical challenges facing his part-time players: [Playing] twice in four days is hard for part-timers. A lot of these guys have just come up from Glasgow today. Willie Gibson and Greg Fleming, the goalkeeper, [have come] from Dumfries.The contrast with their opponents' preparation wasn't lost on McInally: Hearts were up here last night resting. So, it makes it even better and the big thing is we have a chance of going through now if we can win on Saturday [against Elgin City].Hearts head coach Ian Cathro acknowledged his disappointment while recognizing the transitional nature of his squad. We expected a difficult game, he explained. And it's always the case, particularly at the start of these games when you play against teams from the lower leagues.Cathro admitted his team's shortcomings: We're disappointed and we should be doing better in these situations but we're at a stage where new players are here and we're progressing some things and things are a work in progress.Despite showing improvement during the match, Hearts couldn't capitalize on their opportunities. We started to get ourselves in front in the game, we had some energy and played with a little more urgency as things progressed. But we didn't take our chances and maybe some of our decisions in the final third weren't quite right, Cathro analyzed.He remained optimistic about the team's development: We suffered because of that but, as I said, there are a lot of new relationships inside the team and there's a lot of positive things building across all three [League Cup] games and we'll continue to work to get ourselves ready and improving.Looking ahead, Cathro emphasized his team's standards: We're disappointed with the result and have expectations which are higher than that - we move forward very quickly and focus on Saturday [against Dunfermline at Tynecastle].

text: The EU's latest Earth observer has returned its first pictures. The European Space Agency's Sentinel-3a satellite, launched just two weeks ago, has delivered its inaugural images while beginning its specialized mission to monitor Earth's oceans through measurements of sea surface color, temperature, and height.Marine biologists studying global water health and weather forecasters will find this data invaluable for their work. The spacecraft's Ocean and Land Colour Instrument (OLCI) captured the debut images, showcasing the Strait of Gibraltar, California's coastline, and the ice-blanketed Svalbard archipelago.Despite its name suggesting ocean-only operations, OLCI extends its capabilities to terrestrial monitoring, including tracking vegetation conditions across the globe.Volker Liebig, director of Earth observation at the European Space Agency (Esa), explained the timeline: We received the first images on 29 February, but we've had to spend a bit of time working on them to get the calibration right. He acknowledged to BBC News that while not all satellite systems are fully operational, releasing these pictures was deemed important.Several months of testing remain before routine observations commence.The satellite represents one component of the European Union's ambitious Copernicus programme, a multi-billion-euro initiative designed to fuel diverse applications. These range from air quality monitoring and crop performance assessment to water resource management and transport infrastructure development.Esa functions as the technical coordinator, defining satellite specifications before contracting industry partners for construction. Operational continuity through 2030 is assured, as follow-on models Sentinel-3b, c, and d have already been commissioned.Beyond OLCI, the satellite carries a radiometer for measuring surface temperatures of both ocean and land, plus an altimeter for ocean height measurements. This instrument combination proves particularly valuable for monitoring phenomena like El Nino, where eastern Pacific waters experience periodic warming bulges. The current El Nino event—among the largest recorded—has disrupted global weather patterns.Europe's national meteorological agencies eagerly await access to Sentinel-3 data for integration into their numerical forecasting models.Dr Craig Donlon, Esa senior scientist, emphasized the satellite's versatility: Yes, Sentinel-3 is an ocean workhorse, but it's also a global workhorse. He highlighted to BBC News the exceptional vegetation products from OLCI's 21 bands, plus extensive capabilities for measuring ice surfaces, rivers, and lakes through its altimeter.Sentinel-3a now joins its orbital companions from two other series. Sentinel-1a, launched in 2014, employs radar to measure Earth's surface shape, while last year's Sentinel-2a uses color cameras to document land surface usage and temporal changes.Additional Sentinels are planned, with the European Commission and Esa already considering sensor suite expansions. Europe seeks space-based carbon-monitoring capabilities to verify countries' implementation of carbon dioxide and greenhouse gas reduction policies.Prof Liebig outlined the timeline: This would be a multi-satellite mission. The idea would be to have a first prototype satellite by 2025, let's say; and then a full system around 2030. But if we want to achieve this we have to start in this (EU) financial perspective.The European-funded Sentinel series What is the Copernicus programme? text: It didn't much look like a protest. On a picturesque Sunday afternoon, Hamburg's outskirts buzzed with animated conversations as middle-class Germans—accompanied by children and dogs—gathered in stunning parkland. Their casual attire and warm smiles masked the serious nature of their assembly: organizing a petition to halt construction of a proposed refugee center on the verdant space.While participants emphasized they harbored no anti-immigrant sentiment, claiming environmental preservation as their primary concern, deeper anxieties emerged through discussion. The housing crisis plaguing Hamburg had reached critical levels even before the current situation, Birgit explained. With tens of thousands of immigrants arriving, the port city now faced unprecedented strain.I don't think Angela Merkel has any idea what she started, Birgit concluded, as desperate authorities converted shipping containers into makeshift homes and commandeered empty commercial buildings and public spaces for migrant facilities.Hanno repeatedly shook his head, expressing profound concern: I just don't think Germany can integrate this number of people. It's a real worry. A real worry.This gathering represented something far more significant than typical far-right demonstrations that dominate headlines. These were Merkel's traditional supporters—the affluent middle class—now consumed by uncertainty and doubt.Most Germans acknowledge their moral obligation to assist those escaping warfare and persecution, yet the overwhelming scale of arrivals has created widespread unease. Experts predict refugee numbers could reach 1.5 million by year's end, surpassing initial estimates of one million.Like a determined team captain, Chancellor Merkel continues her rallying cry: Wir schaffen es! (We can do it!)—her answer to Barack Obama's Yes We Can. However, Germans increasingly question the feasibility of this promise.Recent polling reveals only one-third of citizens support Merkel's migration policies, while her approval ratings decline. Once known for cautious, poll-driven decision-making through incremental steps, she appears transformed by summer images of Mediterranean drownings and desperate crowds at Europe's borders.A month ago, Merkel stunned her nation by unilaterally welcoming all Syrian refugees without establishing intake limits—a seemingly passionate departure from her traditionally measured, stoic approach that Germans have long admired.Florian Juerg, a Hamburg-based branding consultant, suggests Merkel may be revealing her other self. Until recently, she embodied the rational scientist she trained to be, he explained, but now appears to have reconnected with her moral compass as the pastor's daughter of her youth.Hamburg serves as Germany's marketing and brand imaging center, making Juerg's perspective particularly relevant. When asked about potential damage to Brand Merkel, he remained optimistic about long-term prospects, citing her solid decade-long track record as Chancellor and the time required to build lasting brands.Nevertheless, policy failures could permanently tarnish her legacy. Germans have consistently trusted Mutti (Mummy)—Merkel's affectionate nickname—to make crucial decisions across multiple elections. Her refugee crisis management represents the most significant gamble of her political career.While Brand Merkel contributed to Brand Germany's success, she now risks inadvertent damage to her country. The massive asylum seeker influx will reshape Germany's economy, society, and political landscape, already creating documented divisions within her conservative coalition.Lorenz Caffier, CDU Interior Minister of Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, advocates for balanced approaches: The German constitution demands that we look after refugees but the benefits we give them are too generous.Frankly, I'm amazed at any migrant who doesn't choose to come to Germany. Our benefit system acts like a travel agency. We must put the wellbeing of our own people first, Caffier stated.German media extensively covers benefit disparities between refugees and German welfare recipients, fostering resentment in certain communities. Broader concerns focus on potential strain to national healthcare and educational systems.Caffier insists Germany cannot accommodate unlimited numbers, though he defends Merkel's initial response: Angela Merkel didn't open the door to the refugees. They were already at the door. What was she going to do—send tanks to the Austrian border? Actually it's impossible to close borders. Any politician who suggests that is lying.He demands greater European participation, criticizing Brussels for prioritizing the curvature of cucumbers and bananas over pressing continental issues.Meanwhile, other European leaders show little enthusiasm for accepting hundreds of thousands of asylum seekers. Merkel's leadership role in the migration crisis proves as divisive across Europe as domestically.The era of consensus politics under her guidance has definitively ended.

Anticipation filled her thoughts about an upcoming school performance where she hoped to see a boy who had caught her attention. Yet beneath this typical teenage exterior, darker currents flowed. Marsha we miss you. Our world now is incomplete, like a rainbow with a colour missing. We thank you for the joy that you brought us in your short life. Your goodness, sense of fun, spirit and passion for life remain with us, he continued.Music formed McDonnell's passion, now commemorated through a dedicated music room at the local children's hospice. text: A new chair-based gymnastics exercise programme has significant benefits for people with dementia, says a report. The British Gymnastics Foundation's Love to Move scheme has attracted participation from over 150 individuals, with Age UK research confirming demonstrable benefits in the physical, emotional and cognitive aspects of older people.Following successful results, organizers are working to expand training opportunities and broaden program accessibility nationwide.BGF manager Patrick Bonner described the impact: This age and dementia-friendly programme is astonishing people with its life-changing benefits. So many people involved are seeing their lives improving as a result and it is unthinkable that people are regaining functions which were thought to be lost because of participating in the Love to Move classes.The program's effectiveness has proven so remarkable that both South Korea and Japan have implemented complete state funding, establishing it across every care home in both nations.While exercise generally provides numerous health advantages for individuals facing mental and physical challenges, dementia patients particularly benefit from targeted movement programs. The BGF recognized this potential after discovering chair-based exercises producing extraordinary results in Japanese and South Korean care facilities.Determined to introduce these methods to Britain, the BGF studied 2016 research from Japan's original program. The data clearly demonstrated how simple exercises incorporating cognitive stimulation, memory activation, and music could dramatically transform dementia patients' lives.The BGF adapted the Japanese model's fundamental principles to align with British cultural preferences, creating their pilot Love to Move initiative.Consider this challenge: can you simultaneously tap your head while rubbing your stomach? Most people find this requires intense concentration. Regular practice enhances your brain's ability to process information independently across its right and left hemispheres.Love to Move centers on bilaterally asymmetrical movement - executing different actions with each side of the body simultaneously. This approach increases bilateral movement capacity, encouraging the brain to form additional neural connections and boosting cognitive function.Research proves the program enhances dementia patients' ability to handle daily activities including self-feeding, crafting, playing bingo, and maintaining social relationships with loved ones.Most people know someone affected by dementia - whether recently diagnosed or living with the condition for years. Family members and friends desperately seek any sign of health improvement.Understanding this need, the BGF created a public resource featuring key exercises and expert guidance from head coach Kim Hall. Their downloadable booklet provides program insights, historical context, and essential coordination exercises.Throughout two years in Cambridgeshire, Love to Move sessions concentrated on enhancing coordination, posture, movement, and core strength. Care home staff completed feedback forms documenting resident participants' progress during the pilot program.Staff noted remarkable engagement: Two residents involved were keen not to go off with their visitors…they did not want to miss the class, so they got them to join in as well!Pilot feedback revealed significant improvements across multiple areas. Hand rotations, finger-thumb tapping, aerial shape drawing, and nose-ear coordination exercises effectively enhanced motor skills. Balance and core-focused activities helped participants sit independently in chairs.Residents with severe cognitive decline showed notably improved emotional states. Care staff observed visible enjoyment, increased relaxation, and participants remembering sessions while anticipating future classes.Dementia often complicates social interaction, particularly for residents who rarely engage with others. The pilot created opportunities for relationship building, mutual encouragement among participants, and post-session socialization.One participant shared: I feel stronger. I have difficultly moving, but I've started to move more than I have before.Age UK's findings emphasize essential program elements: social, enjoyable environments led by confident, patient staff, plus dedicated refreshment time following sessions.The BGF envisions replicating Japan's nationwide success by offering Love to Move across all British care homes. This ambitious goal requires extensive staff training, comprehensive awareness campaigns, and qualified coach networks to deliver sessions effectively.As with any pilot initiative, the objective involves learning, adapting, and expanding - precisely what the BGF anticipates achieving through continued program development.

Most people find this very difficult, but with practice it is easier for the brain to process information separately in the two hemispheres. The BGF is striving to bring this practice to Britain, and it has studied a project carried out in Japan in 2016. The result was that simple exercises that combined the stimulation of the brain, memory and music could have a surprisingly positive effect on the life of patients with dementia. The BGF took the basic principles of the Japanese model, adapted them to British cultural preferences, and created the Love to Move program. Love to Move is based on the principle of simultaneous activity on both sides of the body. For two years in Cambridgeshire, Love to Move has been focused on improving balance, posture, movement and core strength. Everyone knows someone with dementia, whether recently diagnosed or long since suffering. Friends and relatives are desperate for any sign of improvement. Staff at the nursing home completed the feedback form, documenting the progress of the residents during the trial. This method increases the brain’s ability to move in both directions at once, strengthening neural connections and improving memory. This method has been shown to improve the daily ability of patients with dementia to do daily tasks, such as eating, doing handicrafts, playing games and relating to their loved ones. Two of the group’s members did not want to go with their visitors, and they dragged them to the group as well. There was a marked improvement in some areas. The rotation of the hands, finger-thumb tapping, drawing in the air, nose-ear-coordination, and balance-enhancing exercises all helped to improve the motor skills of the participants. And the BGF sees the possibility of a national success of Japan in all care homes. The Age UK evaluation showed the essential elements of the programme, social, pleasant and patiently conducted sessions with a devoted time for refreshments afterwards. The care staff observed the visible joy, the relaxation, the memory of the session and the expectation of the next. One participant said, ‘I started moving around more than I normally do.’ The ambitious goal requires extensive staff training, a wide public information campaign, and a network of qualified coaches capable of delivering sessions. As with all pilot projects, the aim is to learn, adapt and develop, which is exactly what the BGF hopes to achieve through the continuing development of the programme.

text: The doctor at the centre of the Nike Oregon Project (NOP) drugs investigation altered athletes' medical records before handing them to anti-doping authorities, according to new disclosures. Since 2015, when BBC's Panorama programme and ProPublica first exposed alleged doping and unethical practices at the Nike Oregon Project (NOP), both Dr Jeffrey Brown and the camp's controversial coach Alberto Salazar have remained under scrutiny by the US Anti-Doping Agency (Usada). The elite endurance training facility, which Nike funds and Salazar directs, has coached Britain's double Olympic champion Mo Farah since 2011.Both men continue to vehemently deny any wrongdoing.This February, the Russian hacking collective Fancy Bears leaked an interim Usada investigative report examining NOP allegations. The Sunday Times, BBC, and New York Times subsequently published details from the document, which outlined various purported anti-doping rule violations. Usada has not yet filed formal charges against anyone connected to its ongoing investigation.Fresh revelations obtained by the BBC and ProPublica now cast additional suspicion on Dr Brown, a Texas-based endocrinologist who has treated numerous Salazar athletes. Previously accused of prescribing thyroid medication to enhance performance—though such medication isn't prohibited under World Anti-Doping Agency regulations—Dr Brown has consistently denied these claims.As Salazar's personal physician, Dr Brown provided Usada with medical records of specific athletes, including Steve Magness, who previously served as Salazar's assistant coach. However, Magness—a key source in the 2015 BBC/ProPublica investigation—alleges that Dr Brown has tampered with his medical documentation.Magness requested copies of his medical notes in August 2015, before signing a release allowing Usada to obtain them from his former doctor. One particular note documents an infusion of L-carnitine, a controversial yet legal supplement, administered by Dr Brown at his Texas office under Salazar's direction in 2011.According to Magness, the left-side note represents his original copy documenting the infusion—a medical procedure requiring him to remain on a drip for over four hours. The corresponding note later submitted by Dr Brown's office to Usada, shown on the right and featured in the Usada report, appears to contain several additions.Multiple checkmarks seemingly were added under 'EXAM' categories, including 'General,' 'Lungs,' 'Thyroid,' 'CV' (cardiovascular), and 'Neuro,' implying Dr Brown conducted a comprehensive health assessment of Magness. Magness, who departed NOP in 2012 and currently coaches at the University of Houston, maintains these examinations never occurred.I do not recall these being done. I wasn't even in a patient room, but instead in his office during this visit. I do not recall him going through his normal checks of my thyroid or [anything else], Magness states.My only speculation is that [those boxes were ticked] to make it look like care for the patient had been given. He might have realised after the fact that when you have a patient, your doctoral duty is to the health of that individual.And that without the proper checks, it might look like he was prioritising a company, Nike, Salazar, that was paying him over the health of his patient.Dr Brown had been my physician since the age of 16.The Usada report alleges Dr Brown violated anti-doping regulations at least four times. Dr Brown categorically denies breaking any anti-doping rules. The Texas Medical Board is simultaneously investigating Dr Brown but declined commentary.L-carnitine, the supplement in question, remains legal and occurs naturally in the human body, helping convert fat into energy. Salazar had become enthusiastic about research suggesting L-carnitine's benefits and was eager to test it on his athletes.Following the trial with Magness, Salazar contacted Lance Armstrong, who was then preparing for a long-distance triathlon. He informed the now-disgraced former cyclist: Lance, call me asap! We have tested it and it's amazing. You are the only athlete I'm going to tell the actual numbers to other than Galen Rupp. It's too incredible.Magness describes himself as having been a reluctant test subject.Wada regulations require that any infusions remain under 50ml every six hours—yet according to the Usada report, infusions of such minimal L-carnitine amounts would provide negligible performance benefits to athletes. After analyzing available data from the medical notes, Usada experts determined the infusion levels must have significantly exceeded 50ml, thereby constituting a doping rule breach.Usada suspects similar procedures were applied to as many as six other US NOP athletes under Salazar's guidance, including Dathan Ritzenhein. The agency also believes medical records concerning Ritzenhein, provided by Dr Brown, were secretly modified to suggest the infusion stayed within Wada's 50ml threshold. In this instance, a 40ml annotation appears to have been inserted prior to Usada submission.The Usada report determines that both Salazar and Dr Brown knew infusions administered to NOP athletes, including Magness and Ritzenhein, exceeded legal limits and violated Wada regulations.The report states: Usada has found that these potential anti-doping rule violations appear to have wholly or largely occurred in the context of a larger conspiracy between Nike Oregon Project coach Alberto Salazar and Houston endocrinologist Dr Jeffrey Brown to collude in order to employ risky and untested alternative and unconventional [and sometimes potentially unlawful] uses of medical procedures and prescription medications [including both substances and methods prohibited under the rules of sport…] to attempt to increase the testosterone, energy and blood levels of Nike Oregon Project athletes in order to boost athletic performance.Usada acknowledges Magness, who recognized rule violations had occurred, for withdrawing from future competitions because he believed he had gained an unfair advantage. Despite Magness's substantial contributions to the Usada investigation as a whistleblower, he may still face suspension for his involvement in the L-carnitine experiment.Dr Brown's attorney informed the BBC and ProPublica that allegations against him were unfounded. In correspondence, lawyer Joan Bain characterized the Usada report leak as illegal and dismissed it as fake news. Ms Bain cited patient confidentiality as preventing Dr Brown from addressing specific inquiries.Ms Bain severely criticized Usada and its investigation, declaring: Notwithstanding its name, you should understand that Usada is not an official government entity, but rather a private corporation which stands to gain financially through publicity, essentially using the press to spread its own 'fake news'.She described this as the latest attempt by Usada to bait Dr Brown into breaking the law by 'leaking' false information to journalists in the hope that Dr Brown will cross the line while trying to defend himself.Regarding allegations of altered notes, she stated: No-one at Dr Brown's office has inappropriately changed medical records. All medical records provided to Usada were accurate and provided with the patient's consent.She continued: Dr Brown did not break any Wada rules and is unaware of any violation of Wada rules by Alberto Salazar… Dr Brown did not infuse any active athlete with more than 50ml of an L-carnitine solution. L-carnitine is an FDA approved amino acid supplement. It is not a banned substance.After Ms Bain's response, Magness wrote to both her and Dr Brown waiving confidentiality regarding the specific notes the BBC and ProPublica were investigating, but Ms Bain offered no additional comment.Alberto Salazar has consistently and forcefully denied violating Wada rules or endangering his athletes' health, responding to the BBC and ProPublica's investigation with an extensive, detailed rebuttal.In 2014, Mo Farah received an L-carnitine injection before a significant race, which UK Athletics (UKA) doctor Robin Chakraverty improperly documented. During April testimony before the Culture, Media and Sport Select Committee, Dr Chakraverty stated the injection measured 13.5mls, well below the 50ml legal threshold, though UKA chairman Ed Warner deemed his recording failure inexcusable.According to the leaked report, Usada continues investigating Farah's use of the substance to establish whether rules were violated. Farah maintains he has never broken any regulations and has pledged to support Salazar unless proven guilty of anti-doping rule violations.

text: In our series of letters from African journalists, Nigerian writer and novelist Adaobi Tricia Nwaubani looks at the clamour for assistance that accompanies a politician's rise to office. Nigeria's political party primaries have concluded, offering voters a clearer vision of who might claim their portion of the national wealth following February 2015's elections.However, successful candidates won't be alone in sharing the country's bounty.When electoral triumph occurs in Nigeria, word spreads with lightning speed—crossing rivers, scaling mountains, traversing fields and forests—reaching kinfolk scattered across the globe. The unemployed anticipate their jobless days ending; the uneducated envision education no longer blocking their corporate ascent; distant expatriates begin plotting homeward journeys.These relatives and friends soon embark on pilgrimages toward the victorious candidate.Phone calls flood in; text messages arrive; gates receive persistent knocking.Campaign assistance gets offered in every conceivable form; victory prayer sessions commence, typically conducted late at night in living rooms.Last week, a Lagos-based friend informed me of his Benin City travel plans. His acquaintance had just picked up a House of Assembly position there. Another contact was positioned for a different prominent role.He's a good friend of my elder brother in Florida, he said. I've already told my brother: 'You'd better come down and rub minds with him and introduce us to him.'Another friend, whose husband maintains close ties with a winning candidate from one of Nigeria's most coveted states, described her constantly ringing phone following his announced victory.Congratulatory calls poured in continuously. Indeed, I had phoned for precisely that purpose.Nigerian culture has long dictated that anyone ascending to power—suddenly wielding the knife to carve the national cake—must invite their clan to both slice and consume alongside them.The most heinous political sin involves forgetting his people after assuming office.He must remember sisters, brothers, cousins, nieces, nephews, in-laws, friends, schoolmates, and others.Preferably through contracts, appointments and jobs.Such failures result in taunts and ostracism; when tenure expires, complete isolation follows.Even beyond funeral rites, bitter tongues continue wagging.Local chronicles will eternally record him as denying his kindred their rightful turn.Numerous entertaining stories circulate regarding the Niger Delta population influx into Abuja, Nigeria's capital, after their kinsman, Goodluck Jonathan, secured the presidency in 2011.My favorite tale comes from a British-Nigerian friend teaching at an Abuja institution where students pay astronomical dollar fees while mocking teachers' inexpensive mobile devices.During a science lesson, she was astounded when one pupil demonstrated extraordinary crustacean knowledge—unexpected for an urban child his age.This student addressed the class, detailing in remarkable depth how these creatures are captured, cleaned and prepared.Afterward, my friend privately questioned the boy about his extensive topic knowledge.The child explained his creek upbringing, where his family sustained themselves through small-scale crustacean trading.This explains why news of a candidate's potential political ascension generates such euphoria.Across much of the world, radically transforming economic circumstances requires years of steady advancement.In Nigeria, elections and political appointments suffice. Suddenly, children transition from creek crustacean-catching to exclusive Abuja schooling.Voracious relatives and friends constitute the primary force driving Nigeria's corruption crisis.Consider the thousands queuing with extended palms behind each office holder.Attempt explaining your system reform intentions now that their turn to feast has finally arrived.If you would like to comment on Adaobi Tricia Nwaubani's column, please do so below.

text: Nigeria's Ogoniland region could take 30 years to recover fully from the damage caused by years of oil spills, a long-awaited UN report says. A comprehensive United Nations study reveals that complete environmental restoration of Nigeria's Ogoniland region would require what could become the world's most wide-ranging and long-term oil clean-up operation.The assessment found communities confronting severe health hazards, including families consuming water containing dangerously high carcinogen levels. Oil giant Shell has acknowledged responsibility for two specific spills while stating that all oil incidents harm both Nigeria and the company.We will continue working with our partners in Nigeria, including the government, to solve these problems and on the next steps to help clean up Ogoniland, declared Mutiu Sunmonu, managing director of the Shell Petroleum Development Company of Nigeria (SPDC).The Bodo fishing community announced plans to pursue compensation worth hundreds of millions of dollars.Nigeria ranks among the world's leading oil producers. The UN evaluation of Ogoniland, situated within the Niger Delta, concluded that five decades of oil operations had penetrated further and deeper than many had supposed.**By Peter Okwoche, BBC News**In 2007, during my visit to an Ogoniland village, I observed a small stream that served as the community's primary water source. Oil spillage effects were unmistakable - a thin oil film covered the water's surface, which villagers pushed aside with their hands before collecting water.Local residents reported no fish sightings in the stream for over five years. They described fatalities from exploding oil pipes and health complications from inhaling fumes from burning oil well heads.My 2011 return visit revealed worsened oil contamination. Villagers had abandoned the stream entirely, walking up to four hours for clean water access.Nigerian governments have consistently failed Ogoniland's population over two decades. This report likely won't catalyze change. Meanwhile, secessionist voices in Ogoniland will intensify.The UN Environmental Programme (Unep) stated: In at least 10 Ogoni communities where drinking water is contaminated with high levels of hydrocarbons, public health is seriously threatened.Unep discovered that seemingly unaffected areas actually suffered severe contamination underground. In one community, the report documented families drinking from wells contaminated with benzene - a known carcinogen - at levels 900 times above recommendations.Scientists at the site, located near a Nigerian National Petroleum Company pipeline, discovered oil slicks eight centimeters thick floating on water surfaces. This contamination reportedly stemmed from an oil spill occurring over six years earlier.The comprehensive report, examining approximately 200 locations across 14 months, determined that Shell had generated public health and safety concerns by failing to implement its own oilfield infrastructure control and maintenance procedures. However, it also identified local pipeline sabotage for oil theft.Regional restoration could require $1bn (£613m) and span 25-30 years for completion, according to the findings.The environmental restoration of Ogoniland could prove to be the world's most wide-ranging and long term oil clean-up exercise ever undertaken if contaminated drinking water, land, creeks and important ecosystems such as mangroves are to be brought back to full, productive health, Unep stated.This report, considered the most comprehensive study of any Niger Delta region, received partial Shell funding following Nigerian government requests.Amnesty International, a longtime campaign advocate, claimed the report demonstrated Shell's pollution responsibility.This report proves Shell has had a terrible impact in Nigeria, but has got away with denying it for decades, falsely claiming they work to best international standards, said Audrey Gaughran, Amnesty's global issues director.Earlier, Unep spokesman Nick Nuttal informed BBC's Network Africa that the study wasn't designed to blame any particular stakeholder operating in Ogoniland. He emphasized that Shell's liability admission for two spills remained separate from the Unep report.Wednesday saw Shell accept responsibility for 2008 and 2009 spills, agreeing to settle under Nigerian law. The Bodo fishing community had alleged these leaks destroyed their environment and livelihoods.Responding to Thursday's report, Mr Sunmonu described it as making a contribution towards improving understanding of the issue of oil spills in Ogoniland.All oil spills are bad - bad for local communities, bad for the environment, bad for Nigeria and bad for SPDC, he stated.We clean up all spills from our facilities, whatever the cause, and restore the land to its original state, he added.The SPDC managing director also called upon authorities to combat illegal refining and pipeline sabotage.Ogoni communities have persistently complained about environmental damage but report being largely ignored. Writer Ken Saro-Wiwa highlighted these issues before his 1995 execution by Nigeria's military government, triggering international condemnation.The resulting campaign compelled Shell to cease oil extraction from Ogoniland, though the company continues operating regional pipelines where spills persist.

text: Learning a foreign language should be made compulsory in primary schools here, a new report has said. A comprehensive review conducted by Stranmillis University College researchers has revealed significant disparities in foreign language education across Northern Ireland's primary schools, highlighting what experts describe as inequitable provision for children throughout the region.Unlike England and Scotland, where primary school pupils are required to learn a foreign language as part of their statutory curriculum, Northern Ireland maintains no such mandatory requirement for second language instruction at the elementary level.The study, commissioned by the Northern Ireland Languages Council—a Department of Education-established body representing over 20 organizations from business, education, and community sectors—examined language learning practices across more than 100 schools.Spanish and French emerged as the most favored languages in institutions that offered foreign language instruction, while some pupils also had opportunities to study German or Mandarin. However, researchers discovered that not every primary school provided additional language education, creating what they termed a lack of equity in provision for children nationwide.Beyond availability issues, the investigation uncovered substantial inconsistencies regarding instruction frequency and the age at which students begin language learning. Primary school principals voiced concerns about insufficient support and resources for both educators and students attempting to deliver quality language programs.Despite these challenges, the overwhelming majority of participating principals and teachers acknowledged the importance and value of additional language learning. Paradoxically, they indicated that foreign language instruction remained a low priority since such programs face no assessment or measurement requirements.The report's authors emphasized that developing language skills proves vital for economic prosperity, social cohesion and the acceptance of diverse cultural identities. They expressed hope that their findings would encourage policy makers, business and educational providers to support the revision and improvement of current curriculum provision in additional language learning.Furthermore, the research highlighted language learning as conducive to economic growth and that can enhance the lives and future employability of children and young people.This situation contrasts sharply with broader European Union trends, where more than 80% of primary pupils receive additional language instruction, underscoring Northern Ireland's position as an outlier in multilingual education provision.

text: Lewis Hamilton collided with Mercedes team-mate Nico Rosberg on the last lap before passing him to win a thrilling Austrian Grand Prix. Hamilton's deficit to Rosberg in the championship battle has narrowed to just 11 points following a dramatic collision that reshaped the Austrian Grand Prix outcome.The pivotal moment arrived when Hamilton attempted an outside overtake at Turn Two, with his German teammate turning in late and causing contact that damaged Rosberg's front wing. Stewards handed Rosberg a 10-second penalty plus two licence penalty points for triggering the collision, dropping him to fourth place.Mercedes faces internal controversy over the race-deciding incident. Hamilton, the world champion, had positioned himself on the outside and drew level heading into Turn Two, but Rosberg held his line wide, delaying his turn-in before the collision occurred. Though Hamilton was forced off track, the impact had already compromised Rosberg's front wing, which generated sparks as it scraped the asphalt while Hamilton swept past. Rosberg subsequently lost additional positions to Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen.Facing boos from the predominantly German-Austrian spectators, Hamilton explained from the podium: He made a mistake into Turn One and I had an opportunity to go around the outside in Turn Two. I left a lot of room on the inside and I guess he locked up and crashed into me.Rosberg, who also received a reprimand for continuing with a damaged vehicle, offered a contrasting perspective. Absolutely gutted, he stated. We were battling and I was struggling a little with my brakes. I went a bit deep but that is fine because I am on the inside so I can dictate. So I was surprised Lewis turned in and caused a collision. It's unbelievable.BBC F1 analyst Allan McNish placed responsibility squarely on Rosberg's shoulders for the incident.Mercedes revealed that Rosberg had experienced a brake-by-wire failure affecting the rear axle during the penultimate lap's closing stages. Nevertheless, team principal Toto Wolff initially characterized the collision as brainless, though he refrained from assigning specific blame.For Hamilton, the victory provides relief after pit errors and questionable strategy threatened to derail his chances. The world champion will undoubtedly seek explanations for how he found himself trailing Rosberg despite starting from pole position and commanding the opening 21 laps while his teammate climbed from sixth place.Saturday's qualifying had seen Hamilton secure a brilliant pole in wet conditions, outpacing Rosberg by over half a second. With his teammate relegated to sixth due to a gearbox penalty, Hamilton appeared set for victory.The early race unfolded favorably for Hamilton as he maintained a comfortable lead while Rosberg battled past Force India's Nico Hulkenberg and McLaren's Jenson Button, reaching third behind Hamilton and Ferrari's Kimi Raikkonen by lap 10.Strategy complications emerged when Hamilton's engineer opted for an early pit stop, fitting the more durable soft compounds while Hamilton continued on fragile ultra-softs at the front. Though Hamilton easily maintained his gap over Raikkonen, this tactical decision allowed Rosberg to close within 21 seconds and claim fourth position behind Raikkonen and teammate Sebastian Vettel when Hamilton finally pitted on lap 21.The gap should have preserved Hamilton's lead, but a left rear wheel problem during his pit stop created delays, allowing him to rejoin behind Rosberg.Following a mid-race safety car period, Mercedes initially planned contrasting strategies - potentially two stops for Rosberg versus one for Hamilton. However, the team ultimately abandoned Hamilton's one-stop approach, bringing both drivers in within a lap of each other on lap 54.Hamilton received used soft tyres while Rosberg was equipped with fresh super-softs - a compound unavailable to the world champion. Despite Hamilton's questioning of the tyre choice, race engineer Bonnington's confidence in the selection proved justified, setting up the dramatic finale.The safety car intervention resulted from Vettel's explosive right rear tyre failure on the pit straight during lap 27 - occurring within the tyre's predicted lifespan established at race start. Vettel, who had been leading ahead of Rosberg, faces another missed opportunity in Ferrari's frustrating season.Out of nowhere the tyre decided to blow up, commented Vettel, marking the first in-race tyre failure since his 200mph blow-out at last year's Belgian Grand Prix.Red Bull's Daniel Ricciardo claimed the final podium spot behind Rosberg, while McLaren's Jenson Button delivered an impressive performance. Button converted his remarkable third-place grid position into valuable points despite spending most of the race embroiled in intense midfield battles, ultimately emerging at the head of the pack.Austrian Grand Prix race results Austrian Grand Prix coverage details

text: Thirteen schoolgirls have been on a hunger strike for six days to protest against daily sexual harassment in the northern Indian state of Haryana. A group of 13 teenage girls in Haryana's Rewari district have launched a hunger strike, demanding protection from sexual harassment during their daily commute to school and the establishment of a higher-secondary institution in their village.The students, ranging from 16 to 18 years old, have been consuming only water while refusing food. They insist they will continue their protest until receiving written guarantees from authorities. Parents and non-striking students have rallied behind the demonstrators, abandoning their agricultural work and daily employment to join the cause.Sexual harassment has become a daily ordeal for these girls as they travel to a neighboring village for their education. Almost every day, we face eve teasing [a local term for sexual harassment], explained Sheetal, one of the 13 protesters, speaking to BBC Hindi's Nitin Srivastava. Should we stop studying? Should we stop dreaming? Are only rich people and their children allowed to dream? The government should protect us or open a higher-secondary school in our village.The harassment extends beyond verbal abuse, according to another student, Sujata, who described how men often try to touch us inappropriately. She added: They write our phone numbers on walls, make nasty comments. Actually much worse happens, but not everything can be described.Local officials in Rewari district have failed to adequately protect the teenagers, according to their accounts. However, authorities have now responded with promises of enhanced security measures. Additionally, the government has pledged to upgrade their village's existing school to higher-secondary level, eliminating the need for the dangerous commute.Despite these assurances, the striking students remain skeptical and demand written confirmation before ending their protest.This unprecedented demonstration marks what appears to be the first time young girls in the region have organized such a protest. The community has rallied around them, with even men acknowledging the need for gender equality.One mother of a protesting student expressed her anguish: These young girls face the kind of harassment that I can't even describe. When we complain to the police, they put pressure on us to take such cases back, she said, describing the situation as painful to see these girls suffer.Rohtash Kumar, whose daughter participates in the strike, emphasized that harassment has plagued the area for years. It's the first time that girls have taken the matter in their own hands. The men in our village support their struggle, he stated.Kumar stressed the importance of concrete action rather than empty promises. Such promises have not been fulfilled in the past. We want to be sure that our struggle doesn't go waste because of a false promise, Mr Kumar added.The week-long ordeal has been particularly challenging for the girls and their families, who have set aside their livelihoods to support the cause.Haryana consistently ranks among India's most backward states regarding gender ratios, with crimes against women occurring frequently. However, this grassroots movement represents a significant shift, as young women take charge of demanding their fundamental rights to education and safety.The protest highlights broader issues of sexual harassment that plague Indian society, particularly affecting young women seeking education in rural areas where infrastructure and security remain inadequate.

text: In our series of letters from African journalists, veteran Ghanaian journalist Elizabeth Ohene reflects on why in Ghana a person's age is not etched in stone. Numbers hold little reverence among Ghanaians. Age figures, in particular, receive remarkably casual treatment.Rarely does someone's birth date or age merit mention in personal narratives. The concept remains largely insignificant in storytelling about individuals.While most global populations maintain unchangeable birth dates from cradle to grave, Ghana operates differently. Newspaper notices regularly announce birth date modifications—a phenomenon typically coinciding with approaching retirement deadlines.Workers routinely visit commissioners of oaths, swearing affidavits to transform their documented 59-year status into a more favorable 55-year profile. This strategic adjustment extends salary collection by several additional years, given that constitutional mandates set public officer retirement at 60.The most extraordinary Notice of Change of Date of Birth witnessed involved an official reducing their documented age by seven years. Some individuals have sworn affidavits creating birth dates that would theoretically place them in Primary Class One before their actual birth occurred.Recent news coverage highlighted this phenomenon's remarkable scope: approximately 800 teachers petitioned the Ghana Education Service for age modifications. While some sought younger documentation, others requested older dates than their current records indicated.Public outrage greeted this revelation, suggesting Ghana might finally embrace global standards regarding birth date sanctity. Young people expressed incredulous reactions: How can people want their dates of birth to be changed?However, a teaching union leader mounted a spirited defense. According to his explanation, teachers sought corrections only because payroll departments had initially recorded incorrect employment dates.This situation persists because birth recording remains uncommon. Historically, illiterate parents neglected registering children's births, allowing dates to vanish into memory's fog.School enrollment supposedly requires birth certificates, yet many children somehow gain admission without proper documentation.Elizabeth Ohene:Ghana's complete disregard for birth date sanctity manifests in ways that undermine official record integrity.Later life birth certificate requirements involve appearing before commissioners of oaths, offering dates based on parental or family guessestimates.When approaching mandatory 60-year retirement and desperately seeking work extension due to inadequate pensions, individuals return to commissioners, swearing they've discovered compelling evidence proving original certificate errors.For instance, someone might claim birth during a village chief's enstoolment, later discovering the ceremony occurred in 1968 rather than 1965. Since official enstoolment records likely don't exist anyway, why dispute three-year differences?This birth date disregard creates additional problems throughout Ghana's official systems.School children appearing no older than 14 possess voters registration cards, despite 18-year minimum voting age requirements.Life consequences follow unless individuals continue visiting commissioners of oaths for new birth dates.Police recruitment advertisements specify 25-year age limits. Someone actually 21 but holding a voters' card claiming 26 years (obtained by posing as 18 at age 14) faces complications.Football players sometimes attempt age reduction to participate in age-restricted competitions. Modern technology increasingly ensures competition integrity, making it difficult for 20-somethings to compete in under-17 tournaments.Numerous attempts to enforce birth and death registration have failed spectacularly.Existing civil service regulations prohibit public officials from changing birth dates during government employment. Workers remain bound to whatever dates they entered service with—no affidavit-based aging or youth restoration permitted.Enforcement proves challenging because many Ghanaians consider ages confidential information requiring no advertisement.Asking someone's age might prompt: Is it my official or real age that you want?The new government firmly promises implementing a national identification system within its first year. All Ghanaians would receive identification cards containing unchangeable biometric data, eliminating affidavit-based birth date acquisition.Everyone awaits this development with bated breath.While anticipating this dramatic transformation, I've pondered potential advantages in the current system where personal age remains changeable and confidential.An online British newspaper article from earlier this year sparked these thoughts.Tennis followers would recognize this Australian Open report excerpt:A few hours after Serena Williams, 35, joined her 36-year-old sister, Venus, in the women's final by trouncing the 34-year-old Mirjana Lucic-Baroni, Federer, 35, somehow conjured some more retro magic to beat Stan Wawrinka, a mere 31, for the 19th time in 22 matches, The Guardian reported.Confronting such prose possibilities in Ghanaian newspapers, many citizens will likely prefer maintaining birth dates as changeable, private events.More from Elizabeth Ohene:Follow us on Twitter @BBCAfrica, on Facebook at BBC Africa, on Instagram at bbcafrica or email africalive@bbc.co.uk
dipper: In our series of letters from African journalists, veteran Ghanaian journalist Elizabeth Ohene reflects on why in Ghana a person's age is not etched in stone. Numbers are not considered sacred by the Ghanians; the age of a person, for example, is treated with remarkably little reverence. The concept is largely insignificant in the story of individuals. In the West, where people are often baptized with the same day of birth, from cradle to tomb, Ghana does not. Those who are approaching the retirement age are, according to the notices published in the newspapers, very often changing their dates of birth; in the case of the teachers, the last notice was that approximately 800 of them were petitioning the Ghana Education Service for the same. The most extraordinary change of date of birth has been that of an official who, with the assistance of a commissioner of oaths, has reduced his age by seven years. This strategic change in age has, as a result, extended the time of receipt of salary by several years, as constitutionally set retirement at sixty for public officials. The revelation of the case caused public outrage, implying that the sanctity of the date of birth was being adopted in Ghana, and young people reacted incredulously: How can they want their birthdays to change? Nevertheless, a teacher's union leader made a vigorous defense: According to his explanation, teachers sought only corrections because the payroll departments had initially recorded the wrong dates of their employment, and the situation remains unchanged because of the rarity of birth registration. Some teachers wanted to be registered younger, others wanted older. As Elizabeth Ohene writes in her book, “Ghana’s total disregard for birth date sanctity manifests itself in ways that undermine official record integrity. Later in life, birth certificates are obtained by going before commissioners of oaths and presenting dates based on the memory or guesswork of the parents or relatives. When approaching the compulsory retirement age of 60 and desperate to work longer, to evade the inadequate pensions, individuals return to the commissioners and swear that they have discovered compelling evidence that demonstrates the original certificate is wrong. One of the pitfalls is that someone who has a voters’ card for 18 but is really 21 (and obtained it by presenting oneself as 18 at age 14) may have complications. Then there are the problems with respect to the minimum age for voting; the schoolchildren, who are supposedly admitted without any certificate of their age, are already carrying voters’ cards that make them look 18 years old, though the minimum age for registration is 18. The new government is set to bring in a national identification system within the first year of its taking over. This would entail the issuing of identification cards with biometric data that could not be changed, thus eliminating the need for affidavits to establish the dates of birth of all Ghanaians. Everyone is waiting for this development with bated breath, but while we await this dramatic transformation, I have been wondering if there might not be advantages to the current system where personal age remains changeable and confidential. An online British newspaper article from earlier this year brought these thoughts to mind. “A few hours after Serena Williams, 35, had joined her 36-year-old sister Venus in the women's final by beating the 34-year-old Mirjana Lucic-Baroni, The Guardian reported, Roger Federer, 35, managed to beat Stan Wawrinka, a mere 31,” The Guardian reported. Confronted with this slew of snide prose on their own doorstep, most Ghanaians are likely to prefer the present system, whereby personal age remains changeable and confidential.

text: A chronology of key events: Between approximately 250-900 AD, Classical Maya city states reached their zenith across what is now southern Mexico, Guatemala, and Belize, before experiencing an enigmatic decline.From around 0-500 AD, the major cultural and religious hub of Teotihuacan flourished as potentially one of the world's largest cities, though its ethnic composition and political structure remain largely mysterious.The 6th-7th centuries witnessed waves of new populations migrating into central Mexico from northern regions, including Nahuatl speakers. The Toltec culture peaked between 800-1000 AD, centered around Tula in present-day Hidalgo province.A revitalized Maya civilization emerged in the northern Yucatan peninsula from the 10th-16th centuries, establishing magnificent cities like Chichen Itza and Uxmal. The Aztec Empire, representing the culmination of indigenous civilizations, dominated central Mexico from 1428-1521 through an alliance of Nahuatl-speaking city states led by Tenochtitlan, now Mexico City.**Spanish Conquest and Colonial Period**In 1519, Hernan Cortes landed at Veracruz with a small Spanish force, initiating Mexico's conquest. By 1521, allied with indigenous anti-Aztec forces, Cortes captured Tenochtitlan. Mexico subsequently became part of the Viceroyalty of New Spain from 1521-1820.**Independence and Early Nationhood**The War of Independence (1810-21) culminated in the brief Mexican Empire, spanning from Central America to modern-day Costa Rica's southern border and including the southwestern United States. Following Emperor Augustin de Iturbide's ouster and exile in 1824, Mexico became a federal republic. Central American provinces immediately seceded, forming Guatemala, Honduras, El Salvador, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica.The nascent Mexican state faced persistent tensions between conservative Spanish-origin landowners and the predominantly indigenous landless population, creating chronic instability and armed conflicts.Texas seceded in 1836 after warfare, joining the United States nine years later. The Mexican-American War (1846-8) forced Mexico to sell its northern territories—including present-day California, Nevada, New Mexico, Arizona, and Utah—to the US.**Reform and Foreign Intervention**La Reforma period (1855-72) featured liberal reforms curtailing Catholic Church power and landholdings. From 1864-7, Archduke Maximilian Habsburg of Austria served as Mexican emperor with French and conservative support under Napoleon III, before Republican rebels toppled and executed him.Porfirio Diaz's 35-year dictatorship (1876-1911), the Porfiriato, delivered stability, modernization, and economic growth while imposing political repression and stagnation.**Revolution and Modern Mexico**The Mexican Revolution (1910-1920) terminated the Diaz dictatorship, establishing a constitutional republic. Liberal Francisco Madero, Diaz's successor, implemented land reform and labor legislation before his assassination in 1913-14. Victoriano Huerta seized power as political unrest continued, with Zapata leading southern peasant revolts.Huerta resigned in 1914 due to US suspicions about his alleged pro-German sympathies, succeeded by Venustiano Carranza. US forces crossed the border in 1916 pursuing guerrilla leader Francisco Pancho Villa, withdrawing unsuccessfully in 1917. A new constitution was adopted that year to ensure permanent democracy.President Carranza's murder in 1920 triggered civil war. The National Revolutionary Party formed in 1929, later renamed the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) in 1946.**Mid-20th Century Developments**President Lazaro Cardenas launched oil nationalization, land reform, and industrial expansion programs in 1934. Leon Trotsky was murdered in Mexico in 1940. Mexico declared war on Japan and Germany in 1942.The 1960s saw suppressed unrest over wealth inequality. The 1968 Tlatelolco student demonstration during the Olympic Games resulted in Mexican security forces firing on protesters, killing or wounding hundreds and shocking the nation.Huge offshore oil reserves were discovered in 1976, with the Cantarell field becoming Mexico's production cornerstone. A devastating 1985 Mexico City earthquake killed thousands and left many homeless.**Contemporary Era**Mexico ratified NAFTA with the US and Canada in 1993. The 1994 Zapatista National Liberation Army guerrilla rebellion in Chiapas was brutally suppressed. Rebels opposed NAFTA and demanded greater indigenous rights recognition, leading to government acknowledgment of the EZLN.Presidential elections in August 1994 were won by PRI candidate Ernesto Zedillo Ponce de Leon after previous candidate Luis Donaldo Colosio's murder. The stock market plunged in December, with the peso losing one-third of its value.Former President Carlos Salinas went into exile in 1995 after his brother Raul Salinas was connected to Colosio's murder. November 1995 saw government-EZLN agreement on greater Mayan autonomy in Chiapas.Southern insurgency escalated in 1996 as the leftist Popular Revolutionary Army attacked government troops. The PRI suffered heavy 1997 electoral losses, losing its lower house majority for the first time since 1929.December 1997 witnessed 45 Indians killed by paramilitary gunmen in a Chiapas village, causing international outcry and prompting President Zedillo's investigation. Chiapas governor resigned in January 1998, peace talks reactivated but collapsed year-end.**Democratic Transition**Vicente Fox of the opposition Alliance for Change won July 2000 presidential elections—the first opposition victory ever. Parliamentary elections saw the Alliance emerge as the strongest party, narrowly defeating the PRI. Fox was sworn in as president in December 2000.March 2001 featured Zapatista guerrillas, led by Subcomandante Marcos, staging their Zapatour march from Chiapas to Mexico City highlighting their demands. Parliament passed an indigenous rights bill in April 2001, which Marcos rejected days later, saying it worsened the Indian population's situation and vowing continued Chiapas uprising.President Fox appointed a prosecutor in November 2001 to investigate left-wing activist disappearances during the 1970s-1980s. Roberto Madrazo won the PRI leadership contest in March 2002.**Truth and Reconciliation Efforts**Millions of secret security files were released in June 2002, illuminating torture and killing of hundreds of political activists by security forces in the 1960s-1970s. President Fox declared his government unafraid to pursue prosecutions.Former President Luis Echeverria was questioned in July 2002 about 1968 student protester massacres when he served as interior minister, and 1971 massacres during his presidency. Three army officers were charged with first-degree murder in September 2002 over 134 leftist killings in the 1970s.An investigator deemed the 1971 student protester shooting by government forces genocide in July 2004, though a judge refused to order former President Echeverria's arrest on charges he ordered the attack.**Drug War Escalation**Six prison officers were murdered in January 2005, placing top-security jails on high alert amid escalating drug gang tensions. Political controversy erupted in April 2005 when Mexico City mayor and presidential favorite Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador was stripped of prosecution immunity by Congress in a land dispute, though the government eventually abandoned prosecution.A federal special prosecutor post was created in February 2006 to tackle violent crimes against women, following UN and rights groups' criticism over 300+ unsolved female murders across 12 years in border city Ciudad Juarez.Conservative candidate Felipe Calderon was declared winner of July 2006 presidential elections with a razor-thin majority over leftist rival Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador, who challenged results with mass street protests. The Federal Electoral Tribunal confirmed Calderon's victory in September.US President George W Bush signed legislation in October 2006 to build 1,125km of fencing along the US-Mexico border. Mexico condemned the barrier plans, intended to curb illegal immigration.A new federal police force was created in December 2006 to tackle drug cartels, with thousands of troops deployed in Michoacan state as part of major anti-trafficking operations.**Intensifying Violence**New domestic violence legislation took effect in February 2007, requiring tougher authority action. July 2007 saw Mexican telecoms tycoon Carlos Slim reportedly overtake Microsoft founder Bill Gates as the world's richest person, while genocide trials against former president Luis Echeverria were suspended.Heavy rains flooded nearly all of Tabasco state in October 2007, leaving 500,000 homeless in one of the country's worst natural disasters.Drug-related killings soared in 2008, with organized crime murders leaping to almost 1,400 in the first five months. Attorney-general Eduardo Medina Mora reported in May 2008 that over 4,000 people had died in 18 months since President Calderon declared war on drug cartels, including 450 police, soldiers, or prosecutors, with many killings concentrated along the US border.Hundreds of thousands joined August 2008 marches throughout Mexico protesting continuing drug-related violence. Faced with declining oil production, the government passed energy reforms in October 2008, including controversial plans allowing private investment in state oil giant Pemex.**Economic Crisis and Continued Violence**The government unveiled nearly $150m in emergency economic measures in January 2009 to protect against US economic downturn effects. Reports indicated about 1,000 people died in drug-related violence during the first six weeks of 2009.Army troops entered Ciudad Juarez in March 2009 as open warfare erupted between rival drug gangs. Authorities closed schools and public buildings in April 2009 after dozens were confirmed killed by the virulent new swine flu virus.The opposition PRI made large gains in July 2009 mid-term congressional elections, winning 48% of Chamber of Deputies seats. Ciudad Juarez's murder rate reached all-time highs in October 2009 amid cartel battles.One of Mexico's most-wanted drug lords, Arturo Beltran Leyva, was killed in a December 2009 shoot-out with state security forces. Authorities put 2009 drug-related killings at around 6,500, the worst bloodshed year since President Calderon's late 2006 drug war declaration.**International Relations and Ongoing Challenges**President Calderon called on the United States in March 2010 to share drug trafficking battle responsibility after three US consulate-connected people were murdered in Ciudad Juarez. US President Barack Obama signed a $600m bill in August 2010 for more border agents and equipment to stem illegal immigration.Wikileaks released US diplomatic cables in December 2010 revealing the US ambassador questioned Mexican security forces' organized crime-fighting ability.An August 2011 Casino Royale attack in Monterrey killed 52 people after gunmen doused the building with fuel and ignited it.**Recent Political Developments**The army arrested a drug cartel leader in May 2012 over 49 people's killing, whose mutilated bodies were dumped on a major Nuevo Leon state road in one of the drug war's worst atrocities.PRI candidate Enrique Pena Nieto won the July 2012 presidential election. text: Stoke City boss Mark Hughes says Liverpool were incredibly fortunate to reach the League Cup final. Following a dramatic penalty shootout defeat, Stoke City's journey ended despite achieving their first victory at Anfield in over half a century. The Potters secured a 1-1 aggregate draw across the two-leg semi-final but ultimately fell short in the decisive spot-kicks.Marko Arnautovic's first-half injury-time strike proved crucial for Stoke, though manager Mark Hughes acknowledged the element of luck involved. It was offside, but we deserved it. We got the goal that won us the game, but not the tie, Hughes told BBC Stoke.The Stoke boss expressed confidence in his team's chances throughout the encounter. We always thought we had a chance even if others didn't, but we just couldn't get that second goal even though we looked the likelier side to score, he explained.Hughes didn't hide his frustration with how the tie concluded, pointing to Liverpool's fortune in progressing. You can see by the reaction of their fans and their players that they have been incredibly fortunate to progress to the final, he observed. Obviously once it goes to penalties it can go either way and heartbreakingly for us it has gone their way. These sort of things happen in sport, but that still doesn't make it any easier to take.The Potters entered the clash facing significant pressure after their underwhelming first-leg display at the Britannia Stadium three weeks prior. Currently sitting ninth in the Premier League table, just one point behind Jurgen Klopp's seventh-placed Liverpool, Stoke needed a strong response.Despite missing captain Ryan Shawcross through injury, with Marc Muniesa stepping in as replacement, the visitors delivered an impressive defensive performance. Liverpool failed to register a single shot on target throughout the match.Hughes's tactical approach proved effective, reverting to familiar Tony Pulis-style methods by deploying big men Jon Walters and Peter Crouch in attack. This strategy transformed Stoke into a more potent offensive force than their hosts.The manager praised his entire squad's commitment. To a man I can't fault any of them, said Hughes. They all put in fantastic performances. I'd highlight Peter Crouch who, along with Marc Muniesa, hadn't played for a long time.Hughes emphasized his team's superior performance on the night. We will hopefully get the credit we deserve. We came in difficult circumstances after losing the home leg, but were very positive and made a few changes, and on the night we were by far the better team, he stated. I'm really proud of what the players produced, but unfortunately we aren't the ones going to Wembley.Looking ahead to Saturday's fourth round FA Cup tie at Crystal Palace, Hughes faces potential injury concerns. Arnautovic sustained a back problem after taking heavy falls from challenges by Liverpool defender Jon Flanagan, while second-half substitute Charlie Adam managed only thirty minutes before departing in the first period of extra time with calf trouble.Interestingly, Adam was among three players on the pitch who featured in Liverpool's last trophy triumph - the 2012 League Cup final victory over Cardiff City, also decided by penalties, where he missed his spot-kick attempt.Stoke right-back Glen Johnson also participated in that Wembley success, converting one of Liverpool's three successful penalties. Jordan Henderson, now Liverpool captain, remained the sole survivor from Kenny Dalglish's 2012 squad still playing. Lucas Leiva, who emerged as one of Tuesday night's penalty heroes for the Reds, had missed that final due to injury.
