text: Respected by his peers and loved by millions, guitarist BB King was a blues legend who influenced a generation of musicians. The legendary blues guitarist who would become known worldwide as BB King entered the world as Riley B King in Mississippi during 1925. His iconic BB moniker emerged as a shortened version of Beale Street Blues Boy, a nickname he acquired following his 1947 relocation to Memphis.King honed his musical craft performing throughout the Chitlin' Circuit - a network of performance venues across America's racially segregated southern territories during that era. The circuit derived its distinctive name from chitterlings, a dish made from stewed pig intestines.His international breakthrough arrived in 1968 with his inaugural European tour, launching a global career that would see him welcomed and celebrated across continents. Reflecting on their friendship in 2007, King declared: I've never met a better man, a more gracious man than my friend Eric Clapton.Another notable partnership materialized in 1988 when King contributed to U2's Rattle and Hum album. Years later, in 2008, he reunited with frontman Bono at a tribute concert.King's distinguished career brought him to the White House on multiple occasions. In 1990, George and Barbara Bush presented him with the National Medal of Arts.Sixteen years afterward, he returned to 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue to receive the Presidential Medal of Freedom from another Bush administration member.Between these formal ceremonies, King enjoyed a casual jam session with President Bill Clinton in Beverly Hills during 2001. The saxophonist performing alongside them was Reverend Dave Boruff.BB returned to the White House in 2001, characteristically carrying his guitar. Throughout his career, King christened all his instruments Lucille, honoring a woman whose involvement in a fire nearly destroyed his first guitar.In Stockholm during 2004, King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden presented him with the Polar Music Prize. The recognition celebrated his significant contributions to the blues and his fundamental importance to the development of modern popular music.Reflecting on his career philosophy in 2010, King observed: I think that I know my job pretty well. But I'm never any better than my last job. I think that I'm here and, just as easy, cannot be here. So I never think that I've got it made.

text: British reggae band UB40 have praised Jeremy Corbyn as an incorruptible politician who will put working people first as they backed his campaign to remain as Labour leader. Celebrity endorsements continue flowing toward Jeremy Corbyn as the Labour leadership contest intensifies, with legendary British band UB40 throwing their weight behind the embattled politician.The Birmingham-formed group, whose record sales have reached 70 million worldwide, praised Corbyn for inspiring youth engagement and presenting what they termed a believable alternative to conventional politics. Their support joins that of other notable figures including actor Daniel Radcliffe, though best-selling Harry Potter author JK Rowling has sharply criticized Corbyn as a lousy leader.Corbyn faces a leadership challenge from Owen Smith, with results scheduled for announcement on 24 September.UB40, originally named after the government's unemployment benefit form of their era, dominated British charts throughout the 1980s and 1990s. The band accumulated 50 hit singles, including chart-toppers Red Red Wine, Can't Help Falling in Love, and I Got You Babe. Despite recent departures of three original members that sparked legal battles over the band's name usage, remaining members led by guitarist and vocalist Robin Campbell have rallied behind Corbyn.Campbell explained their endorsement: Jeremy has re-ignited an interest in politics for people who no longer felt included, and engaged and inspired a new generation of young voters who, for the first time, believe that they have an incorruptible politician who truly represents them.Drummer Jimmy Brown characterized Corbyn as the sole frontline politician willing to speak up for working people who have been badly treated by successive governments, including New Labour, in recent decades.The Labour leader, who recently survived a no-confidence vote following the EU referendum despite opposition from most of his MPs, welcomed UB40's support before their planned joint appearance Tuesday.UB40's story was and remains inspiring; people from across cultures and backgrounds coming together and combining their talents - in a time when prejudice was more prevalent - and creativity to produce music that has endured across decades, Corbyn responded.Corbyn has positioned arts as a priority for any future Labour government. His arts manifesto, released last month, promises additional funding for primary school arts activities across England and establishment of a unified national arts scholarship program.Meanwhile, tensions with prominent critics persist. text: Almost four million children in the UK do not own a book, according to a report by the National Literacy Trust. A charity's recent findings reveal a troubling surge in the number of children lacking personal book collections, with the figure climbing from one in ten back in 2005 to one in three today.The comprehensive study, which examined 18,000 children across 111 UK schools in September, found that 33.2% of school-aged participants did not possess books of their own - equivalent to approximately 3.8 million children nationwide.The research demonstrated a stark correlation between book ownership and academic performance. Children who maintained personal libraries showed significantly higher reading abilities and stronger overall school achievement compared to their peers without books.Among young people who owned books, more than half demonstrated reading skills above their expected age level, while fewer than one in ten fell below grade expectations. The contrast proved striking for children without personal book collections: nearly a fifth struggled to meet expected reading standards, with only one-third achieving above-average performance.The study highlighted concerning disparities along economic and gender lines. Children from wealthier families demonstrated higher rates of book ownership compared to those receiving free school meals, while boys showed lower book ownership rates than girls.Trust director Jonathan Douglas expressed particular alarm at the dramatic increase in bookless children over the past two decades.We know there is a direct correlation between book ownership and children's reading abilities, Douglas stated. With one in 6 in the UK struggling with literacy it is very worrying that many children could be missing out on opportunities to develop these essential skills.The research uncovered additional concerning patterns regarding children's exposure to reading culture. Approximately one-fifth of participants reported never visiting either bookshops or libraries, suggesting limited access to literary resources beyond school settings.However, the study also identified encouraging findings about reading engagement. Children who owned books demonstrated higher likelihood of daily reading habits, and the research showed that consuming any reading material - including magazines - outside classroom settings at least monthly correlated with improved reading achievement.The survey also revealed connections between reading proficiency and receiving books as gifts, underscoring the importance of books as presents in developing literacy skills.The trust strategically released these findings alongside launching their Christmas Gift of Reading campaign, which seeks public donations to provide books and reading support for disadvantaged children. Several children's book illustrators have contributed specially designed cards to support the fundraising initiative.The research reinforces growing concerns about educational inequality and literacy development, particularly as the proportion of children without access to personal reading materials continues expanding across the UK.

text: Conservative backbenchers are demanding radical changes to school funding in England within months. Speaking to BBC Radio 4's the World at One, he emphasized: I think you would be fascinated how strong the feelings are on this issue and the sort of campaign that is going to be pursued in the course of this year.Graham Stuart, the Conservative former chairman of the education select committee, believes dozens of Tory MPs want the earliest possible announcement, preferably during July's Budget. The most generously funded regions receive approximately £7,000 per student, while disadvantaged areas struggle with barely £4,000 per pupil.Despite ministerial intentions to reform the system dating back to 2010, followed by promises in 2013 and renewed pledges in the Conservative manifesto, the funding formula remains unchanged. But we recognise there is still work to which is why we have committed to looking at what more needs to be done to ensure that all local areas are funded justly.

text: Brightly coloured murals adorn the walls of the 'Little Hands' nursery. Beyond the chicken wire fence, dusty roads stretch into the distance, but inside this makeshift classroom with concrete walls and plastic tenting overhead, four- and five-year-olds sing and dance just like children anywhere else in the world.This scene unfolds in Jordan's Zataari camp, now home to thousands of Syrians who fled their war-torn homeland. What makes this kindergarten unique is that many students have never known life outside these camp boundaries.Many of the children we are seeing here now were born in the camp. They've known no other existence, says Neil Mathers, the head of Save the Children in Scotland.Save the Children operates three nurseries within Zataari, serving 52% of the camp's youngest residents. Yet the need far exceeds capacity.There are 40,000 children who need this kind of support in Zataari camp alone. Our kindergartens reach around 2,000 children so much more is needed to handle just the children in this camp, Mr Mathers says.From this sprawling settlement—one of the locations where UK-bound refugees will be selected—Syria's hills shimmer faintly through the desert haze. Located just miles south of Jordan's Syrian border, Zataari has expanded across 8 sq km (3 sq miles) of barren, stony terrain to become Jordan's fourth largest city by population.More than 80,000 people now inhabit what ranks as the world's second largest refugee camp. Their homes consist of tents, tin shacks, and ramshackle huts scattered across the desert landscape. Summer temperatures soar above 50C, while winter nights plunge below freezing.It's tough, says Dominic Graham, Jordan country director for Edinburgh-based charity Mercy Corps. Life in the camps is tough.Mercy Corps joins dozens of non-governmental organizations that have maintained operations in Zataari since its establishment four years ago, when Syria's increasingly brutal civil war first drove refugees across borders.Basic infrastructure exists—water, sanitation, and shelter systems function throughout the camp. A rudimentary economy has emerged, complete with markets and small shops selling daily necessities. Yet despite this unwanted permanence, existence remains bleak. Lives remain suspended, leading nowhere.Initial expectations proved tragically optimistic. Syrian refugees, government officials, and aid agencies alike believed President Assad's regime would collapse quickly, making this a crisis of months rather than years. Those assumptions have long since crumbled.Hassan, who arrived in Zaatari last year, represents countless others who withhold their full names to protect relatives still inside Syria. With no savings remaining, he and his family now contemplate returning despite ongoing dangers.He said: I will go back as soon as it is safe. But he doesn't think that will be soon.According to Mr Graham from Mercy Corps, most refugees desperately want to resume their former Syrian lives, but the prospects of that are getting thinner and thinner.Zataari represents merely the visible portion of a massive displacement crisis. Nearly eight million internally displaced people remain trapped inside Syria. Those who reach camps like Zataari are often the fortunate ones—either geographically advantaged by living near borders or financially capable of paying smugglers for safe passage to neighboring countries.The most vulnerable and poorest frequently remain behind, making internal aid delivery crucial, according to Steve Gordon from Glasgow, Mercy Corps' regional security manager.If you are assisting inside Syria and people are staying there and not coming out, they are not becoming a burden on the surrounding countries.Challenges multiply exponentially as front lines shift constantly and Russia's intervention reshapes conflict dynamics. Mercy Corps reports massive population movements amid these changing circumstances. Gordon emphasizes that increasing danger paradoxically heightens supply needs.If an area is going to be cut off you have to pre-position supplies in those areas to sustain those communities through what could be very hard times.Children splash in water sprayed from tankers to settle dust on camp streets while Syria's distant hills remain barely visible. Whether these young residents will ever see their homeland again remains unknowable, but future possibilities increasingly influence refugee decisions about staying or leaving.Near the security checkpoint, a weathered silver bus awaits departure for the Syrian border. Despite the dangers that originally drove them here, some refugees find camp life so hopeless they choose return—a small but steady trickle as memories of past threats fade.Others set their sights on Europe and new beginnings there. Individuals and small family groups undertake perilous journeys, hoping successful settlement in Germany, France, or Britain might eventually allow remaining family members to follow.The Syrian refugee crisis has consumed billions in international spending. Since the war began, the UK alone has allocated just over £1bn across the region, with £330m directed specifically to Jordan.Jeff Tudor, who heads the UK government's international development programme in Jordan, brings veteran humanitarian experience to this intractable situation. He recognizes no simple or rapid solutions exist.He says: We're hanging on in there, but ultimately we will need a political solution to what is happening in Syria. Even if we get a political solution tomorrow we are looking at at least a decade. The refugees won't go back overnight, the situation in Syria won't allow it.

text: Scotland's largest council has said the greater Glasgow area will suffer unless there is specific government action to mitigate the effects of Brexit. Following the UK's referendum decision to exit the European Union, Glasgow City Council has released a comprehensive report outlining the economic hurdles ahead for the region. The document emphasizes that both Scottish and UK governments must implement specific policy decisions to safeguard the city's interests.Central to these requirements is ensuring that EU-funded initiatives receive continued backing from both governmental levels. Frank McAveety, Glasgow City Council leader, warned that immediate governmental intervention is essential to prevent potential economic turmoil.I believe that Brexit will confront Glasgow with major economic challenges, McAveety stated. I also believe these can be overcome if special action is taken by the Scottish and UK governments. If that happens then the problems associated with Brexit can become an opportunity for economic growth and not a threat of crisis.The comprehensive study, titled Brexit and the Glasgow Economy: Impacts, Actions and Asks, represents a collaborative effort between Glasgow City Council, Glasgow Chamber of Commerce, and the Glasgow Economic Leadership board. This partnership encompasses the council, chamber of commerce, Scottish Enterprise, and Skills Development Scotland.More than 100 prominent figures from business, local government, and academic sectors contributed to the report's development, according to council officials. The document will be presented to the first minister's Standing Committee on Europe, under the leadership of Professor Anton Muscatelli, Principal of Glasgow University.Six primary recommendations targeting both Scottish and UK governments form the report's core strategy for Brexit impact mitigation.Professor Sir Jim McDonald, who chairs the Glasgow Economic Leadership board and serves as Principal of Strathclyde University, acknowledged Brexit's profound implications. There is no doubt that Brexit is a fundamental system shock and one that poses challenges to us all, he observed.We will now position our city to meet the challenges of Brexit and exploit longer-term opportunities to grow our economy. Only by working together can we boost our economic fundamentals: our skills, innovation and entrepreneurship. It is on these foundations that our future will and must be based.Stuart Patrick, chief executive of Glasgow Chamber of Commerce, stressed the urgency of coordinated action. He emphasized that navigating post-Brexit realities requires swift, unified responses.In order to take advantage of the new world as it exists in the aftermath of the Brexit vote and to seize the opportunities that will be presented to us, a clear, collective, coherent and forward looking approach from the City of Glasgow and from the Scottish and UK governments is required, Patrick explained.We cannot do this alone and whilst uncertainly continues around our future trading relationship with the EU we must combine all our efforts now to secure investment and jobs and to boost trade.

text: Mevlut Mert Atlintas shouted phrases in broken Arabic in the seconds after he shot dead Russian ambassador to Turkey, Andrei Karlov. Interior Minister Suleyman Soylu identified the gunman as a 22-year-old policeman, revealing that Altintas was born on 24 June 1994 in the town of Soke in quiet, conservative Aydin province in western Turkey. Following the shooting, as terrified onlookers scattered, he delivered a chilling declaration quoting an Islamic teaching about jihad: We are the ones who pledged loyalty to [the Prophet] Muhammad to fight jihad as long as we live.He also shouted Allahu Akbar, or God is great.Switching to native-sounding Turkish, he then said: Don't forget about Syria, don't forget about Aleppo. All those who participate in this tyranny will be held accountable.After shooting the ambassador, Altintas refused to surrender and engaged in a firefight with police for approximately 15 minutes before being killed. Immediately following the incident, family members including his father, mother and sister were detained for questioning at their homes in Soke.Now investigators face a crucial determination: whether the attacker was motivated by the destruction of eastern Aleppo, or was part of a wider plot to derail relations with Russia.Unconfirmed reports suggested he had been suspended for several weeks until mid-November because of suspected links to the plotters behind Turkey's failed July coup. text: The SNP's national executive has ruled not to endorse two sitting MPs as candidates in the general election. Two former SNP MPs who now serve as independents have been denied party endorsement for the upcoming general election, forcing them to step aside as the party's ruling body made its candidate selections known.The SNP's National Executive Committee informed Michelle Thomson and Natalie McGarry that they would not receive backing for their respective seats. Both politicians had previously withdrawn from the SNP parliamentary group under different circumstances.Thomson, who represents Edinburgh West, removed herself from the party whip in 2015 during an ongoing police investigation concerning property transactions. Following the NEC's decision, she expressed being very disappointed but confirmed she would not seek re-election after careful consideration.Meanwhile, McGarry was denied endorsement amid fraud allegations. The Glasgow East MP responded via Twitter, stating the NEC's decision came as no surprise and that she would make no further statement, preferring to concentrate on constituents & staff.On Saturday, the SNP announced that all 54 of its current MPs had received candidate endorsement. Westminster leader Angus Robertson praised the parliamentary group's performance, declaring: SNP MPs have been the hardest working group at Westminster and, with Labour in complete disarray, the only real opposition to the Tory government.Robertson added: Over the coming weeks we will work harder than ever to retain the trust of people in every community across Scotland.In her detailed statement, Thomson defended her position regarding the property investigation, emphasizing: Since September 2015 there have been reports concerning a solicitor I used some seven years ago. I have always made it clear that I have done nothing wrong and it is a matter of public record that it was the solicitor who was under investigation and not myself, that no charges have ever been brought and that I assisted PS (Police Scotland) on a purely voluntary basis.Thomson criticized the party's selection process, arguing that even in political parties, the concept of natural justice must apply, as must the need for defined processes that are applied fairly, rigorously and transparently. She recommended the SNP employ the services of an external body to help them develop a process as soon as possible.Reflecting on her parliamentary service, Thomson stated: I have been privileged to be the MP for Edinburgh West. After careful consideration I have decided not to stand again at this time and I would encourage all the political parties to avoid personal smears and instead focus on what people really want to hear about.The developments come as Britain prepares for the 8 June election following Prime Minister Theresa May's snap election announcement, which MPs subsequently endorsed by 552 votes to 13.With Thomson and McGarry's departures, the SNP must now identify five candidates total. This includes finding replacements for the Glasgow East and Edinburgh West constituencies, where several party activists have already declared their candidacy intentions.The remaining three seats requiring candidate selection are Dumfriesshire, Clydesdale and Tweeddale, Edinburgh South, and Orkney and Shetland - constituencies the party failed to capture in 2015.

text: Lufthansa pilots have begun their eighth strike this year, forcing the cancellation of 1,511 flights over Monday and Tuesday. A labor dispute that began targeting primarily European routes has now escalated, with Lufthansa facing an expanded strike affecting international flights starting Tuesday. The walkout threatens to disrupt travel for 200,000 passengers as the conflict over retirement and pension modifications intensifies.The Vereinigung Cockpit (VC) union, representing approximately 5,400 Lufthansa pilots, has broadened its industrial action to amplify pressure on the airline. This expansion follows last week's 12-hour stoppage at Germanwings, Lufthansa's budget subsidiary, where VC members participated in a targeted work halt.Central to the dispute is Lufthansa's proposal to increase pilots' retirement age from 55. While the company has agreed to preserve existing retirement arrangements for current employees, it refuses to extend these benefits to future hires. This compromise has failed to satisfy union demands.We are extending the strike in order to send a clearer signal. Perhaps now, Lufthansa will finally come round, declared union board member Markus Wahl. text: Joe Rowley scored his first goal to give Chesterfield a victory over Port Vale that keeps their slender League One survival hopes alive for another week. A teenage striker's second-half intervention has pushed Chesterfield closer to survival while deepening Port Vale's relegation fears in a crucial League One encounter.Joe Rowley, just 17 years old, struck the decisive blow that now leaves Vale nine points adrift of safety with only four matches left to play. The result condemns the visitors to yet another fruitless away trip, intensifying their battle against the drop.The opening 45 minutes reflected both sides' precarious league positions, with limited quality on display. Vale's best early opportunity came in the 27th minute when Thorsten Stuckmann got down well to deny JJ Hooper's low effort, but neither team could establish meaningful control before the interval.Everything changed after the break. Vale nearly broke the deadlock seven minutes into the second half as Chris Eagles found himself with a golden chance at close range, only to be brilliantly thwarted by Stuckmann's reflexes. However, Chesterfield capitalized on this reprieve just two minutes later when their rapid counter-attack paid dividends.The breakthrough arrived when Kristian Dennis unleashed a powerful drive that Deniz Mehmet could only push away. Rowley was perfectly positioned to pounce on the loose ball, firing home to give the Spireites a vital advantage.Vale's struggles to fashion clear-cut chances continued throughout the remainder of the contest. Their desperation nearly cost them further punishment in the 81st minute when Dan Gardner unleashed a thunderous 25-yard strike that forced Mehmet into an acrobatic save, tipping the ball over his crossbar.The closing stages saw Vale throw everything forward in search of a lifeline. Despite mounting sustained pressure during stoppage time, with the visitors earning multiple corners, Chesterfield's defensive resolve held firm to secure three precious points.This victory significantly improves Chesterfield's survival prospects, while Vale - sitting just one point above the relegation zone despite having a game in hand - face an increasingly daunting task to preserve their League One status. text: Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara became the first player to score four successive one-day international centuries as his side beat Scotland at the World Cup. Scotland's pursuit of their first World Cup victory fell short despite posting their highest-ever total while chasing against a Test-playing nation, as Sri Lanka secured a comprehensive win in Hobart to claim their fourth Pool A triumph.Kumar Sangakkara's remarkable tournament form continued with his fourth century of the competition - a masterful 124 that anchored Sri Lanka's imposing 363-9 total. The 37-year-old wicketkeeper-batsman has now struck tons against Bangladesh, England, Australia, and Scotland in this World Cup campaign.The veteran left-hander achieved another milestone by surpassing 500 ODI dismissals as Scotland were eventually dismissed for 215. His latest century moves him within one of Sachin Tendulkar's World Cup record of six hundreds, while his ODI run tally of 14,189 trails only the retired Indian legend's 18,426 in the 50-over format.I've been batting and keeping for a long time, it's getting harder and the joints are creaking and aching, but I consider myself lucky to be part of a great team, Sangakkara reflected. No matter how hard you try, it's hard to pinpoint why I'm playing so well. Maybe I'm making better decisions at the crease, I don't know. Whatever it is, it's working for me at the moment.At Bellerive Oval, Sangakkara became the first player ever to register four World Cup centuries, following previous scores of 105 not out against Bangladesh, 117 not out against England, and 104 against Australia. The prolific batsman, who has hinted at ODI retirement following this tournament, has enjoyed exceptional form over the past 12-18 months, recently becoming the fastest to 12,000 Test runs while scoring his 11th double century - just one shy of Don Bradman's record.Sri Lanka's formidable total was built on a crucial 195-run second-wicket stand between Sangakkara and Tillakaratne Dilshan (104). The pair reached their centuries on consecutive deliveries before Josh Davey struck twice in quick succession to dismiss both batsmen.Davey's impressive 3-63 figures elevated him to the tournament's leading wicket-taker with 14 scalps, edging ahead of New Zealand's Trent Boult and Tim Southee. Captain Angelo Mathews provided late fireworks with a blistering 20-ball half-century featuring four consecutive sixes off Matt Machan's bowling, threatening to push Sri Lanka beyond 400. However, Scotland's disciplined catching and bowling in the death overs restricted the tail-enders.Scotland's response began disastrously when Kyle Coetzer offered a simple return catch to Lasith Malinga on just the second ball. Despite this setback, captain Preston Mommsen (60) and Freddie Coleman (70) restored dignity to the chase with a valuable 118-run fourth-wicket partnership.Once this partnership was broken, only all-rounder Richie Berrington (29) managed a meaningful contribution as Scotland's fifth defeat confirmed their winless tournament status. They face co-hosts Australia in their final group encounter on Saturday in Hobart.Sri Lanka's commanding Pool A performance positions them for a likely quarter-final clash with South Africa in Sydney on Wednesday.Listen to highlights from Test Match Special's and 5 live Sport's 2015 World Cup coverage.

text: Too many patients are locked into mental health rehabilitation wards far from home, a review of England's psychiatric services suggests. The Care Quality Commission has revealed that 3,500 beds exist within locked mental health facilities nationwide, though officials believe many patients could receive better treatment in community-based residential care closer to their homes.Safety concerns on mental health wards emerged as another significant issue in the comprehensive report, while NHS England emphasized that progress continues with increased funding allocations.Claire Murdoch, head of mental health for NHS England, acknowledged reasons for optimism exist, but stressed that improvements aligned with the NHS five-year plan priorities remain essential.The CQC's examination encompassed all specialist mental health services throughout England, including both NHS-operated facilities and NHS services delivered through independent sector providers.Nearly all services earned ratings of good or outstanding for maintaining caring, compassionate staff, with numerous examples of excellent patient care documented across the system.However, multiple areas of concern surfaced during the investigation.Locked rehabilitation wards particularly troubled CQC leadership, with two-thirds managed by independent providers failing to deliver appropriate 21st-century care models. Patient stays averaged 341 days on these wards - an excessive duration that risks institutionalization while undermining community rehabilitation goals.Dr Paul Lelliott, lead for mental health at the CQC, expressed surprise at the scale of locked rehabilitation beds discovered. We can't say exactly how many of the people on these wards don't need to be in locked facilities, but we do suspect that quite a high proportion of people in these services could, and should be, moved back to be much closer to home and be cared for in residential settings that provide much more independence, and also be supported by community services rather than being in hospital, he stated.Safety deficiencies affected approximately one-third of services requiring improvement, while one in 20 received inadequate safety ratings - indicating immediate patient safety concerns.Inspectors highlighted old and unsuitable buildings as contributing factors, citing examples of corridor blind spots preventing proper observation of patients at self-harm risk.Nursing shortages compounded safety worries, with mental health nursing staff declining 12% between January 2010 and 2017.Brian Dow from Rethink Mental Illness charity commented on the findings, recognizing sector-wide commitment to high-quality care delivery while acknowledging an awful long way to go remains ahead.There is fairly large number of services that the CQC says need improvement and that raises big questions about what is happening in this system, Dow observed. Is there enough money in there? Do we have the right kind of people able to deliver the care? Are people involved in their own care and are people supported and trained to deliver the care?Ms Murdoch described the report as a really fair assessment of national mental health services. It sets out the fact that most providers of mental health care are now either moving towards the good category or are good and moving towards outstanding - so it is showing improvement. But quite rightly it also looks at what needs to improve next, she told the BBC.

text: Safety inspections will be carried out at schools across Scotland following the collapse of a wall at an Edinburgh primary, BBC Scotland has learned. A decade after Miller Construction completed their work, defects discovered in four Edinburgh buildings forced temporary closures across the capital's school system.Storm Gertrude's January assault on Oxgangs primary school proved catastrophic - hundreds of bricks were torn from the building's exterior wall. Safety inspections that followed exposed fundamental problems with the external wall construction dating back to the school's 2005 completion under the Public Private Partnership 1 project.The Oxgangs incident triggered broader investigations that uncovered identical issues at three additional Edinburgh institutions: St Peter's RC Primary, Firrhill High and Braidburn Special Schools. Miller Construction had built all four facilities during the same period, before Galliford Try acquired the company in 2014.Officials declared the quartet of schools unsafe for student occupancy, leading to immediate temporary shutdowns. Reopening is scheduled to coincide with the end of Easter holidays.Now, precautionary surveys are expanding beyond Edinburgh's borders to examine schools constructed by the same contractor across Glasgow, Fife and Inverclyde regions.The four schools temporarily closed in Edinburgh comprised the second phase of the PPP1 programme, which was completed by Miller Construction in 2005, a Galliford Try spokesperson explained. We have already started remedial work at Oxgangs Primary School and are assessing the requirement for work on the further three schools.The company emphasized swift action: Any remedial work required will be carried out as quickly as possible allowing the children to return to their studies with the minimum disruption.Despite having no awareness of additional defects, Galliford Try has proactively reached out to clients whose PPP school projects involved Miller Construction in Glasgow, Fife and Inverclyde. While we are not aware of any defects, as a precautionary measure, we have contacted the clients of the PPP school projects Miller Construction undertook in Glasgow, Fife and Inverclyde, the spokesperson noted. Further investigations will be carried out as appropriate.Edinburgh's original PPP1 programme formed part of a massive educational infrastructure initiative. The 2001 agreement, valued at £360m, established a 30-year arrangement where private consortium partners designed, constructed and managed school facilities in exchange for fixed council payments. Miller Construction participated in this consortium and similar ventures throughout Scotland.The scale of these partnerships was substantial - Glasgow's PPP1 deal, signed one year prior to Edinburgh's, carried a price tag three times larger and encompassed 29 secondary schools plus one primary across the country.Glasgow City Council has confirmed that surveys will now examine the handful of schools constructed by Miller Construction under their PPP contract.Meanwhile, inspections are proceeding in other affected regions. text: The head of the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), Martin Wheatley, is to stand down from his post after just two years in charge. The Financial Conduct Authority announced that its chief executive will depart in September, marking the end of a turbulent tenure at the City regulator.Chancellor George Osborne expressed gratitude for Mr Wheatley's contributions, stating he had done a brilliant job of launching the FCA in tough circumstances. However, Osborne added: The government believes that different leadership is required to build on those foundations.Tracey McDermott, Mr Wheatley's deputy, will assume interim leadership while authorities conduct a search for his permanent successor.Reflecting on his departure, Mr Wheatley said he was incredibly proud of what he and his team had achieved together in building the FCA over the last four years. I know that the organisation will build on that strong start and work so that the financial services industry continues to thrive.Behind the scenes, Treasury officials orchestrated Mr Wheatley's unexpected exit from the Financial Conduct Authority leadership. Sources indicate that recent discussions between Treasury representatives and the FCA chief made it unmistakably clear that the Chancellor would not extend Mr Wheatley's contract beyond its March 2016 renewal date.Facing this inevitable outcome, Mr Wheatley opted for an early departure rather than serving out his remaining months under such circumstances.Relations between the Treasury and Mr Wheatley had long been strained, particularly due to his confrontational regulatory philosophy. He famously declared his intention to shoot first and ask questions later when confronting misconduct within the financial services sector.This aggressive stance generated considerable hostility from banking industry leaders, who frequently directed harsh criticism toward Mr Wheatley and his regulatory approach.Treasury Committee chairman Andrew Tyrie acknowledged Mr Wheatley's contributions during a challenging period. Martin took over at an exceptionally difficult time. He was faced with the challenge of changing the culture of both the regulated community and the regulator, given the exposure by the crisis of the shortcomings of the FSA, Tyrie explained.With the interests of millions of consumers to protect, tens of thousands of firms to regulate and the need to secure more competition in the financial services sector, it will be essential to find a high quality successor, he added.Mr Wheatley's regulatory career began when he joined the Financial Services Authority in September 2011, before ascending to lead the restructured FCA following its April 2013 launch, succeeding Hector Sants.His reputation as an uncompromising regulator was forged through previous roles in Hong Kong's markets and at the US Securities and Exchanges Commission - credentials that initially made him an attractive candidate for the FCA position.Recently, Mr Wheatley had attempted to moderate perceptions of his regulatory approach, repeatedly assuring City leaders that the FCA wasn't seeking to put heads on sticks nor hunting for scalps under new banking accountability regulations.Nevertheless, the FCA under his leadership imposed some of the largest regulatory penalties in City history.The regulator's tenure wasn't without controversy. Last year, a significant scandal emerged involving the insurance sector when the Daily Telegraph published leaked information suggesting the FCA planned to investigate 30 million pension policies, including some dating back to the 1970s.The revelation triggered massive sell-offs in insurance company shares, erasing billions in market value and prompting a parliamentary investigation. The fallout resulted in four senior executives, including Mr Wheatley, forfeiting their annual bonuses.

text: Crime involving mopeds has gone up by more than 600% in London in the past two years, BBC London can reveal. Scotland Yard's internal statistics reveal a staggering surge in moped-enabled criminality across London, with 7,668 recorded offences in 2016 alone - representing approximately 22 incidents daily. This dramatic escalation from just 1,053 cases throughout 2014 and 4,647 in 2015 has prompted serious concerns among law enforcement officials.The Metropolitan Police attributes this explosion primarily to teenagers who steal mopeds before deploying them as getaway vehicles for various criminal enterprises, including attacks, robberies, and thefts. While other major UK cities have experienced similar trends, London's problem dwarfs all others in scale and severity.The capital's unique characteristics make it particularly vulnerable to such crimes. Its dense concentration of luxury retail establishments, combined with countless tourists carrying expensive mobile devices, creates an irresistible target-rich environment for opportunistic criminals.Supt Mark Payne, who leads Operation Venice - established two years ago specifically to combat this growing menace - expressed grave concerns about the shifting criminal landscape. I think it's a huge concern because it is a change in criminal behaviour, he stated. The fact of the matter is it's much more difficult to deal with people on mopeds than it was people who were committing those sorts of crimes before on foot or on bicycles.Despite identifying 200 suspected individuals linked to moped-related crimes, the Met faces significant prosecution challenges due to insufficient evidence in many cases. Additionally, pursuit policies create complications when suspects ride without helmets, as safety concerns often prevent officers from giving chase.Recent incidents have intensified scrutiny of police pursuit protocols. Four Islington officers currently face disciplinary proceedings following the death of teenager Henry Hicks, after an inquest jury determined he died during an unauthorized pursuit in 2012. Separately, the police watchdog continues investigating the death of 18-year-old Lewis Johnson, whose scooter crashed during another pursuit.To circumvent prosecution difficulties for major crimes, the Met has adopted what it calls an Achilles Heel strategy - reminiscent of tactics once used against notorious gangster Al Capone. This approach targets repeat offenders through lesser charges such as driving without insurance, lacking proper licenses, or other traffic violations when more serious allegations cannot be proven.However, the Met firmly rejects suggestions that the situation has spiraled out of control or that criminals exploit helmet-related pursuit restrictions. Officials maintain they have achieved an appropriate balance between public safety and effective law enforcement when evaluating high-speed chase risks.As part of their response strategy, police have also encouraged moped owners to enhance their vehicles' security through additional locking mechanisms to deter theft.

text: Banking giant JP Morgan Chase plans to raise the hourly wages of 18,000 US staff over the next three years. JP Morgan Chase will boost wages for its lowest-paid employees, with CEO Jamie Dimon emphasizing the private sector's responsibility to tackle income inequality.The salary adjustments will impact bank tellers and customer service representatives, lifting their hourly compensation from $10.15 (£7.71) to a range of $12-$16, with specific amounts determined by geographical location.In a New York Times opinion piece, Dimon declared: A pay increase is the right thing to do. Wages for many Americans have gone nowhere for too long. The executive argued that this decision enables more people to begin to share in the rewards of economic growth.Beyond social responsibility, Dimon positioned the wage hike as a strategic business move that would help the bank attract and retain quality employees. Following the announcement, JP Morgan's stock price climbed 1.2% on Tuesday.This wage increase places JP Morgan among a growing list of major corporations addressing worker compensation. Starbucks revealed plans Monday to raise wages for 150,000 hourly employees, while McDonald's announced similar increases for workers at company-owned locations in April.The broader economic context reveals persistent wage stagnation throughout the post-recession recovery period, despite improvements in employment levels. Federal Reserve Chair Janet Yellen has identified this trend as evidence that the labor market hasn't reached full capacity, prompting the central bank to monitor wage growth developments closely.Income disparity between high and low earners has emerged as a pivotal issue in the current US election cycle.Dimon's New York Times piece urged businesses to expand their commitment to employee welfare. He suggested that companies unable to afford wage increases could still contribute through worker training initiatives and mentoring programs.The CEO also advocated for government action, specifically calling for expansion of the Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC) to cover more workers. Currently, the EITC provides tax refunds to low-income workers with children.We face many challenges. But they can be overcome by government, business and the non-profit sectors working together to build on models of success that advance economic opportunity and create more widely shared prosperity, Dimon concluded.

text: Police have said the number of people caught drink-driving during the annual Christmas crackdown increased significantly on the previous year. Between 27 November and 2 January, authorities made 396 arrests—marking a dramatic 42% surge from the 282 recorded during 2014-15. Among those detained was a police officer, while another motorist was apprehended with children present in the vehicle.The arrests encompassed drivers who were unfit to operate vehicles, along with those who either couldn't provide samples or refused to do so. One individual registered four times above the legal drink-drive threshold, and another was caught driving under the influence on separate occasions.Assistant Chief Constable Alan Todd of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI) condemned those arrested for disregarding the safety of themselves and others through this shameful and incredibly dangerous practice. He warned that convicted offenders would lose their driving privileges for a minimum of twelve months, with many facing potential job loss or imprisonment.Every year across Northern Ireland, drinking and driving kills, maims and wrecks families, he said. We detected a driver, with their children in the car, at three o'clock in the afternoon having been drinking.Todd urged drivers to consider the devastating impact of their choices: Think about the consequences to yourself and your family of being involved in a serious collision. How would you feel if some innocent person was killed?The arrested police officer faces both court proceedings and internal PSNI disciplinary action, potentially resulting in suspension or dismissal, according to ACC Todd.Men comprised the majority of offenders at 325 arrests, while women accounted for 71 cases. The age range spanned from 16 to 83 years old.Environment Minister Mark H Durkan highlighted the grave statistics: Drink-driving has caused over 2,000 deaths and serious injuries since 2000. text: The amount of nursery and pre-school provision for children in special schools is to be reduced. Starting this September, Northern Ireland's Education Authority (EA) will implement a significant reduction in pre-school hours across all 39 special schools throughout the region.Children with moderate to severe learning difficulties will see their daily attendance cut from at least 4.5 hours to just 2.5 hours. This dramatic change emerged through correspondence between the EA and a concerned parent.The EA's letter explicitly states that from September 2016, all pre-school children will receive 2.5 hours in pre-school per day. Officials justify this decision as one that is designed to increase the opportunity for children to access special school places, while promoting greater regional consistency.Strong opposition has emerged from the Strategic Leadership Forum for Special Schools (SLFSS), which represents principals and governors. In their submission to the Northern Ireland Assembly, they expressed complete disagreement with the policy shift.The organization warns that reduced hours will hold back and restrict the development of children with complex needs, citing multiple negative impacts they anticipate from the change.Francine Wilson exemplifies parental concerns about the new policy. Her three-year-old son Aodhan, who has Down's Syndrome, was expected to receive five hours of nursery placement when starting special school this September.Aodhan has Down's Syndrome and we were hoping in September 2016 he would get five hours of nursery placement, Wilson explained. Receiving two and a half hours will, I believe, result in delayed development in Aodhan, both educationally and socially.The EA defends its position by referencing established educational policy. A spokesperson emphasized that the reduction aligns with the Department of Education's 'Learning to Learn' framework.There has been a progressive move towards part-time places in all sectors, the spokesperson stated. This policy recognises the research evidence that there is no discernible difference in children's development at the start of primary school between those who received part-time and full-time pre-school provision.The authority maintains that the restructuring will increase the opportunity for children to access special school places, preferably nearer to their homes. They conclude that the provision of increased access and greater regional consistency is a priority.

text: Chris Coleman says the 2018 World Cup campaign will be his last as Wales manager. Wales manager Chris Coleman has declared that the upcoming World Cup qualifying campaign will mark his final chapter with the national team, despite his reputation soaring to unprecedented heights following their remarkable Euro 2016 semi-final achievement.At 46, Coleman remains bound by contract through the conclusion of the next World Cup. Wales will kick off their qualifying journey with a home fixture against Moldova on 5 September.I am sure this will be my last campaign whether we qualify or not, said Coleman. That will be six or seven years in the job, which is a long time. So I think this will be my last hit, at it so I will give it my best shot, but I would not consider going anywhere else. I want to see this through.The manager expressed confidence in his squad's potential, citing their optimal age profile. There's success in this team, I think, because they're at a good age. But I'll certainly give everything I've got in this next campaign. I'll make sure they do.Since Coleman's January 2012 appointment, both Wales and their manager have experienced a dramatic reversal of fortune. The nation had plummeted to 117th in world rankings just five months before his arrival. Though Coleman endured the most disastrous start of any Wales manager—losing his opening four matches—he has since orchestrated the country's golden period.Euro 2016 marked Wales' return to major tournament football after a 58-year absence. Their semi-final run surpassed their previous pinnacle achievement: reaching the 1958 World Cup quarter-finals.Following qualification success, Coleman secured a contract extension in May that extends through Russia 2018. He harbors no second thoughts about finalizing the agreement before Euro 2016's triumph.If they [FAW] wanted to talk to me about another contract I would be cashing in a bit, wouldn't I? Same as if I jumped ship and went somewhere else because we had done well at a tournament, Coleman explained. I would not feel right. I have signed a good contract and I am looking forward to the campaign.Wales' underdog status throughout history may shift following their European Championship exploits. The 2018 World Cup qualifying draw has placed them alongside Austria, Serbia, Republic of Ireland, Georgia and Moldova—a relatively favorable grouping.However, Coleman anticipates fresh challenges. The biggest challenge for us is that we will be a scalp now in this campaign because of what we've just done, said Coleman. Teams will play differently against us and rather than us being the underdogs, which we're very good at, we'll be expected to win.This expectation shift demands tactical evolution. We've not been used to breaking teams down. We've been used to hitting teams on the counter-attack because they've attacked us because they expect to get something from us, Coleman noted. We may have to look at how we approach it slightly differently in terms of what the opposition are going to do to us.The 5-3-2 formation that served Wales throughout Euro 2016 and most qualifying matches may undergo modification. Coleman previously deployed a four-man defense effectively, notably in a 2014 goalless draw against Belgium, and tactical adjustments remain under consideration.When you change formation with an international team, sometimes you're on thin ice, but you have to be brave and I will, Coleman added. I'd rather do that than not do anything. In my first campaign, for large parts of it I didn't do anything. I left it the same. I wouldn't make that same mistake again.The former Fulham manager reflected on early career lessons. You learn from that, you learn from failing and coming up short. I was trying to do everything that Speeds [the late Gary Speed, Coleman's predecessor] was doing because I was told it was working and don't change it. It didn't work for me - it blew up in my face. I'll never make that mistake again.

text: Rafael Nadal beat world number one Novak Djokovic in a pulsating four-set final to claim his second US Open title in New York. After a grueling three hours and 21 minutes, the 27-year-old Spaniard delivered a magnificent performance to claim victory in a captivating encounter, winning 6-2 3-6 6-4 6-1. The third set proved pivotal as he demonstrated remarkable resilience to secure the triumph.Arthur Ashe Stadium's 23,000 spectators witnessed an extraordinary spectacle, highlighted by an incredible 54-shot rally - surpassing the tournament's previous longest by 20 shots - that perfectly encapsulated this thrilling battle.This victory brings Nadal's Grand Slam singles collection to 13 titles, positioning him just one behind Pete Sampras on the all-time leaderboard, while Roger Federer maintains his record with 17. Following his seven-month absence due to knee injury that forced him to miss last year's US Open, Nadal is poised to reclaim the world number one ranking.Having this success is amazing, he said. Let's hope he stays healthy because it wil be great for our sport.The Majorcan expressed his passion for competition: I really love the competition, I really love the sport. All my career I dreamed to be involved in matches like today. I enjoy every moment. These things are not forever. In a few years I won't have this chance. I try my best, I have passion and that's all I can do.Monday's final delivered the anticipated electrifying, punishing contest as these rivals clashed for the 37th time - surpassing the McEnroe-Lendl rivalry to establish a new Open era record since 1968. Starting as many observers' favorite, he immediately validated those expectations by dominating the opening hour, unleashing devastating forehands that left Djokovic scrambling for answers.Nadal secured two service breaks to capture the first set in a swift 42 minutes. However, the following 80 minutes belonged entirely to Djokovic, whose forehand began controlling proceedings while his return game intensified the pressure.The seemingly unbreakable Nadal serve crumbled three consecutive times, beginning with that exhausting 54-shot rally that utilized every corner of the court. Djokovic stormed through six of seven games to establish a commanding 2-0 third-set advantage.With Nadal staggering and defending another break point to prevent falling two breaks down, that crucial hold proved decisive when Djokovic's momentum stalled and errors returned in the sixth game.At the two-hour, 17-minute mark, the world's premier players stood deadlocked at 3-3 in the third set. After surviving an early fourth-set break point via net cord fortune, Nadal eliminated luck from the equation by crushing another forehand on his subsequent opportunity.This titanic struggle concluded anticlimactically as Djokovic sent two backhands beyond the tramlines, falling behind 5-1. Yet emotions ran high after Nadal watched the Serb find the net on match point.The triumphant Spaniard collapsed to the court before tearfully embracing his supporters.All of my team knows how much this match today means to me, added Nadal. text: Yorkshire captain Andrew Gale and one-day skipper Alex Lees both made half-centuries to help their side avoid the follow-on against Lancashire. Yorkshire avoided the follow-on but Lancashire maintained their commanding position as the Roses match at Old Trafford headed into its final day.The visitors posted 360 in their first innings, with Alex Lees contributing 85 and Andrew Gale adding 83 in a crucial 130-run partnership for the third wicket. Kyle Jarvis proved Lancashire's most effective bowler, claiming 4-70.However, Lancashire's openers ensured their side's dominance continued. Tom Smith (35*) and teenage sensation Haseeb Hameed (30*) guided the home team to 70-0 by stumps, extending their overall lead to 204 runs.At just 19 years old, first-innings centurion Hameed now sits within 40 runs of reaching 1,000 County Championship runs in his debut full season - a remarkable achievement for the young opener.Yorkshire's morning began promisingly from 136-2, but Lancashire quickly struck. Jarvis dismissed Lees lbw in his opening over, while Gale fell agonizingly short of his first Championship century of the campaign, managing 83 before steering Smith to gully - just 17 runs from three figures.The afternoon session proved devastating for the Tykes. A dramatic collapse saw three wickets tumble for merely 11 runs after lunch, with Jarvis instrumental in the destruction. The seamer claimed two victims with the second new ball, first forcing debutant Jake Lehmann to chop on for 46, then trapping Tim Bresnan lbw. Simon Kerrigan (3-91) had earlier triggered the mini-collapse by having Adil Rashid caught at short-leg.At 283-7, Yorkshire still required 62 runs to reach their follow-on target of 345. Andrew Hodd (43) and Steve Patterson steadied the ship with a valuable 58-run stand spanning 17 overs, easing any Yorkshire anxieties.Hodd recorded his season's best score - matching Gale's achievement - before falling agonizingly close to safety. With just four runs needed, the wicketkeeper top-edged Kerrigan to Liam Livingstone, who completed a spectacular diving catch after racing from slip toward gully.Nathan Buck bowled Patterson before Kerrigan wrapped up the innings by having Ryan Sidebottom caught behind. However, Smith and Hameed then batted with composure through to the close, leaving Lancashire firmly in control.Lancashire spinner Simon Kerrigan told BBC Radio Manchester: It's a good pitch. So far, it's been a good toss to win. There's quite a few foot-holes for the left-handers, and they've got quite a few. The right-hand batters are going to have a bit of rough for when Arron bowls.It's spinning. Off the good stuff, the odd one turned. I'm confident it will start to go. It's just a case of spinning it hard and hitting the right areas when I do get a go.If the sun bakes it, it could be one of those where two sessions at them is enough. It doesn't seem like one of those slab pitches that you get at Old Trafford where it goes slower and slower.Yorkshire's Andrew Hodd told BBC Radio Leeds: The boys showed fight with the bat. We thought this might have been a game to win, but how it's looking it might be a dead one unless they come out firing.I've been really struggling. text: England conceded two late goals as Gareth Southgate's final match as interim manager ended in a 2-2 friendly draw against Spain in a Wembley friendly. Phil McNulty, BBC Sport's chief football writer, evaluates England's performance as they concluded their 2016 campaign.**Joe Hart (goalkeeper) 6** His 45-minute stint saw excellent protection from his defence. Hart faced minimal challenges.**Nathaniel Clyne (right-back) 7** A very capable performance, though perhaps insufficient to displace Kyle Walker as England's preferred right-back option.**Gary Cahill (central defence) 6** Faced relatively few problems during the opening half before his substitution.**John Stones (central defence) 6** His tendency for excessive risk-taking persists - a first-half pass created difficulties for both England and Eric Dier. Against elite opposition, he must improve his decision-making.**Danny Rose (left-back) 7** Continues developing as an international defender with another good showing.**Eric Dier (defensive midfield) 6** Provided a decent protective barrier and contributed to England's control throughout most of the match.**Jordan Henderson (central midfield) 7** Exemplary captaincy performance, highlighted by his superb cross that created Vardy's goal.**Jesse Lingard (right winger) 7** Demonstrated encouraging signs with effective running. While still developing, the promise is evident.**Raheem Sterling (left winger) 7** Outstanding during his 65-minute appearance. His pace and liveliness, combined with strong link-up play with Lingard, impressed.**Adam Lallana (forward) 7** Delivered an excellent 25-minute display before injury struck.**Jamie Vardy (striker) 8** Despite escaping punishment for an early shocking tackle on Cesar Azpilicueta, he subsequently displayed his Leicester City championship form, culminating in an excellent diving header goal.**Substitutes****Theo Walcott (for Lallana 25 minutes) 5** Sporadic moments of quality but minimal overall impact. Should have converted a chance to secure a 3-0 advantage.**Tom Heaton (for Hart 45 minutes) 6** Impressive until Spain's late resurgence. While powerless to prevent Iago Aspas's strike, Isco's equaliser disappointingly slipped through his legs at the near post.**Phil Jagielka (for Cahill 45 minutes) 6** A solid contribution - though questions remain why Burnley's Michael Keane wasn't given the 45-minute opportunity.**Andros Townsend (for Sterling 65 minutes) 5** Delivered a couple of decent crosses.**Marcus Rashford (for Vardy 67 minutes) 5** An unusually quiet outing.**Aaron Cresswell (for Rose 79 minutes) 5** Faced a challenging introduction as Spain intensified their efforts.Subscribe to the BBC Sport newsletter to get our pick of news, features and video sent to your inbox.

text: They call Lynton Crosby the Wizard of Oz - the political magician who has been hired by the Conservatives to mastermind their next election campaign. These are external links and will open in a new windowMuch like the enigmatic wizard, Crosby operates from the shadows, drawing skepticism from those who question his reputation - particularly given that his last Conservative general election campaign ended in defeat.Nevertheless, his track record includes remarkable victories in his native Australia and, more recently, orchestrating Boris Johnson's successful London mayoral re-election bid.Born 55 years ago on a South Australian farm, Lynton Crosby grew up with a father who possessed artistic and musical talents rather than agricultural instincts. The family soon relocated to nearby Kadina, where his father established an arts and crafts business.Crosby's childhood was notably content and privileged, according to all reports.Robyn Hewett, one of his two elder sisters, recalls: Mum and Dad adored him. They did anything for him. At primary school, he loved debating. He was easy-going and friendly and he just used to love putting on plays and performing in the shed to other children. And very academic, I guess you'd say.His parents' devotion knew no bounds. When Crosby gained admission to Adelaide University for economics, they relocated to the city to remain close to him. Though not particularly political themselves, they instinctively supported the Liberals - Australia's conservative movement - as most rural residents did.After working briefly in private industry, Crosby's transition into Liberal politics seemed natural, and he discovered his passion there.His candidacy skills, however, proved lacking. As he acknowledges, he transformed a competitive seat into a Labour stronghold and later confessed with hindsight, I wouldn't have voted for me.Crosby then shifted to behind-the-scenes operations, ultimately becoming campaign director for Liberal Prime Minister John Howard.Mr Howard told BBC Radio 4's Profile: I think he's a very professional political campaigner. He's just interested in making sure that the party he supports wins. As a party leader of long-time standing, I can only say that's exactly the sort of mentality you want from somebody who is your principal campaign manager.Under Crosby's management, Howard secured four straight electoral victories, though critics accused him of employing questionable methods: dog-whistle campaigns targeting voters' prejudices about crime and immigration, plus wedge issues forcing opponents to defend unpopular positions.Former Australian Senator Cheryl Kernot, who faced multiple Crosby campaigns, observes: His company's website describes him, with a certain amount of pride, I think, as a 'master of the dark arts of politics.' I remember most vividly the 10 years that he was masterminding conservative campaigns here, and the focus on refugees and asylum seekers, and the exploitation of basic instincts of fear of difference, and latent prejudice.John Howard dismisses such criticism: There's nothing grubby about Lynton. He's a tough campaigner. He's no more or less ruthless than any other effective campaigner. And this wedge nonsense [is] the bleating of people who didn't like the Liberal Party winning in Australia.Similar accusations followed Crosby to Britain during his work on Michael Howard's 2005 Conservative campaign.Daniel Finkelstein, currently a Times columnist but then working for the Tories, facilitated the introduction between Lynton Crosby and Conservative leader Michael Howard.They immediately hit it off. Both of them are very obsessive about politics... I think Michael appreciated Lynton's ability to pick issues because that's the way that Michael thinks, Finkelstein explains.While Crosby brought focus and discipline to the Conservative effort - boosting worker morale through daily prizes for top press releases - campaign slogans such as How would you feel if a bloke on early release attacked your daughter? earned the Tories their nasty party label. Conservative advertisements featured dog-whistle messaging like are you thinking what we're thinking?Yet Crosby's supporters - numerous as they are - argue that despite his brutal advertising approach, the man himself remains civilized.Daniel Finkelstein cautions: The one thing that I think would be a mistake is to think of Lynton Crosby as a sort of crude, ball-busting Australian outsider. He is not an intellectually unsophisticated, crude campaigning person at all. He's a pretty clever guy.Following the Conservatives' 2005 defeat, Crosby attributed the loss to timing constraints: You can't fatten a pig on market day. However, he left sufficient British admirers for Boris Johnson to recruit him for the 2008 London mayoral race.Given London's natural Labour leanings, electing a Conservative mayor twice required considerable political skill.Crosby demanded discipline from Johnson, insisting he adopt a more serious approach and focus on voter concerns rather than personal projects - never hesitating to speak truth to power.Boris Johnson remembers: I remember once, it was the end of a very long day, I was absolutely exhausted and I had to give a speech to a bunch of Conservative councillors - this was the 2007/2008 campaign. I was at the end of my tether - barely knew what I was talking about and I thought I'd done more or less a good job with these guys and got through it in one piece. I tottered out of the room and my phone buzzed with a text. text: The gaming industry needs to get behind a centre dedicated to videogames or risk losing it forever, Games Workshop founder Ian Livingstone has said. The National Videogame Foundation has been established by Mr Livingstone and fellow developers to support Nottingham's National Videogame Arcade (NVA), with Livingstone envisioning it as gaming's equivalent to what the National Gallery represents for art.Just twelve months after opening, the NVA teetered on the brink of closure. The co-founder of Games Workshop and key figure behind the Lara Croft franchise launch, Mr Livingstone, declared supporting the UK's sole institution of this type both his personal and the gaming industry's duty.According to Livingstone, the arcade's near-collapse paradoxically elevated its visibility. There were people [in the industry] who didn't know about it, he explained. They asked 'what is it?', 'how can we help?'Despite strong visitor satisfaction - averaging 4.5 out of 5 on Tripadvisor - various factors including funding delays left the business financially depleted. Co-director Iain Simons revealed that arcade staff accepted deferred payment to maintain operations while appealing to videogame developers for investment support. Mr Livingstone responded to this call.His involvement came as little surprise. Present at the March 2015 launch, Livingstone had emphasized gaming's ubiquity - people across all demographics engaging with games via smartphones and consoles wherever they go. He frequently highlights the industry's substantial $100bn valuation.Beyond entertainment value, Livingstone champions gaming as a genuine art form deserving recognition. He believes the NVA should transcend museum status to examine videogames' cultural impact.Education will be the National Videogame Foundation's primary focus. Livingstone characterized this as a call to action and a vital moment for videogames' cultural confidence. The foundation will manage both the annual October GameCity Festival and arcade operations.TIGA CEO Richard Wilson, representing the UK's games industry, praised the NVA as a great project where major videogame developers could assume a bigger role to play. He acknowledged, however, that smaller companies face constraints and cannot always dedicate necessary time and resources.National Videogame Arcade timeline

text: China's economy is slowing down. President Xi Jinping is acutely aware of this reality, just as we all are.This looming concern represents one of the most significant challenges - casting long shadows - over his current United States visit.Following three decades of remarkable 10% average annual expansion, China's economic momentum has dramatically decelerated. The growth rate dropped to 7.4% last year.Numerous economists harbor deep skepticism regarding China's official statistics, believing the actual figures fall considerably below reported levels. The IMF projects 6.8% growth for the coming year. This deceleration was inevitable.According to the IMF, China is undergoing a transition toward a new normal, featuring slower yet safer and more sustainable growth.This new paradigm has become necessary as the driving forces behind China's former economic dynamism continue to weaken. An aging demographic means the expanding workforce can no longer contribute as significantly to economic output.Previous robust growth has narrowed the technological divide with developed nations worldwide. Consequently, opportunities for rapid advancement through technological catch-up have diminished.Investment represents another growth engine that enhances an economy's productive capabilities. However, China's investment levels have reached extraordinarily high thresholds. IMF research indicated as early as 2012 that these levels were excessive.What makes investment excessive? It redirects resources away from other economic sectors, including consumer spending. When countries over-invest, projects increasingly become economically inefficient.Financial markets have grappled intermittently over recent weeks with a crucial question: Will this transition proceed smoothly, or will China experience a hard landing - an abrupt deceleration or potential recession?This outcome holds profound implications for the global community.By certain measures, China represents the world's largest economy, commanding 17% of worldwide economic activity.While the US economy rivals China's size, it lacks comparable growth velocity. This dynamic will likely persist for years, possibly decades, even after China stabilizes at more sustainable growth rates.China's influence on global expansion therefore exceeds that of other nations, as does its potential to drive increased demand for international goods.The distinction between hard and soft landing scenarios carries enormous significance. What should we anticipate?Economic opinions diverge - as they invariably do. Willem Buiter, Citigroup's chief economist and former Bank of England and London School of Economics figure, has articulated a particularly pessimistic assessment.We believe that there is a high and rising likelihood of a Chinese, emerging market and global recession scenario playing out, Buiter states.Defining recession sparks debate, particularly regarding emerging economies and global markets more broadly.Buiter's framework centers on economic potential. He characterizes global recession as sub-2% growth lasting at least one year, with China's threshold set at 2.5%.As a China data skeptic, Buiter believes the Chinese economy has already approached these levels more closely than official numbers indicate.For worldwide economic conditions, he estimates a 40% probability of moderate recession, with 15% odds of severe downturn accompanied by financial crisis.Should this materialize, he argues, sluggish growth across key emerging markets - particularly China - would likely drag the world into recession. We consider China to be at high and rapidly rising risk of a cyclical hard landing, Buiter warns.His reasoning? Classic warning indicators abound - industrial overcapacity, excessive borrowing and debt accumulation, plus irrational exuberance episodes in asset markets, recently affecting property and equities.This is the classical recipe for a recession in capitalist market economies, he observes.Such developments would inevitably impact numerous other nations. Several emerging economies, including major players Brazil and Russia, already face recession.China ranks among the most crucial export destinations globally - leading the list for South Korea (over 25% of exports), Saudi Arabia, and Iran.Among major economies, China serves as Japan's second-largest export market, America's fourth-largest, and Germany's second-biggest destination outside the European Union.Even nations with minimal direct Chinese trade could easily experience hard landing effects through supply chain connections or commodity price fluctuations driven by weakened Chinese demand.Consider two essential industrial commodities: crude oil and copper.Crude oil prices have plummeted over 50% since last June. Supply-side factors contribute significantly - US shale production and Saudi Arabia's reluctance to reduce output as historically practiced.However, disappointing Chinese demand growth represents another crucial element in this price decline.Copper serves as vital construction industry raw material, extensively used in electrical systems, with China's building surge creating enormous copper appetite.Copper prices have similarly halved since 2011, with China's slowdown serving as the primary factor.This presents the pessimistic perspective.Yet some analysts maintain more optimistic outlooks. London-based Capital Economics recently advised clients: In contrast to the widespread doom and gloom about China's immediate economic outlook, we think growth has already stabilised after a slowdown at the start of the year, and that there are good reasons to expect stronger growth in the months ahead.Before his US visit, President Xi informed the Wall Street Journal: The Chinese economy is still operating within the proper range.President Barack Obama, Xi's host, undoubtedly hopes this assessment proves accurate and conditions remain stable. He's certainly not alone in this sentiment.
