The Armenians call this region Artsakh, its ancient name, and the region was annexed by the Russian Empire in the nineteenth century, in which the two groups of people lived in relative peace, despite occasional bloodshed in the early twentieth century. In the early 1920s, the Soviet authorities, as part of their strategy of division and control of the region, created the Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Region. A century-old rivalry between Christian Armenians and Muslim Turkic-Persian influences lies at the bottom of this enduring conflict, with roots extending far beyond the Soviet era. This territory, which was ethnically Armenian, was included in the Soviet Socialist Republic of Azerbaijan. At the end of the eighties, as the Soviet authority was weakening, the Armenian-Azeri conflict exploded in Karabakh when its parliament voted to unite with Armenia, and this decision set off the armed clash between Azerbaijani and Armenian forces, which began in 1988 and left twenty to thirty thousand dead. Ethnic Armenians seized control of Karabakh, seized more Azerbaijani territory outside the borders of Karabakh, and thus created a buffer zone between Karabakh and Armenia. The collapse of the Soviet Union in the late autumn of 1991, the armed conflict between Karabakh and Armenia broke out, and in Karabakh itself - where the de facto status of the republic lacks international recognition - a full-fledged war broke out. In the course of the war, over one million people fled their homes: about a quarter of the pre-war Azeri population, a quarter of Armenians and Armenians fled, and neither of these groups have been able to return since the war ended. A cease-fire agreement brokered by Russia in 1994 put an end to the fighting, leaving Karabakh and large areas of the surrounding Azerbaijani territories under Armenian control. This agreement established the current de facto state controlled by ethnic Armenians. Armenia has never formally recognized the independence of Karabakh, but serves as the region's primary financial and military patron. Intermittent cease-fire violations have continued to cost lives on both sides. The Minsk Group, co-chaired by Russia, France and the United States, which has been working to resolve this conflict for years, has seen some progress in bringing the two sides together. Since December 2006, the region has witnessed a controversial vote on the draft constitution, in which the population overwhelmingly approved it, and since then, a series of meetings between the presidents of Armenia and Azerbaijan has been held, which, according to the results of the talks, have resulted in some progress, but in the end, momentum has stalled. This conflict is still classified among the post-Soviet frozen conflicts, and the negotiations have so far failed to achieve a final peace agreement. Despite decades of diplomatic efforts, this conflict continues to be intractable. Since then, serious violations of the ceasefire have taken place, and April 2016 marked the most serious escalation when dozens of soldiers were killed on both sides during renewed fighting.

text: Tortoises, Roald Dahl and the man behind Love Actually are just three of the ingredients in Esio Trot, a romantic comedy for BBC One starring Dustin Hoffman and Dame Judi Dench. The combined ages of 77-year-old Dustin Hoffman, Dame Judi Dench at 79, and Richard Curtis - a comparatively youthful 58 - total more than 214 years.However, as Dame Judi observes, age remains merely a number - particularly within a fresh TV comedy drama that deliberately demonstrates how romance can blossom during life's later chapters.Drawing from Roald Dahl's 1990 children's book, Esio Trot chronicles a solitary London bachelor captivated by the flirtatious widow residing in the apartment beneath his. Mrs Silver's tortoise obsession appears to create an impossible barrier to any romantic possibilities - until Mr Hoppy (Hoffman) devises an unconventional strategy to capture her attention.The title's backwards spelling of tortoise hints at Mr Hoppy's scheme for those unfamiliar with Dahl's 1990 masterpiece. Reading sdrawkcab becomes central to this tale, which also showcases James Corden as the neighboring guide and narrator.Curtis, creator of Four Weddings and a Funeral, Notting Hill, and the Blackadder television series, confesses being a huge fan of the author he compares to Charles Dickens. Yet adapting Esio Trot held special appeal because it enabled him to explore something about love between older people.I was writing all these films about people for whom, if it doesn't work out, they can try again, Curtis explained to reporters last November. But if you're older and lonely, the stakes are higher. I wanted to do something about people finding love who both presumed they wouldn't. I thought that would make it even more dramatic.Dame Judi's enthusiasm matched Curtis's vision. She declared wanting to play Mrs Silver unconditionally despite the character being somewhat stupid. After they said Dustin's name I would have come in to walk across the street, admits the actress, who appears next year in The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel sequel.Both films address mature characters often overlooked by an industry favoring younger demographics - a situation Dench finds unacceptable. Age is a number that's imposed on you, she states firmly. It's that thing that everyone says - 'you're as old as you feel'. It drives me absolutely spare when people say 'Are you going to retire?' or 'Don't you think it's time you put your feet up?'The Oscar winner for Shakespeare in Love, who portrayed M in seven James Bond films, continues: I don't want to be told I'm too old to do something. I want to try it first. It's not to do with age; it's to do with the engine. As long as you keep it going, you won't fall over.For Hoffman, falling presented genuine concerns during a scene where he and Dame Judi dance to Louis Armstrong's jazz. I'm not a dancer, nowhere near it, admits the veteran star of The Graduate and Tootsie. I thought after the first two lessons it wasn't going to work and I wasn't going to be ready. But it wasn't a problem because [Mr Hoppy] wasn't supposed to know how to dance. We were just naturally doing it.While praising Dench as an extraordinary talent with great energy who allows you right into her bone marrow, Hoffman feels differently about his other co-stars - the tortoise ensemble supporting Mr Hoppy's romantic mission.You've never smelled anything until you've smelled 60 tortoises, he sighs. That tortoise poo was the real thing - there was no CGI for us. I always get warm [on set] so I always want air conditioning. We brought in these big machines, but by the third day we weren't using them anymore. It was all because of the tortoises. If they get too cold, they won't act.Regarding off-camera socializing during London filming earlier this year, Hoffman explains: Judi wanted to socialise, but I was always too tired. I don't socialise when I'm working. I don't socialise when I'm not working. Other than that, I love people!BBC One broadcasts Esio Trot on January 1st at 1830 GMT.

text: Pupils at a County Antrim school have developed a new tool to target cyberbullying. Ballyclare High School has launched 'Step Up', a pioneering digital reporting platform that school officials believe represents the first system of its kind across Northern Ireland. The innovative tool enables students to access support whether they're at home, within school premises, or using their smartphones.Through the school's website, pupils can now communicate concerns directly to appropriate teaching staff. When students click a designated button, they're directed to an online form where they specify their year group and select which staff member should handle their situation.Emma Blacoe, a 14-year-old who contributed to the system's development, explained how comprehensive the reporting capabilities are. Pupils can upload files and pictures of screenshots and chats if they feel someone's in danger, she said. They can also simply just say if they're being pressured or bullied or if anyone else is.The platform prioritizes privacy and choice - information submitted remains visible only to the student and teaching staff, with pupils having the option to identify themselves or maintain anonymity.David Andrew, another student involved in creating 'Step Up', emphasized the system's user-friendly design and accessibility. If pupils really feel there's something which needs to be sorted out they can do it, he said. Bullying is never acceptable and the sooner someone steps up, the sooner it can be sorted out.According to Mhairi Hill, the school's head of cyber safety, staff commitment to investigating every allegation remains absolute. Staff will pick it up and the earliest opportunity and follow the procedure already in place for dealing with incidents, she said.Hill highlighted how digital evidence strengthens their response capabilities. With online bullying, pupils can come to us with screenshots and that's concrete evidence we can use to take the investigation forward.The school maintains rigorous standards for following up reports. We would establish the facts before proceeding but we would follow up every report, Hill explained. If a child has felt it's necessary to raise the concern then it's worth following up in our eyes.She emphasized the educational impact of addressing these issues promptly. We have a duty of care for our pupils and if a pupil's upset or distressed in class they're not going to learn to their full potential so it's important that we address these issues.

text: Colombia's President Juan Manuel Santos has met 30 rebels of the ELN, the country's second largest armed group, who laid down their arms. A significant milestone toward peace emerged when 30 members of Colombia's National Liberation Army (ELN) laid down their weapons in the southeastern Cauca region, marking what President Santos described as a great step towards peace.The surrender represents the largest single ELN contingent to abandon armed struggle, according to Mr Santos, who personally welcomed the rebels in Cali. Among those who surrendered their arms and equipment were three pregnant women.This is what the [peace] process is about. So every member of the ELN and the Farc follows their path fighting for their ideals, but without violence and without arms, he said during the ceremony.While the ELN remains excluded from ongoing peace negotiations between the government and Colombia's largest rebel group, the Farc, the left-wing organization's leadership has shown interest in participating. Officials estimate the ELN maintains approximately 1,500 members, but the government maintains its position that hostage releases must precede any inclusion in talks.The group continues to hold captives, though it recently freed a Colombian soldier.Meanwhile, momentum builds in the Cuban-hosted peace talks launched in November last year between the government and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc). Ivan Marquez, the Farc's chief peace negotiator, declared Monday that the nearly five-decade armed conflict was approaching its conclusion.Speaking to Colombian network RCN, Marquez urged left-wing parties and unions to support the peace effort while cautioning against hasty agreements. It is possible [to reach an agreement by November]. But to achieve peace you need time. A bad peace deal is worse than war, he said.The government aims to finalize a peace accord by November, representing the fourth attempt at negotiated settlement since the conflict began in the 1960s. Chief government negotiator Humberto de la Calle emphasized that the Cuban talks seek to transition rebels from armed struggle into legitimate political participation.Progress has been achieved on land reform, though five additional agenda items require resolution. Marquez recently proposed convening a Constitutional Assembly to ratify agreements reached in Cuba.In an apparent effort to draw the ELN into negotiations, the Farc issued a statement last month discussing potential unification with their rival rebels.The Farc's fighting force has diminished significantly, from approximately 16,000 members in 2001 to an estimated 8,000 today. However, the government insists that all rebel groups must disarm and release hostages before joining the political process.

text: Nottingham Forest have made an approach to Burton Albion to speak with former player Nigel Clough in relation to their managerial vacancy. The 50-year-old Clough accumulated over 300 appearances for the Reds across two separate stints, with his initial period occurring under the management of his father Brian.Currently in his second tenure leading Burton, Clough returned to the Brewers in December 2015 and successfully steered them to Championship promotion last season.On 14 January, Forest dismissed their former manager Philippe Montanier.In the Championship standings, Burton sits three positions below Forest, who occupy 19th place and maintain a five-point cushion above the relegation zone.When BBC Radio Nottingham reached out to Forest for comment, the club declined to respond. Similarly, Burton remained silent when BBC Radio Derby sought their reaction.During his latest press conference, Clough addressed the mounting speculation connecting him to a potential Forest move following Montanier's exit from the City Ground.It's an easy link and a logical one from lots of points of view, Clough told BBC Radio Derby on Wednesday.All these sort of allegiances you have and everything, yeah they're strong, but in football people go to rivals all the time.It's very difficult when you spent 18 years - I'm just over 50 years old - so a third of my life involved with a certain club [Nottingham Forest].Since retiring as a player, Clough has never taken the managerial reins at Forest, despite his deep connections to the club.His standing among supporters suffered only during his managerial periods with traditional rivals Derby County and Sheffield United.Nevertheless, when he returned with Burton for August's EFL season opener, which Forest claimed 4-3, he received a warm welcome.While Clough spent much of his Forest career as the manager's son under Brian, his own contributions ensured no dressing room tension or supporter criticism would arise.His 131 goals trail only Grenville Morris in the club's scoring records, and he belonged to the late 1980s generation that made Wembley nearly an annual spring destination.In the 1989 League Cup final victory over Luton - the club's first silverware in almost ten years - he netted twice, while his vision and technical ability perfectly complemented strikers like Lee Chapman, Nigel Jemson and Teddy Sheringham, earning him England recognition.Following his father's departure after the dismal 1992-93 campaign that concluded with top-division relegation, Nigel left to join Liverpool after nine years of service. He later returned on loan during 1996-97 in an unsuccessful short-term attempt to preserve Forest's top-flight status.

text: ScottishPower customers will soon be able to buy gas and electricity in bundles of days rather than signing up to standard or fixed-price deals. ScottishPower is revolutionizing energy purchasing with a groundbreaking PowerUp scheme that mirrors how consumers fuel their cars or purchase mobile data packages. This innovative approach aims to demystify energy bills for customers who struggle with traditional billing methods.Chief executive Keith Anderson explained the company's philosophy: We're saying to people buy it by the day, not by kilowatts or a fancy tariff you don't understand. The initiative emerged after executives returned to fundamental principles, examining consumer behavior at petrol stations.You go to the garage and put £50 in your car. Inherently you know that will last you two to three weeks, Mr Anderson observed. We thought why don't we do the same thing with energy.The system operates through a specialized app featuring a consumption gauge that monitors energy usage in real-time. Each customer receives a personalized daily energy allocation based on their typical consumption patterns, with adjustments made for seasonal variations throughout the year.Customers can purchase gas and electricity packages ranging from single days to full months, with the flexibility to buy up to 180 days in advance. The app's fuel gauge functionality keeps users informed about their remaining energy reserves and current consumption levels.A significant advantage of PowerUp is the elimination of standing charges, while ScottishPower promises some of its most competitive pricing within the scheme's tariffs. Initially launching for existing customers, the company will evaluate expanding access to the broader market based on pilot program results.The energy sector has long struggled with consumer engagement issues. A comprehensive two-year competition authority investigation revealed that many consumers remain disconnected from the energy market, frequently failing to switch to more economical deals.Industry regulator Ofgem has endorsed this innovative approach. Their statement emphasized: We want more competition to increase choice and drive down prices for consumers. We encourage suppliers to offer new innovative tariffs to help people engage in the market and find the best deal which suits them. Innovative tariffs can be tailored to an individual consumer's needs and give people more control over their energy bill and how they pay for it.Claire Osborne, energy expert for Uswitch.com, praised the initiative's potential impact: Energy bills are notoriously difficult to understand and so this approach, similar to how we buy petrol, should help consumers use less, waste less and pay less for their gas and electricity. The fact that the deal has no standing charge will be attractive to many customers - particularly those with second homes which are unoccupied for part of the year - as there's nothing to pay on days when no energy is used.Following successful pilot testing, ScottishPower believes this model could fundamentally transform energy purchasing patterns across the industry.

text: The Dalai Lama has called on his fellow Nobel Peace Laureate, Aung San Suu Kyi, to do more to help persecuted Rohingya Muslims in her country, Myanmar. I met her two times, first in London and then the Czech RepublÂ­ic. text: Thousands of Yemenis have taken to the streets of the capital, Sanaa, to protest after an air strike killed more than 140 people at a wake on Saturday. Outside the United Nations headquarters, protesters assembled to demand an international probe into the deadly strike attributed to the Saudi-led coalition. While Saudi Arabia has not admitted involvement, the kingdom has committed to launching its own investigation.The Saudi coalition entered Yemen's ongoing civil conflict in support of the internationally recognized government. In response to Saturday's devastating attack, influential former Yemeni leader Ali Abdullah Saleh—now aligned with the Houthi rebels controlling Sanaa—has urged citizens to launch retaliatory strikes against Saudi border forces.Saturday's bombing left over 500 people injured after targeting a funeral gathering for the father of Houthi-designated Interior Minister Gawal al-Rawishan. The ceremony drew numerous Houthi officials, with Minister al-Rawishan suffering severe injuries in the assault. One rescue worker characterized the scene's aftermath as a lake of blood.International condemnation has poured in from the United Nations, European Union, and United States. UN Secretary-General Ban Ki-moon declared that any deliberate attack against civilians is utterly unacceptable while demanding accountability for those responsible.The Saudi-led coalition has promised to immediately investigate this case along with the Joint Incidents Assessment Team in Yemen and experts from the United States who participated in previous investigations. Their statement referenced reports about the regrettable and painful bombing in Sanaa, emphasizing that the coalition confirms that its troops have clear instructions not to target populated areas and to avoid civilians.Washington announced an immediate review of its already-diminished coalition support. White House National Security Council spokesman Ned Price emphasized that US cooperation with Saudi Arabia was not a blank cheque.Houthi leader Abdul-Malek al-Houthi countered in a televised statement that the strike occurred with a green light from Washington using American weaponry. The rebels' spokesman branded the attack an act of genocide.Yemen faces a catastrophic humanitarian crisis, with four-fifths of its 28-million population requiring aid, according to UN humanitarian officials. Since fighting erupted in 2014, nearly three million people have been forced from their homes.The Houthis seized the capital that year, compelling President Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi's government into exile. The Saudi-led coalition has conducted thousands of airstrikes targeting the Zaidi Shia rebels, whom it suspects serve as Iranian proxies.A recent UN assessment calculated that 3,799 civilians have perished since the Saudi-led aerial campaign commenced in March of last year, with coalition strikes accounting for 60% of civilian fatalities during a twelve-month period.

text: The Pope's plea to tackle climate change is likely to get a cool reception from some key energy politicians in the US. As Pope Francis prepares to address Congress on Thursday regarding climate change, telling a White House audience Wednesday that the problem could no longer be left to a future generation, a prominent Republican lawmaker maintains her skeptical stance on the issue.Marsha Blackburn, holding the second-highest position on the House energy committee, continues to question the scientific consensus on global warming. In comments made earlier this year for an upcoming Radio 4 documentary series Climate Change - Are we Feeling Lucky?, the Tennessee representative declared that the jury is still out saying man is the cause for global warming, after the earth started to cool 13 years ago.Blackburn's assertions go beyond questioning human causation. She claimed the planet has experienced a 1-degree Fahrenheit cooling over the past 13 years and stated flatly that no evidence would convince her of man-made warming. When confronted with data showing Earth's surface temperature had remained relatively stable rather than cooled during that period, she doubled down: I think we've cooled almost 1 degree (F).These claims directly contradict findings from major scientific institutions, including NASA, which document continued planetary warming evidenced by melting ice, rising sea levels, and warming oceans.The congresswoman, representing a state heavily dependent on coal, refused to identify the sources informing her climate skepticism. We have met with different researchers, she explained. We had had numerous committee meetings in which we've had individuals come to present and from all of that and what we have been able to read you come to an opinion.Her position extends to broader scientific theories. There are some that feel like human activity is the cause for carbon emissions and because of that we need to revert to where we were in the 1870s for carbon emissions. I just choose to disagree with that, Blackburn said.When pressed about what scientific evidence might change her mind on climate threats, her response was unequivocal: I don't think you will see me being persuaded. She also rejected evolutionary theory when asked directly: No, I do not.These views carry significant political weight as Congressional Republicans work to dismantle President Obama's greenhouse gas reduction initiatives.Leading climate scientist Professor Brian Hoskins of the Royal Society called Blackburn's statements absolutely staggering and complete nonsense. He emphasized: It is nonsense to say the world has cooled. If no evidence will persuade Ms Blackburn of climate change, that shows how well-founded her views are.Correction 25 September 2015: An earlier version of this report implied that Marsha Blackburn's comments were made in relation to the Pope's address. They were actually given in an earlier interview and the headline and text have been amended to make this clear.Follow Roger on Twitter @rharrabin

text: BBC Ouch wants your funny, confusing or embarrassing stories about those awkward situations which occurred because you're disabled or have mental health difficulties. **Tales of the Misunderstoned: Share Your Story This Summer**This summer brings another chance to relive extraordinary moments through Tales of the Misunderstood - our live storytelling celebration.Perhaps you once crafted a clever tale about losing your leg to a shark attack, only to watch it spectacularly backfire when your boss believed every word and shared it at a major conference.Consider that evening when a waiter automatically handed you the children's menu simply because you're a person with restricted growth.Think about those moments when friends and colleagues carefully avoid words like mad or crazy in your presence, knowing you see a therapist.Your actual story will undoubtedly prove far more captivating than these examples - and we're eager to discover it.Whatever narrative you bring, we welcome it. Our only requirements: the story must be authentic, you must be disabled or experience mental health challenges, and your tale should weave this reality throughout.Selected storytellers will collaborate with a premier comedy script producer before taking the stage at Edinburgh Fringe Festival this August.Ready to take the plunge?Draft your story and submit it - deadline 9 July - alongside personal details about yourself.A summary works initially, though previous successful applicants typically sent complete stories in their opening submissions.Contact us at ouch@bbc.co.uk or through Facebook direct messages.Should you possess an exceptional story but require accessibility support to share it, we'll collaborate to enhance and communicate your narrative effectively.Your final piece should run approximately seven minutes. Whether delivered as comedic stand-up or as compelling insight into unexplored territory, both approaches work brilliantly.Beyond performing for our welcoming audience, we'll film your presentation for BBC broadcast.This marks our second storytelling event - the inaugural show took place in March 2017.Browse two performances from our London debut, where many participants stepped onto a stage for their very first time.The 9 July deadline approaches quickly.Compelling submissions will receive follow-up contact detailing next steps.UK-based participants can access travel funding, while accommodation awaits those traveling significant distances.All accessibility requirements will receive our full attention. text: Two people have been killed and two others injured in a stabbing in a house in Canterbury. Kent Police detained a suspect at a Dickens Avenue residence shortly after 19:30 BST Tuesday, following a violent incident that left two people dead and two others hospitalized with serious injuries.The arrested individual, believed to have been acquainted with the victims, was taken into custody at the scene where two people had sustained fatal wounds.Rab Hendry, a local resident, described rushing to assist one of the wounded—a man in his twenties who had been stabbed in the abdomen. I saw two lads, I believe they were brothers, and the oldest one said his brother's been stabbed in the stomach, Hendry recounted to the BBC.I got him to the ground and saw the wound was opened right up. I put tea towels on him and put pressure on it until [paramedics] came.The neighbor explained how the boy was panicking and appeared white as a sheet, prompting Hendry to maintain conversation in an effort to keep the victim calm.Jamie, another local resident who declined to provide his surname, witnessed the aftermath inside the property. He reported seeing a woman collapsed in the doorway and what appeared to be a man's body deeper within the house. Despite police officers performing CPR in attempts at resuscitation, Jamie understood both individuals had perished.The violent incident has left the typically peaceful neighborhood reeling. Charlotte Bunn, 83, whose home sits directly across from the crime scene, expressed her disbelief at such violence occurring in their quiet area.I only knew the people who lived there to say hello to when out in the garden or walking in the street. They seem all right. I can't find any fault, Ms Bunn stated, noting that residents at the property typically stayed one or two years then move on.It's a quiet area. All the time I have lived here I have only had trouble once, she added.One unnamed neighbor speculated that local authorities may have placed individuals at the residence.Law enforcement established a perimeter around the property, summoning serious crime officers to investigate. Forensic specialists arrived at the Dickens Avenue location, erecting a forensic tent outside the front entrance as part of their examination.According to Kent Police, efforts to notify victims' next of kin are underway, though formal identification procedures remain incomplete. A police spokesman confirmed that detectives are working to establish the circumstances surrounding the deadly incident.

text: Welsh exiles Taulupe Faletau, George North, Jamie Roberts and Rhys Priestland will have to rely on being picked as wildcards for future Wales selection. Wales head coach Warren Gatland faces significant selection constraints as the Welsh Rugby Union's senior player selection policy restricts him to choosing just three overseas-based players for international duty.The policy, dubbed 'Gatland's Law', has created a seven-man list of eligible overseas players, marking the first time the WRU has publicly disclosed these names since the rule's implementation for the 2016-17 season. From this group, only three wildcard selections are permitted per campaign.Dominic Day, Nicky Thomas, and Rhodri Williams join the affected players, while Bath's Luke Charteris remains exempt and available for selection under the policy's grandfather clause.The selection restrictions operate across separate campaigns - Six Nations, summer tours, and autumn internationals - with different wildcard choices possible for each period. Robert Howley will oversee team selection as he deputises for Gatland, who is preparing for his role leading the 2017 British and Irish Lions tour to New Zealand.Wales' autumn international schedule features matches against Australia, Argentina, Japan, and South Africa at Cardiff's Principality Stadium throughout November. The squad announcement is scheduled for Tuesday, 18 October.The policy emerged from a landmark £60m, six-year agreement signed in August 2014 between the WRU and Wales' four professional regions, resolving prolonged disputes over the sport's direction. This deal established rules prioritizing home-based talent over overseas players, though exceptions remain possible.Players who secured overseas contracts before the policy's introduction remain unaffected, including Toulon's Leigh Halfpenny and Exeter's Tomas Francis.WRU chief executive Martyn Phillips acknowledged the challenging position facing players and supporters. Players have been aware that there would come a point, if they left or signed new contracts outside Wales, that the policy would impact on selection, Phillips explained.We are aware that supporters may be concerned that we will not be selecting from a full list of players, but the alternative where players increasingly play outside Wales isn't sustainable for the long-term success of our game whether that be professional or community rugby, he added.Phillips emphasized the strategic nature of the policy while recognizing player autonomy: Clearly the player ultimately has the choice but we will do all we can to ensure that playing in Wales gives the player the best professional rugby experience possible.The policy aims to strengthen domestic rugby by encouraging Wales' top talent to remain within the country's professional regions rather than seeking opportunities abroad.

text: Mark Percival scored 14 points for St Helens as they won a fiery derby against Wigan Warriors and secured a fifth straight Super League victory. St Helens delivered a masterful defensive display to defeat Wigan Warriors and secure fourth place heading into the Super 8s phase, while the hosts remained in second position.The visitors established early control when Percival converted an opening penalty, though Lewis Tierney's try briefly leveled proceedings for Wigan. However, further scores from Percival and Morgan Knowles extended Saints' advantage to 16-4 by the interval.Luke Walsh's crucial drop-goal and a late James Roby try sealed the triumph for Keiron Cunningham's men despite challenging, waterlogged conditions at the DW Stadium.The defeat proved costly for Wigan, who squandered an opportunity to match points with league leaders Hull FC after the Black and Whites secured victory over Salford. Warriors now face consecutive losses heading into next week's Challenge Cup semi-final clash with Hull FC, having seen their impressive nine-game winning streak ended by Leeds the previous Friday.St Helens' defensive resilience shone throughout, epitomized by Joe Greenwood's goal-line heroics to deny Sam Tomkins in the second period. The match featured disciplinary issues when New Zealand prop Frank-Paul Nuuausala received a sin-bin punishment on his home debut for striking Louie McCarthy-Scarsbrook, who also saw yellow.John Bateman marked his return to Wigan's lineup following an eight-week suspension and £10,000 fine for an alleged altercation with another player.Warriors coach Shaun Wane expressed his disappointment: I'm gutted, devastated. We didn't turn up and got what we deserved. The smartest team won. They were good on the floor and were allowed to be good. Our defence was very good for large parts of the game but our attack was off. Too many individual players had a poor game. We've got seven hard days of work ahead of us now. We need to make sure we turn up against Hull with the same commitment to defence but we've got to be better on attack.Saints boss Keiron Cunningham praised his squad's resilience: I'm just pleased for my players, they stood up to everything Wigan threw at us - they could probably still be playing now and not score. That's what self-belief brings to a side. We went through a tough spell but we're a real close-knit group and now we're heading in the right direction. Wigan are a great attacking side and were fully stacked tonight. They had lots of threats but I thought we stuck to the plan. We're not going to fall in love with ourselves, we give ourselves a good shot for the top four.Wigan Warriors: S Tomkins; Tierney, Gildart, Sarginson, Manfredi; Williams, Smith; Sutton, Powell, Flower, Bateman, Isa, O'Loughlin. text: Golfing legend Jack Nicklaus joined those hailing Rory McIlroy after the 22-year-old re-wrote the record books in winning the US Open by eight shots. The golfing world's most celebrated figures have united in praise for the sport's brightest emerging talent, with legendary voices offering extraordinary acclaim.Jack Nicklaus, nearly five months senior to McIlroy when claiming his inaugural major championship in 1962, delivered a striking assessment: He's ahead - and his score is way ahead of my pace. I think this kid's going to have a great career - I don't think there's any question about it.Fellow Northern Irishman Graeme McDowell elevated the comparison further: He's potentially the next Tiger Woods.The tributes from golf's elite paint a picture of unprecedented potential realized at Congressional.It was obviously an unbelievable performance. I thought he played just fantastic golf. It is so great to see a nice young man play well, to do well, came one assessment of the dominant display.The analysis continued with particular emphasis on McIlroy's mental fortitude: We are all aware that he has been there before, but he showed that he learned from his mistakes, and he showed that he knew how to play the last two days with a big lead. Not only did Rory know how to play with a big lead, he played it confidently, played it smartly, and he never put himself in position to be in trouble.Character evaluation proved equally impressive: He's humble when he needs to be humble and confident when he needs to be confident. I like his moxie - he's cocksure and I like that. You've got to have that.Past disappointments were acknowledged but contextualized: He obviously had a couple of disappointments at the Masters and last year's Open [McIlroy started 63-80 at St Andrews and finished with an 80 at Augusta], but I didn't think that was going to happen again and it hasn't.Early recognition of exceptional talent emerged in recollections: I first heard about him when he shot that 61 at my home course in Portrush. You hear rumours about people and good players come and go, but this kid was something a bit special.The fulfillment of long-anticipated promise drew particular attention: It's great to see him out there fulfilling his potential. He's been like an accident waiting to happen. He's been groomed to be a superstar and he'll handle it very well. It's not a monkey off his back, it's a gorilla. He could go on and do some big things.Technical prowess earned specific recognition: He's probably the best driver of the ball I've ever seen. We nicknamed him the 'BMW' because he is the 'ultimate driving machine'.Superlative assessments flowed freely: Nothing this kid does ever surprises me. He's the best player I've ever seen. I didn't have a chance to play with Tiger when he was in his real pomp, but this guy is the best I've ever seen, simple as that.The broader impact on golf received emphasis: He's great for golf. He's a breath of fresh air for the game and perhaps we're ready for golf's next superstar and maybe Rory is it.Historical perspective emerged in discussions of major championship potential: If you are going to talk about someone challenging Jack's record there's your man. Winning majors at 22 with his talent - he would have 20 more years, so probably 100 more majors in him where he could be competitive. It would give him a great chance. Rory has proved in playing the majors so far that he is comfortable making the scores.Recognition of emerging talent crystallized: You can tell that Rory has had this type of talent in him for some time now, and to see him putting it together is pretty neat to see.Talent assessment reached extraordinary heights: As I've said before, I think he has probably the most talent I've ever seen from a golfer. It's lovely to watch him play, he has such a fluid motion and he hits it far.Development and consistency drew professional analysis: Rory has always had the potential to play at this level. He's done a lot of work this year on his body. We look at the swing a bit more often now to make sure the good swings are in place more often. He's developing a level of consistency now that we haven't seen before.Comparisons to golf's greatest dominated discussions: The way he's playing out there, it's almost Tiger-esque. To have the lead that he has in the US Open is pretty ridiculous and at such a young age. Obviously the next generation is starting to kick up now and he's the guy that's leading it.Comprehensive skill evaluation emerged: He's got a lot of talent and he's only 22. He's got the world in front of him really. His game looks flawless. His swing looks great. I think it looks just as good as when Tiger was in his prime and swinging at it at his best. You just don't see any flaws.Historical context shaped the praise: I think fundamentally he's as good as we've seen ever in my era, take Tiger Woods out of it. When Tiger was going well, that's as good as I've ever seen. I think Rory is in that same boat. His swing is mechanically sound, and he's got a great short game and he putts it well, and he's long. So he's got all the tools. So it's pretty impressive.Humorous acknowledgment of superior ability surfaced: Rory has more talent in his pinky than I have in my whole body.Maturity beyond years drew attention: He's about 27 in golf years. He's very polished on experience. I don't think we've seen a rookie come out with his composure and be ready to play on our Tour right away like he is.Final assessments captured the extraordinary nature of the performance: What he's been doing is really something unbelievable. He's probably got one of the nicest swings in the world, if not the nicest. It's been fantastic to watch what he's been doing in this tournament. In my opinion, right now he's playing at a different level to the rest. So for sure he is an inspiration. I admire him a lot.

text: Hospital visits for alcohol poisoning have doubled in six years, with the highest rate among females aged 15 to 19, a report has found. England's emergency departments are witnessing a dramatic surge in alcohol-related visits, with A&E attendances likely linked to alcohol poisoning climbing by over 50% across nine years to reach 250,000 annually, according to new Nuffield Trust research.The crisis hits hardest in deprived communities and northern regions, with men aged 45-64 bearing the heaviest burden. Emergency hospital admissions for alcohol-related conditions including liver disease have similarly escalated by more than 50% during the same period.However, these stark figures represent merely the tip of the iceberg, the Nuffield Trust cautioned. Their calculations exclude alcohol-fueled violence and accidents, focusing solely on direct medical consequences like alcohol poisoning and liver disease. Additionally, intoxicated individuals who arrive at A&E but leave without treatment or admission aren't captured in these statistics.Weekend patterns reveal the concentrated nature of this crisis. Half of all A&E visits likely stemming from alcohol poisoning - occurring when someone consumes toxic alcohol levels typically within short timeframes - happen between Friday and Sunday, with peak hours falling between midnight and 2am.The strain on emergency services intensifies as three-quarters of these patients arrive via ambulance, further stretching already pressured resources, researchers noted.Gender and age disparities paint a complex picture. Young women aged 15-19 require hospital admission for alcohol poisoning 1.4 times more frequently than their male counterparts. Meanwhile, socioeconomic factors create stark divides: A&E attendance rates and emergency admissions linked to alcohol prove three to four times higher among the population's poorest fifth.Geographic patterns show elevated hospital admission rates concentrated in northern England and urban centers. When examining broader alcohol-related hospital admissions encompassing conditions like liver disease, middle-aged men between 45-64 constitute the largest demographic group.Alcohol poisoning occurs when someone consumes toxic alcohol quantities, typically within brief periods, creating life-threatening situations requiring immediate medical intervention.Joint report author Claire Currie emphasized the timing significance: With the Christmas party season in full swing, it's worth considering the full burden over-indulgence in alcohol is placing on our NHS, as well as the obvious human cost.She continued: Our research has uncovered a picture of rising and avoidable activity in hospitals, representing a stark challenge for the Health Service at a time when it's already great pressure. Hospitals alone cannot tackle this issue - the government must consider measures such as minimum unit pricing, restricting availability and limiting marketing and advertising.Historical data reveals concerning trends. In 2013, approximately 18% of English men and 13% of women consumed alcohol at levels considered harmful. By 2013/14, roughly one in twenty emergency admissions related to alcohol consumption.Contrasting patterns emerge across Britain's nations. Scotland has experienced declining alcohol admissions recently, while Wales shows stabilizing trends. Office for National Statistics data suggests young adult binge-drinking continues falling, with over one-fifth of UK adults now abstaining completely from alcohol.Jackie Ballard from Alcohol Concern highlighted particular concerns regarding middle-aged and older demographics exceeding recommended limits, frequently within domestic settings.These are the people who tend to require the most complex and expensive health care due to the mental and physical problems caused by drinking too much and alcohol's impact on the ageing body, Ballard explained.She added: Alcohol is linked to over 60 medical conditions and unless society and the government starts to take this seriously and acknowledges the health problems too much alcohol can cause, the situation will only get worse and the NHS will continue to strain under the burden of alcohol harm.Government response acknowledged the pressures facing emergency services. A spokesman stated: People should always drink alcohol responsibly - very busy ambulance services and A&E staff can do without this extra demand.The official continued: The government has taken action to tackle cheap alcohol by banning the lowest priced drinks and we are already seeing fewer young people drinking on a regular basis.

Home to the public university's football team, its 20,000 capacity better suits MLS requirements. text: A former chaplain and an ex-principal of a Roman Catholic care home have been found guilty of abusing boys. Two former staff members from a defunct East Yorkshire children's home have been convicted of multiple sexual offences spanning two decades, following an extensive 10-week trial at Leeds Crown Court.James Carragher, 75, who served as head of St William's Children's Home, and Anthony McCallen, 65, the facility's former chaplain, faced a combined total of 87 charges relating to sexual abuse of minors between the 1970s and 1990s. Both men had entered not guilty pleas to all accusations.The court proceedings revealed disturbing patterns of abuse targeting vulnerable boys aged 10 to 16. Evidence presented to the jury included testimony from 18 adult men who described being indecently touched during their time at the institution.Particularly troubling details emerged about late-night swimming sessions orchestrated by Carragher, a previously convicted sex offender from Merseyside. Witnesses testified that boys were taken swimming after lights-out at the home and instructed not to wear any swimming trunks. The emotional toll of these revelations became evident when one victim abruptly left the courtroom after recounting how both defendants had visited him while he slept and sexually assaulted him.Carragher's criminal history includes previous convictions for sexual offences, resulting in a seven-year prison sentence in 1993 and a 14-year term in 2004. For this case, he faced 50 counts of indecent assault plus 12 additional serious sex offences. McCallen, also from Merseyside and previously convicted of abusing two boys in the 1990s, was charged with 18 indecent assaults and seven other serious sexual offences.After 11 days of deliberations, the jury delivered partial verdicts. Carragher was found guilty on 24 charges - 21 counts of indecent assault and three serious sex offences - while being cleared of 30 additional charges. McCallen received guilty verdicts on 11 charges, including one serious sexual offence, though he was acquitted of eight other allegations.However, the jury remained deadlocked on 13 charges and was subsequently discharged by Judge Jeffrey Marson QC, who commended their handling of the complex case.I've never ever in many years of doing this had a jury who had to consider so many charges, it is way beyond the norm, and they are some of the most difficult charges to deal with, Judge Marson stated, praising the jurors' conduct throughout the proceedings.Both defendants are scheduled for sentencing on January 4.St William's Children's Home, located in Market Weighton, operated under the ownership of the Diocese of Middlesbrough and management of the De La Salle Brotherhood until its closure in 1992.The Diocese of Middlesbrough issued a statement expressing hope that those affected by the abuse can move on with their lives. The statement continued: We condemn any behaviour which harms young people. The behaviour of Anthony McCallen whilst he was a priest was a betrayal of the trust that was placed in him from the Diocese of Middlesbrough.

text: Shares in the UK's biggest estate agent, Countrywide, have plummeted following the publication of its gloomy report on the property market. Countrywide's shares plummeted 12% on Thursday, adding to the 5% decline triggered by the government's announcement to eliminate letting agents' fees.The property giant, which operates 55 high street brands including Bairstow Eves, John D Wood and Gascoigne Pees, delivered a sobering third quarter trading update. Revenue dropped to £188.5m from £197.1m in the corresponding period last year, while the company warned that stamp duty modifications and Brexit uncertainty would continue dampening transaction volumes.Market activity has proven particularly challenging, with Countrywide projecting a 6% decline in transactions for 2016 and anticipating further deterioration throughout 2017. The company acknowledged that reduced transaction levels during the year's second half would push 2016 profits toward the lower end of expectations.Regional disparities emerged starkly in the September quarter data. While overall house exchanges fell just 1% compared to the previous year, London experienced a dramatic 29% contraction. Mortgage approvals similarly weakened, declining 12% year-on-year.The lettings division faced unique pressures from first-quarter stamp duty changes, which triggered an unusual surge in rental property supply as investors rushed to complete purchases before the deadline. Despite these headwinds, residential lettings grew 14% in the September quarter, with London posting a modest 1% increase.Wednesday's Autumn Statement delivered what industry observers called a hammer blow to estate agents through the proposed ban on letting agents' fees. Starting this September, Monmouth Comprehensive will introduce a new uniform policy requiring parents to purchase items exclusively from Trutex, a designated supplier, sparking outrage among families over the mandatory £20 trousers and £16 skirts.The policy directly contradicts Welsh Government uniform guidance, which recommends that governing bodies consider stipulating basic items and colours but not styles so that items can be bought from retail chains at reasonable prices and not just from one supplier.Despite this conflict, Monmouthshire council defended the school's decision, stating that consultation occurred with the whole school community over a lengthy period following government guidelines.Deputy head Andy Williams warned parents in a letter that sending students home (in line with Welsh Government guidance) is, of course, our last resort, though hundreds of concerned parents have flooded the community Facebook page with complaints.Paula Beddis Simpson, expressing her frustration, wrote: I am a single parent doing 2/3 jobs to make ends meet, it's totally unfair. As long as they are proper grey school trousers and pupils look smart, what is the problem?Alex Watkins echoed similar sentiments, adding: It's not as if people are refusing to adhere to the uniform, just would like to choose where to buy trousers skirts and shirts. It's hardly unreasonable.The comprehensive overhaul replaces the current polo shirt and jumper combination with branded blazers and ties for year seven and sixth form students, citing that the existing uniform had become tired, inconsistent and not fit for purpose. Other year groups may transition voluntarily or when replacement becomes necessary.According to the school's calculations, the complete uniform costs £97 for boys and £93 for girls, though parents estimate expenses exceeding £100 when forced to use the exclusive supplier.The school, preparing to relocate to a new £33 million building in 2018, acknowledged there has been some concern over the cost of trousers and skirts from our suppliers.Williams defended the supplier restriction, explaining: We trialled the use of barcodes for parents to buy cheaper (but often less ethically sourced) items from high street retailers. But quickly found that codes and styles changed, allowing many students to create a very different style of uniform including tight, skinny jean type trousers and inappropriate skirts. The school simply cannot keep pace with brand and style changes that will add to inconsistency in a school with over 1500 students.Council officer Will McLean clarified that the design of school uniforms and the rules which apply to them are determined by school governing bodies.As a concession, pupils eligible for free school meals will receive complimentary uniform items during their first year.

text: Head teachers in England are keeping up the pressure on school funding, sending a letter warning about cash-starved schools to almost two million families. School leaders spanning 17 councils are demanding immediate government intervention to address critical funding shortfalls as the Queen's Speech approaches, outlining the administration's legislative agenda.Education financing disputes dominated election campaigns, emerging as a pivotal concern for voters at their doorsteps. While Conservative pledges included an additional £1bn annually through identified savings, significant uncertainty clouds the largest portion of this promised increase.The primary question mark hangs over the government's commitment to eliminating universal free school meals for infant pupils—a policy introduced three years prior. Without a parliamentary majority, pushing through legislation to axe these meals would prove considerably more challenging. Celebrity chef and school nutrition advocate Jamie Oliver has vocally opposed this proposed removal.More than 4,000 schools will receive warning correspondence from headteachers alerting parents to impending staff reductions and diminished subject offerings. Pre-election forecasts suggested some institutions might slash operating hours or implement four-day weeks for certain students.School governors have endorsed these funding concerns, with West Sussex witnessing an unprecedented gubernatorial strike—the first of its kind.The correspondence will reach families across these local authorities: Brighton, East Sussex, Northamptonshire, Surrey, Cambridgeshire, Essex, Oxfordshire, Thurrock, Cornwall, Hertfordshire, Peterborough, Wokingham, Devon, Norfolk, Suffolk, West Sussex and Dorset.Parents will learn about Institute for Fiscal Studies research indicating Conservative education spending proposals would result in real-terms cut of 2.8% in per-pupil funding between 2016 and 2022. These headteachers represent a regional coalition campaigning against educational funding deficits.Teachers' unions are simultaneously pressing for enhanced school investment. National Union of Teachers general secretary Kevin Courtney stated: The general election has forced the government to accept that there is a major problem with school funding that must be addressed. This matter cannot wait - unless the government acts now, class sizes will be higher and fewer subjects will be taught in September.Beyond overall school budget discussions, the government must determine whether to advance new allocation formulas for individual institutions. Officials have promised fairer distribution methods for school budgets while defending their funding protection record.A Department for Education spokeswoman emphasized: The core schools budget has been protected in real terms since 2010 and is set to rise from £41bn in 2017-18 to over £42bn in 2019-20 with increasing pupil numbers. But we recognise that schools are facing cost pressures and will continue to provide support to help them use their funding in cost-effective ways.

text: The flagship Conservative election pledge to open a further 500 free schools in England is being put into practice, with applications invited for new schools. Education Secretary Nicky Morgan has launched the next phase of free school expansion, targeting 270,000 additional places across the coming five-year period. She characterized these institutions as modern engines of social justice.The application window opened Friday, signaling the commencement of another substantial wave of free school development. Among anticipated submissions are New Croydon Academy, emphasizing science and technology education, and Gipsy Hill Secondary Academy, where multiple south London primary schools collaborate to establish secondary provision.Currently, over 250 free schools operate nationwide, with more than 150 additional institutions receiving approval. These state-funded establishments mirror academies in their operational independence, functioning beyond local authority control while enjoying enhanced curriculum and staffing flexibility.Prime Minister David Cameron championed these educational startups during campaign season, asserting they were raising standards and restoring discipline. The coalition government initially introduced the program to expand choice and foster innovation, enabling local parents and community organizations to establish schools when existing provision proved inadequate.However, professional educational groups increasingly dominate the sector. Policy Exchange research revealed that established academies or academy chains opened over two-thirds of recent free schools, while parent and community groups launched fewer than one-fifth.Opposition has emerged from Labour and teaching unions, who contend the free-school initiative fails to address placement shortages in critical areas. The Department for Education counters that nearly three-quarters of 125,000 created free school places emerged in shortage zones, with half are in the most deprived communities in the country.Free schools are at the heart of the government's commitment to deliver real social justice by ensuring all pupils have access to a world-class education, Mrs Morgan declared. This is at the core of our commitment to govern as one nation - creating a country where everyone, regardless of their background, can achieve their high aspirations.The education secretary emphasized that free schools offered a fresh chance for families to break the cycle of disadvantage by providing a quality of schooling never before seen in many communities.Sarah Pearson, interim director of the New Schools Network supporting free school establishment, reported collaboration with approximately 30 prospective groups. These organizations had been putting in the hours in the last few months to finalise their applications, she noted.Expected applications include various specialized institutions. Sir Craig Tunstall, executive head teacher of the federation spearheading the Gipsy Hill proposal, aims to address academic decline among bright primary students transitioning to secondary education.In our area there is a shortage of outstanding secondary places and too often the first year is spent treading water academically because teachers and pupils are taking time getting to know each from scratch, he explained.Shadow education secretary Tristram Hunt criticized the initiative as irresponsible public fund usage. When there is a shortage of school places, rising class sizes, widespread teacher shortages and schools face significant real-terms budget cuts, parents will find it odd that David Cameron continues to plough hundreds of millions of pounds into building new schools in areas where there is already a surplus of places, Hunt argued.National Union of Teachers leader Christine Blower dismissed effectiveness claims: As the government knows, free schools and academies do not raise standards in any more effective way than maintained schools. She characterized the program as far more about privatisation and ideology than social justice and equality.NASUWT union leader Chris Keates advocated for traditional oversight: Local authorities should be left to manage place provision and to determine the type of school provision that would best meet the needs of local communities.
dipper: The flagship Conservative election pledge to open a further 500 free schools in England is being put into practice, with applications invited for new schools. The application window opened on Friday, starting a major wave of free school development. Among the anticipated applications is New Croydon Academy, a specialist science and technology school, and Gipsy Hill Secondary Academy, a secondary school which aims to unite several South London primary schools in its secondary provision. Secretary of State for Education, Nicky Morgan, has launched a further wave of free schools, aiming to increase their number by 270,000 places over the next five years. She described them as modern engines of social justice. These establishments, backed by the state, mirror academies in their operational independence, establishing themselves outside the local government control while having full curriculum and staffing freedom. The programme was originally introduced to increase choice and to foster innovation, enabling parents and local groups to establish schools where existing provision was inadequate. But professional educational groups have come to dominate the sector; research by the Policy Exchange has shown that established academies or academy chains have launched more than two-thirds of new free schools, while parents and local groups have launched only one-fifth. Opposition has been voiced by the Labour Party and by the teaching unions, who claim that the free schools fail to resolve the problem of shortages in key areas. The Secretary of State for Education replied that nearly three-quarters of the 125,000 places created were in disadvantaged areas, and that more than half were in the most deprived communities. She said that the new schools represented a fresh opportunity for families to break the chain of disadvantage, by offering a quality of education not seen in many communities. The interim director of the New Schools Network, which supports the establishment of free schools, reported that it had been working with about thirty groups of prospective parents, who had been working hard in recent months to complete their applications. Sir Craig Tunstall, executive head of the federation spearheading the Gipsy Hill plan, said the idea was to address the academic decline of bright children when they move on from primary to secondary education. There are too many children in our area who have not been given an outstanding secondary education and too often the first year is spent treading water, because teachers and pupils have to get to know each other, he explained. The shadow education secretary, Tristram Hunt, said the project was an irresponsible use of public funds. “With the increasing class sizes, the widespread shortage of teachers, the real-term cuts in school budgets, it will seem strange to parents that the prime minister continues to pour hundreds of millions of pounds into building new schools in areas where there are already surplus places,” he said. The National Union of Women Teachers leader, Christine Blower, dismissed any claim to effectiveness: “The government knows very well that free schools and academies do not raise standards any more effectively than maintained schools. It is more a matter of ideology and a private company’s interests than of social justice and equality. Local authorities should be left to manage place provision and to decide on the type of school that would best serve local communities.”

text: Wrexham's appointment of Dean Keates as manager is not the first time the Welsh club have turned to a familiar face to lead them. Dean Keates has stepped into his inaugural managerial position, taking the reins from Gary Mills after accumulating more than 150 league appearances and leading Wrexham to FA Trophy glory in 2013 as captain.The north Wales outfit has a tradition of promoting former players to management, with Arfon Griffiths, Brian Flynn, and most recently Andy Morrell all receiving their maiden opportunities at the helm. Each manager left a distinctive legacy at a club now enduring its eighth consecutive season outside the Football League.Since Morrell's tenure - during which Keates served as club captain - Wrexham has failed to generate a credible play-off campaign. Currently managing National League North side Tamworth, Morrell was among the first to congratulate Keates on his appointment.He's perfect for it, Morrell told BBC Radio Wales Sport. He's somebody who is ambitious, enthusiastic and has got Wrexham at heart. He fought tooth and nail when he was a player for them and put his body on the line and he'll do exactly the same thing in the manager's job as well. It's a great opportunity for him because these don't come along very often.Both Morrell and Keates began their managerial careers on interim terms - Morrell assuming control in September 2011 following Dean Saunders' departure to Doncaster Rovers before securing permanent status. The circumstances differ significantly, however: Morrell inherited a Conference-leading squad, while Keates faces the challenge of lifting Wrexham from 14th position, eight points adrift of play-off contention.I was in a better position because we had won seven out of the 10 games, Morrell recalls. All I had to do was carry on doing what we were doing and the lads were great. Dean has got to somehow change the mind-set of the players. They've got to change that mentality into one that's a winning one and he can do it. He'll lead from the front and he'll tell them exactly what he wants.Keates' appointment has sparked comparisons with another diminutive midfielder-turned-manager, Brian Flynn. Standing 5ft 5ins, Keates quipped during his press conference: I'm a bit taller than Flynnie though.The former Wales international Flynn transitioned from player to manager in November 1989, replacing Dixie McNeil. Under his 12-year stewardship, he revolutionized a team that had finished bottom of the Football League into FA Cup giant-killers, orchestrating memorable victories over Arsenal and West Ham United.Peter Jones, chair of Wrexham Supporters' Trust, drew parallels between the appointments: It's a very similar situation to when Brian Flynn came in and look at the success he had at the football club. We felt the opportunity for Dean was the right time. He knows the club, he knows everyone here.Flynn's reputation for nurturing young talent at Wrexham resonates with Morrell, who emphasizes the importance of homegrown development for the club's future prosperity and stability.I hope they can get a plan in place not just to try and make the play-offs this season or next season, Morrell told BBC Wales. You've got assets there that you can sell whereas at the moment they seem to be ignoring that. If they can get those players through then that gets the fans on board. If there's a plan in place there's no reason why in a few years' time you can't be pushing again. There's so many big teams that are struggling to get back to where they should be and Wrexham are a Football League club in mine and a lot of people's eyes. Keatsy will be positive and he'll push them on and make them play well.

text: The growing buy-to-let property market in the UK could post a threat to wider financial stability, a Bank of England committee has said. The Bank of England's Financial Stability Committee (FPC) has determined that buy-to-let mortgage lending could potentially amplify housing market volatility during both booms and busts.Since 2008, this sector has experienced a dramatic 40% surge in lending, according to the FPC's findings. text: Rakesh Shukla is a software engineer who's found his life's calling in looking after dogs that no-one wants, writes the BBC's Geeta Pandey in Bangalore. Dogs erupted in a joyful chorus of barks and yelps as the vehicle stopped outside a weathered farmhouse near Karnataka's capital in southern India. Within moments, Rakesh Shukla found himself surrounded by the pack, their bodies pressing against him as they nuzzled and licked with unbridled enthusiasm.The reunion clearly delighted Mr Shukla as much as his four-legged companions. He conversed with them, offered gentle pats to some, scratched behind ears, and hoisted one onto his shoulder before guiding me through his three-and-a-half-acre sanctuary. I had worked in Delhi, in the United States and then set up my own company in Bangalore, he recalled. Life was all about buying big cars and expensive watches and living a fancy life. text: It's that time of year again where we put the clocks forward and all get one hour less in bed! On Sunday, March 26, at 1am, the clocks will spring forward - likely while most people remain sound asleep in their beds.This temporal shift marks Britain's transition from Greenwich Mean Time (GMT) to British Summer Time (BST), alternatively known as Daylight Saving Time (DST) or GMT+1. The practice reached a significant milestone last year, celebrating its centennial anniversary since first being implemented in the UK.Sunday morning's adjustment will extend daylight into the evening hours throughout the summer period. After learning about the origins of this practice, test your knowledge with our quiz below.The concept originated with Benjamin Franklin, an American politician and inventor, who proposed the idea in 1784 while residing in Paris. Franklin reasoned that rising earlier during natural daylight hours would reduce candle consumption.However, the practice reached British shores through William Willett, a builder who happened to be Coldplay singer Chris Martin's great-great-grandfather. Willett championed the concept after becoming frustrated when his beloved golf games were curtailed by early sunset.In 1907, Willett published The Waste of Daylight, a leaflet urging people to rise earlier. His passion for golf drove his advocacy - he resented having matches cut short due to insufficient light as darkness fell.Parliamentary discussions about clock adjustments began in 1908, but widespread public opposition prevented legislation. Despite Willett's lifelong campaign to promote the idea, Britain only adopted the system in 1916 - tragically, one year after his death.Germany actually implemented the practice first during World War One, shortly before Britain followed suit. During World War Two, Britain experimented with British Double Summer Time (BDST), advancing clocks an additional hour during summer months, though this arrangement proved short-lived.Currently, British clocks fall back one hour on October's final Sunday and advance one hour on March's last Sunday. While numerous countries worldwide have adopted similar systems, many nations continue operating without seasonal time changes.Public opinion remains divided on the merits of clock adjustments. Supporters argue BST conserves energy through improved natural light utilization and reduces traffic accidents.Critics contend the practice fails to achieve energy savings while creating morning darkness that endangers schoolchildren. They also cite potential health concerns associated with the time changes.Test your understanding of these facts with our quiz!

text: Archaeologists and officials have expressed outrage about the bulldozing of the ancient Assyrian city of Nimrud by Islamic State militants in Iraq. Iraqi officials confirmed Thursday that IS militants launched their destructive assault on Nimrud, the ancient site established in the 13th Century BC. The UN's cultural agency chief denounced this systematic devastation across Iraq, labeling it a war crime.The extremist group, which maintains control over vast territories in Iraq and Syria, justifies its actions by declaring shrines and statues to be false idols requiring destruction.They are erasing our history, declared Iraqi archaeologist Lamia al-Gailani.Located along the Tigris river approximately 30km (18 miles) southeast of IS-controlled Mosul, Nimrud has yielded countless artifacts. While many treasures have been relocated to Baghdad museums and international collections, numerous pieces remained at the original site.BBC Middle East correspondent Jim Muir notes that this destruction attempt draws immediate comparisons to the Taliban's 2001 demolition of Afghanistan's Bamiyan Buddha rock sculptures.Beyond destroying artifacts, Islamic State profits from antiquities trafficking - a crucial revenue stream for the organization.The tourism and antiquities ministry reported Thursday that IS assaulted the historic city of Nimrud and bulldozed it with heavy vehicles. Officials accused the militants of continuing to defy the will of the world and the feelings of humanity, demanding a UN Security Council session to address Iraq's cultural heritage protection.Given Nimrud's extensive area, complete destruction remains unclear, our correspondent reports. However, a local tribal source informed Reuters: Islamic State members came to the Nimrud archaeological city and looted the valuables in it and then they proceeded to level the site to the ground. There used to be statues and walls as well as a castle that Islamic State has destroyed completely.Unesco chief Irina Bokova condemned the assault, stating: This is yet another attack against the Iraqi people, reminding us that nothing is safe from the cultural cleansing under way in the country. The deliberate destruction of cultural heritage constitutes a war crime. There is absolutely no political or religious justification for the destruction of humanity's cultural heritage.Dr Gailani explained to the BBC: Nimrud for us in Iraq and for me as an archaeologist is one of the most important [sites]. There are still quite a lot of things that are standing - the reliefs and the statues, the famous winged bulls. They are erasing our history. I wish it was a nightmare and I could wake up.British Institute for the Study of Iraq president John Curtis called it a horrific crime against the cultural heritage of the whole world, describing Nimrud as the best preserved Assyrian site in Iraq.The previous week saw IS release footage apparently depicting militants wielding sledgehammers against historic artifacts in a Mosul museum. The video showed one militant drilling through and dismantling what appeared to be a stone winged bull. Militants described these artifacts as false idols, providing religious justification for their destruction. The UN also condemned that attack as a war crime.Since June 2014, IS has maintained control over Mosul - Iraq's second-largest city - and surrounding areas, a region containing nearly 1,800 of the country's 12,000 registered archaeological sites.Iraqi forces and Shia militia have joined efforts to expel IS militants from Tikrit in the north, receiving Iranian support. A US-led coalition continues targeting the militants through air strikes.Friday reports indicated Iraqi forces successfully cleared IS fighters from al-Baghdadi town in western Anbar province, supported by US-led strikes. The town, captured by IS last month, sits approximately 8km (5 miles) from an air base housing hundreds of US troops training Iraqi soldiers.

text: Political sketch writer Quentin Letts has apologised for an article he wrote mocking the disability of broadcaster Andrew Marr. Following a Guardian article by media commentator Roy Greenslade, Letts issued a Twitter apology for his remarks about Marr. The stroke survivor had been described as Captain-Hop-Along, growling away on BBC One, throwing his arm about like a tipsy conductor in Letts' Daily Mail review of Robert Peston's new ITV show.Marr suffered a stroke in January 2013.Greenslade's Guardian piece, titled It isn't Funny or Smart for Quentin Letts to Poke Fun at Andrew Marr, condemned the remarks. I don't want to come off all namby-pamby, Greenslade wrote. I understand that no-one should be beyond criticism and that Letts was exercising his right to press freedom. But really Quentin, that was a graceless remark.The media commentator subsequently demanded an apology from Letts.Acknowledging his comments about the admirable Marr were horrid, Letts faced fierce backlash on social media. Users responding to his apology tweet branded him utterly disgraceful and appalling.Both the print and online editions of the Daily Mail carried the controversial article.Jackie Ashley, Marr's journalist wife, criticized Letts' piece on Twitter, highlighting the harmful message it conveyed to disabled individuals.The Stroke Association issued a strong statement: A stroke is not a joke. Stroke survivors deserve our respect and support, and Andrew Marr deserves an apology. The organization urged people to file complaints with the Independent Press Standards Organisation.An IPSO spokesperson told the BBC: we have received a total of 11 complaints about the article. All of the complaints are under Clause 12 (Discrimination), with one or two also citing Clause 1 (Accuracy) or Clause 4 (Intrusion into grief or shock). It is IPSO policy not to comment on the identity of individual complainants, so I am unable to confirm the names of anyone who has contacted us on this article.Meanwhile, Robert Peston's debut ITV Sunday politics talk show garnered tepid reviews after its weekend premiere. Letts had characterized Peston's programme as breathless and batty - and bound to be a hit.
