The general secretary of CND, Kate Hudson, deplored the apparent sidelining of this debate. Corbyn, meanwhile, increased his shadow cabinet to 68 members, adding seven new faces, including Paula Sherriff (women and equalities), Richard Burden (transport), Wayne David (defence), Khalid Mahmood (foreign office), Rupa Huq (home office), Lyn Brown (home office) and Gill Furniss (business). The reshuffle that followed the election had made the Social Democrats very angry. “At a time when the party’s delegates have voted against relaunching Trident in the last two elections and the party leader has been twice elected on the basis of a strong opposition to Trident,” she said, “the CND calls on party members to insist on the defence policy review being published and a democratic debate on Trident at the next party conference.”

text: China's Communist Party and its more than two-million-man army aren't supposed to like video games. The Communist Party and its military forces have fully embraced an industry they once desperately tried to suppress. Today's gaming sector generates over 50 billion Chinese RMB ($7.9bn; £5.2bn) annually, marking a dramatic reversal from the official 2000 ban on home-video consoles.That prohibition, implemented amid fears of corrupting Chinese youth, represented a futile attempt at King Canute communism—trying to stem capitalism's rising tide and block Western cultural infiltration. The harsh rhetoric about electronic heroin ultimately succumbed to overwhelming consumer demand, while consoles persisted through grey markets and gaming migrated online.China's latest propaganda weapon comes disguised as entertainment: Glorious Mission, a military-designed video game that has attracted over one million downloads since its public debut months ago. Though resembling a typical violent shooter, this title serves as the state's newest tool for ideological influence.Originally created as a training simulator for Chinese soldiers, the game features state television footage of military ranks enthusiastically controlling virtual People's Liberation Army forces across battlefield scenarios. The virtual adversaries occasionally bear striking similarities to the US and its allies, prompting speculation about the real-world conflicts being simulated.Army sources reveal that releasing the game publicly aims to instill patriotic values—the military's core values—among civilians. Gu Kai, vice-president at developer Giant Network Technology, believes the game will boost army recruitment.Most young boys, from the bottom of their hearts, want to be a soldier. They like to fight, they like to win, and if this video game can make that dream come true, I won't be surprised, he says. I would hope that somebody will play the game and fulfil their dream.The propaganda elements appear deliberately unsubtle. News reports describe one stage recreating the fiery atmosphere of camp life.At a Shanghai internet cafe, nearly all 100 terminals buzz with players engaged in intense online battles against goblins, aliens, and human enemies. One patron, who spends over 10 hours weekly gaming there, acknowledges video games' potential for ideological manipulation.It's possible, he says. Most of the players here are young. A military video game could make you feel familiar with and then develop an affinity for the army.Glorious Mission represents both a military about-face and evidence that China extends beyond internet censorship—routinely banning search terms and deleting posts—to actively weaponizing digital platforms. The country already deploys Communist Party bloggers to post pro-government commentary online.The gaming industry's apparent rehabilitation provides the latest arsenal addition. State media reports suggest authorities may soon officially abandon their moral objections entirely, with the console ban potentially facing review.Gu Kai believes China has definitively moved past its gaming concerns. I've met some of the officials, he says. They stopped worrying about video games years ago. Most of them are promoting gaming as a new, hopeful and fast growing industry. At least here in Shanghai all the officials are very open and supportive.While China isn't pioneering military gaming—Glorious Mission resembles a US military training and recruitment tool created a decade earlier—attempting to shape public consciousness and cultivate nationalist loyalty represents a more ambitious campaign. In China's virtual battleground, this ideological warfare will likely escalate.

text: Christian Eriksen scored twice as Tottenham proved far too strong for spirited Hull City at White Hart Lane. Tottenham Spurs strengthened their hold on fifth position in the Premier League table after securing their eighth victory of the campaign, with Denmark midfielder Christian Eriksen netting twice in a commanding performance against Hull City.The match opened with Danny Rose providing the perfect assist for Eriksen's opener within the first quarter-hour, capitalizing on excellent build-up play along the left flank. Kyle Walker mirrored this contribution from the opposite wing after the interval, effectively ending any realistic prospect of a Hull revival.Eriksen came agonizingly close to completing his hat-trick when Hull goalkeeper David Marshall brilliantly tipped his exceptional free-kick onto the woodwork, leaving Victor Wanyama to convert the simple rebound from close range.While Hull cannot dispute the final outcome, the comprehensive scoreline perhaps didn't fully reflect their efforts, as the Tigers matched their opponents for significant periods of the contest. Nevertheless, their defensive frailties remain glaring - conceding 35 goals across 16 fixtures represents a damning indictment for the league's second-bottom club. Their away form continues to deteriorate, with this sixth consecutive defeat on the road equalling their top-flight record.Spurs controlled both possession and scoring opportunities throughout, registering 27 attempts on goal, though clear-cut chances remained relatively scarce. The wing-back pairing of Rose and Walker proved consistently threatening, providing the primary source of Spurs' attacking threat.Rose's 14th-minute sprint down the touchline to collect Jan Vertonghen's long pass set up the opening goal. After advancing and cutting inside his marker, he found Eriksen, who powered the ball high into the net.Spurs' tactical setup featured Eric Dier alongside Vertonghen and Toby Alderweireld in a three-man defensive structure, granting their wing-backs increased freedom to venture forward. The second goal followed a similar pattern, with Dier's ball over the top finding Walker, who advanced into the penalty area before delivering a low cross that Eriksen tucked away at the far post - his fifth goal in four Premier League appearances.Rose's involvement continued when he won the free-kick that led to Spurs' third goal, capping an outstanding individual display from the England international.Despite the significant disparity in league standing and resources between the teams, Hull delivered a performance that temporarily matched their hosts' intensity. The visitors managed 10 shots against a top-five opponent away from home - something they've struggled to achieve against weaker opposition at their own ground this season. With improved composure, they might have drawn level at 1-1.Jake Livermore impressed against his former employers and nearly restored parity during Hull's sustained pressure following the opening goal. Hugo Lloris produced an excellent save to deny his initial attempt.Hull's second significant opportunity emerged as Spurs supporters began expressing frustration with their team's inability to dominate the visitors early in the second half. Following referee Andre Marriner's rejection of several Spurs penalty appeals - including one after Andrew Robertson bundled over Eriksen - Hull launched a dangerous counter-attack.The move concluded with Livermore receiving possession on the right side of the area, but his initial effort was blocked and his follow-up cleared by Lloris's left boot. Three minutes later, Eriksen's second goal effectively sealed Hull's fate.Spurs manager Mauricio Pochettino reflected: I think it was a game we dominated. I think the most important is the three points, to be close to the top four. In some parts the team play well, which is hard against a team playing for survival.Regarding Eriksen's performance, Pochettino added: He was very close to a hat-trick. It was a very good performance for him - he played very very well.On Eric Dier's future amid transfer speculation, the manager stated: I know there are a lot of rumours, but he's 100% our player. He's very important for us. He signed a contract after the Euros and showed his commitment to the club. There's no doubt his future is at White Hart Lane.Hull manager Mike Phelan remained philosophical despite the defeat: We came here with a fabulous attitude. They've come here and played the ball, controlled it, restricted their attempts, but at a certain time in the game we were more than value for money. I thought they did very well but we're on the end of a 3-0 defeat - but we have to stay positive.Phelan emphasized the importance of upcoming fixtures: Every game is key, it's all on the next game and we can only look forward. I'm staying positive for these players and hopefully we can add to the group in January. If we can keep creating opportunities and doing the right things, I'm hoping we can turn positive performance into results. We're looking at improving the group. We definitely need to be adding that extra to give the club and supporters and players a lift.Tottenham return to White Hart Lane on Sunday at 16:00 GMT to face Burnley, while Hull travel to West Ham on Saturday (15:00 GMT) for another London fixture.Match ends, Tottenham Hotspur 3, Hull City 0. text: The Football League season is poised for another dramatic climax as six teams aim to be promoted by winning their respective play-off finals at Wembley. The Championship play-off final on Saturday between Hull City and Sheffield Wednesday carries an estimated £170m prize for the victors.Sunday will see Barnsley face Millwall in the League One final, while AFC Wimbledon and Plymouth Argyle complete the 2015-16 season with Monday's League Two showdown.**Saturday 28 May, 17:00 BST**Steve Bruce brings extensive promotion experience to Hull's cause, having guided Birmingham City to Premier League elevation in both 2002 and 2007, before achieving the same feat with the Tigers in 2013.Yet Saturday marks Bruce's maiden Wembley appearance for a play-off final - the culmination of a turbulent journey for his squad. Their campaign suffered from persistent inconsistency, and they nearly threw away a commanding 3-0 first-leg advantage against Derby County in their semi-final.You can just detect there's a big game around the corner, Bruce told BBC Radio Humberside. The players are tackling each other and champing at the bit. You just have to put them on a little bit of a leash at times because we need to let them go on Saturday.Hull's last Wembley visit came in 2014's FA Cup final defeat to Arsenal. text: Sharks have patrolled the oceans for at least 400 million years and evolved into a huge range of remarkable species. The ocean teems with extraordinary sharks: deep-sea lantern species that illuminate the darkness, wobbegong sharks sporting shaggy beards, and magnificent whale sharks—the sea's largest fish—gracefully filtering plankton through their massive mouths.Yet despite this diversity, one image dominates public perception: shark attacks.For beachgoers, divers, and surfers, the reality proves far different from popular fears. Encounters with sharks remain extraordinarily rare, while fatal attacks are even less likely. Lightning strikes, bee stings, and automobile accidents present significantly greater dangers than these marine predators.The statistics tell a stark story: humans kill millions more sharks annually than sharks kill humans.According to the International Union for the Conservation of Nature (IUCN), a recent report reveals that one-quarter of all shark and ray species face extinction threats. Overfishing represents their primary danger, with the largest species facing the gravest peril.Despite this conservation crisis, Western Australia recently implemented a controversial shark cull following multiple attacks in the region.Scientists are now exploring alternative approaches to address human-shark conflicts.At the University of Western Australia (UWA), Prof Shaun Collin leads a team of neurobiologists attempting to understand shark psychology. We're trying to tread this very fine line of protecting both humans and sharks at the same time, Prof Collin told the BBC World Service programme Discovery.Through research into shark brains and sensory systems, the team develops and tests non-lethal deterrents. Their goal involves manipulating sharks' sophisticated senses to discourage approaches and attacks on humans.Among their innovations is a shark-proof wetsuit designed to mimic poisonous black-and-white banded sea snakes—creatures many sharks instinctively avoid.Marine biologist Walter Starck originally conceived the striped wetsuit concept years ago. Now, detailed shark vision research helps the UWA team modernize this approach.Nathan Hart, UWA assistant professor, explained that shark eyesight falls short of human visual capabilities. We've made sure that the size of the bands can be detected by a shark from a certain distance, he says.Current testing involves wrapping the fabric around barrels filled with dead fish, then observing wild shark responses.While still in early stages, Nathan reports encouraging preliminary results. Based on what we know about the sensory systems of sharks, they should reduce your risk to some extent, he says. Just like a seatbelt in a car, it doesn't reduce your risk to zero; it's a matter of reducing your risk by a certain amount and by as much as possible, he adds.Beyond individual swimmer protection, researchers explore methods to exclude sharks from specific areas. We can try and define areas on the beaches where people are confident they can go and swim, says Dr Hart.Bubble curtains offer one potential solution for protecting popular beaches. The concept involves laying perforated hosepipes across the seafloor, pumping air through them to create bubble plumes that sharks might avoid crossing.Sharks can detect bubbles through sight, sound, and their lateral line system—sense organs common to many fish species. It's a system of what's known as 'distant touch'; it detects vibrations and very low-frequency sound in the water, Nathan explained.Early experiments revealed that tiger sharks eventually overcome their hesitation to cross bubble barriers, demonstrating their learning capacity.Eugenie Clark, a veteran marine biologist at Florida's Mote Marine Laboratory, pioneered shark learning studies during the 1950s. Known as The Shark Lady, Dr Clark trained captive sharks to press targets with their snouts and ring bells for food rewards, proving for the first time that sharks possess learning and memory abilities.Eugenie recalled transporting a trained baby nurse shark as a gift for Japan's Crown Prince, who shared her fish fascination. The airline gave me an extra seat for the shark. Most people didn't know, he was such a tiny thing he was less than two feet long. But he never made a mistake, says Eugenie.Recently, I witnessed shark learning capabilities firsthand, particularly their ability to learn non-aggressive behavior toward humans.During a diving expedition off Fiji's Pacific waters, I encountered my first bull sharks—notorious for their aggressive reputation. Local operators from Beqa Adventure Divers have trained approximately 100 bull sharks to approach divers individually and gently accept hand-fed fish chunks.These sharks have learned proper behavior for receiving food rewards. They know us very well, Fijian divemaster Papa told me before the dive. That's the good thing, they know what's going on.Initially uncertain about my reaction to these massive predators, my anxiety disappeared underwater as I observed the bull sharks' grace and calm demeanor. Without safety cages or repellents, I never felt threatened.Beyond improving sharks' reputation as mindless killers, these Fijian divers demonstrate that living sharks provide far greater value than dead ones.Throughout Fiji and globally, sharks face intense pressure from Asian demand for shark fin soup.Meanwhile, Western Australia's shark cull continues despite beachside protests. The region experienced an abnormal spike in attacks—seven fatalities over three years compared to 20 throughout the previous century.The Western Australian government responded by deploying baited hooks offshore from popular beaches. Any captured great white, tiger, or bull sharks exceeding three meters are shot and dumped at sea.Shark attack survivor Rodney Fox opposes the cull. Fifty years after suffering a horrific great white attack in South Australia, he has become a dedicated shark advocate. We just have to learn how to live with the sharks and not just kill them from fear, he told me.Fox considers deliberate shark killing an unscientific, irrational strategy for reducing attack rates.However, Western Australia's government maintains the cull protects swimmers and surfers. Premier Colin Barnett stated: The West Australian government is absolutely confident that the policy in place is the right policy and we intend to continue it.More than 100 scientists signed an open letter urging Mr Barnett to reconsider, emphasizing the cull's environmental impact and the slim probability of catching sharks responsible for specific attacks. Every scientist that I've heard of and talked to all agree that it's not the thing to do, says Mr Fox.

text: Poland's Prime Minister Beata Szydlo has vowed to press on with judicial reforms, saying the government would not yield to pressure from the street and from abroad. Thousands of protesters flooding Polish streets achieved a significant victory Monday when President Andrzej Duda vetoed controversial legislation that would have allowed government appointees to replace Supreme Court judges.The decision followed widespread demonstrations across Poland and mounting pressure from European leaders. European Commission officials had threatened sanctions this week unless the judicial changes were abandoned, while European Council President Donald Tusk, Poland's former prime minister, warned of a black scenario that could ultimately lead to the marginalisation of Poland in Europe.Despite the presidential veto, Prime Minister Beata Szydlo delivered a defiant televised response, declaring her Law and Justice (PiS) government would press forward with judicial reforms.We all want to live in a fair Poland, this is why the reform of the courts is needed... Today's veto by the president has slowed down work on the reform, Szydlo stated. We cannot yield to pressure from the streets and abroad... We have a stable majority. We won't give in to pressure. We will realise our plan.President Duda's announcement surprised many observers, given his former membership in the right-wing ruling party championing the legislation. In his televised statement, he explained his reasoning after consulting with legal experts and judges.As president I don't feel this law would strengthen a sense of justice, Duda declared. These laws must be amended.The president rejected two proposed laws while approving a third measure granting the justice minister authority to appoint lower court heads. His decision came after weekend discussions with advisers, including Zofia Romaszewska, a veteran communist-era dissident who endured imprisonment during martial law in the early 1980s.Romaszewska had warned Duda against returning to times when the general prosecutor could do virtually anything. She told Polish media that allowing the attorney-general to control the Supreme Court was completely out of the question.Demonstrations erupted in dozens of cities including Warsaw, Krakow, Gdansk, Poznan, and Lublin, with opposition lawmakers crediting protesters for influencing the presidential decision. Calls for continued protests have emerged, though the movement now focuses on pressuring Duda to veto the remaining approved reform.The president acknowledged Poland's judicial system requires modernization, noting its reputation for sluggish proceedings. I'm absolutely a supporter of this reform, but a wise reform, Duda emphasized, while warning against changes that might separate state institutions from society.International alarm has grown over the three reforms, which grant sweeping powers to the justice minister and parliamentarians. Both U.S. and EU officials have expressed concerns about the legislation's implications.Last week, Duda had attempted compromise by modifying government plans for the National Judiciary Council, requiring additional political party support for nominees. However, he expressed regret that Supreme Court reform drafts weren't provided before the lower house Sejm vote.The president particularly objected to expanding the justice minister's role, noting this official simultaneously serves as Poland's attorney general.Parliamentary options remain for challenging Duda's veto. While Law and Justice holds a simple Sejm majority, overriding presidential decisions requires three-fifths support. Though theoretically possible with backing from smaller party Kukiz'15, such cooperation appears uncertain.More likely, the government will spend coming weeks redrafting the rejected bills to secure presidential approval. The PiS government has consistently denied accusations that reforms represent authoritarian drift, expressing disappointment with Duda's decision.Much depends on Jaroslaw Kaczynski, the PiS co-founder widely regarded as the government's true power broker, as Poland navigates this constitutional standoff between executive branches.

text: Returning to Cold Feet after more than a decade since it was last seen on TV felt like putting on an old jumper, Fay Ripley has said. Eight fresh episodes of the beloved comedy drama will air this autumn, marking the return of Cold Feet after more than a decade since its conclusion in 2003 following five successful series.The revival comes at an opportune moment, according to co-star John Thomson, who believes there's currently a great need for nostalgia. He explained that the timing couldn't be better to bring back something so feel-good as Cold Feet, noting that the world isn't in a great place at the moment, and there's a great need for nostalgia, to look back at the days when things seemed okay.The original series finale drew over 10 million viewers who witnessed the funeral of Rachel, the central character portrayed by Helen Baxendale. Now, the new installment will explore how the intervening years have shaped the lives of couples Jenny and Pete, Karen and David, plus widower Adam as they navigate middle age and parenthood of teenagers.For lead actress Ripley, returning to Jenny felt remarkably natural. She was delighted to revive the role, describing the experience as bumping into an old friend. Despite initial concerns about getting back into character, she found that within a minute, it was the same. The reunion proved seamless thanks to the cast's established chemistry. It was like stepping back in time. We've got a shorthand when we work together, all of us, which is incredibly handy, Ripley explained.This familiarity eliminated formalities on set, as Ripley humorously noted: You can just go in and say, 'I've got a banging headache, my menopause is giving me gip'.Hermione Norris initially harbored reservations about reprising Karen's role. It's that thing in life - you think 'Don't go back, just move forward', she reflected. It was so of its time and it was so loved, I thought maybe it should be left as I didn't want to do anything that would have undone that.However, creator Mike Bullen convinced her this wasn't a remake but rather revisiting these characters in this chapter of their life. The new series demonstrates technological evolution, with Karen now using dating app Tinder, illustrating how dating has transformed.Norris deliberately avoided rewatching previous episodes before filming commenced. It was amazing how much I'd forgotten - I couldn't remember how many children David and I had, she admitted.The absence of Baxendale proved emotionally challenging for Norris. I missed Helen hugely - because Rachel was Karen's best friend. I really felt her absence. It's like it would be in real life, if you've lost a really good friend, she said. However, Ripley confirmed there would be no shower moment for Rachel - referencing the infamous Dallas scene where Bobby Ewing's death was revealed as a dream. She assured fans that Baxendale was happy with the show continuing, adding: She's cool with it.The experience of working with age-appropriate colleagues resonated strongly with Norris, who found it comforting to see familiar characters reunited. I really appreciate being with my own generation. As an actor, and as Karen. I find as a woman, I love being older. The weight of experience - you just don't have that as a 30-year-old, she observed.Robert Bathurst's return as David hinged entirely on script quality. It's all very much down to the script. I wouldn't have done it for the sake of it, he stated. He attributes the show's enduring appeal to its focus on ordinariness, explaining: It's about people and how they rub along together. Bathurst hopes the new series will stand alone while attracting fresh audiences.The cast welcomes BBC Radio 1 presenter Cel Spellman, who portrays Matthew - Adam and Rachel's son, previously seen as an infant in the original series finale. Spellman found joining the established production daunting and binge-watched the complete series for preparation. I started to realise why the show was so successful, he discovered, though his enthusiastic fan mother constantly pecked his head for storyline details.Both Mrs Spellman and devoted Cold Feet enthusiasts must exercise patience, as producers remain tight-lipped about plot developments to preserve surprises before the autumn premiere.Follow us on Twitter @BBCNewsEnts, on Instagram at bbcnewsents, or email entertainment.news@bbc.co.uk.

text: An electrical fire in a tunnel under a pavement in central London is still burning as firefighters have reported difficulty tackling the blaze. Firefighters battled through Thursday night against an underground blaze that has raged for over 24 hours beneath London's Holborn district, forcing mass evacuations and widespread disruption across the West End.The London Fire Brigade (LFB) confirmed crews would continue working most of the night on Thursday as they fought to contain the fire within the tunnel system. More than 5,000 people fled the area Wednesday when smoke began billowing from an inspection cover, while over 100 businesses faced significant impact from the ongoing emergency.Assistant Commissioner Dany Cotton described the operation as exceptionally challenging. This is a technically difficult and unusual incident to tackle as it is underground, she explained. The underground location makes firefighting very hazardous, requiring special precautions against potential gas explosions.Despite these obstacles, Cotton reported progress: Firefighters have, however, been applying water through access points throughout the night, to control the spread of the fire. She urged the public to steer clear of the immediate vicinity.Currently, 35 firefighters and six fire engines remain stationed on Kingsway, where the LFB has reduced the cordon size though road closures persist. Underground cables are suspected as the fire's origin, though investigators have yet to determine the exact cause.Met Police Inspector Neil Johnson warned of prolonged disruption ahead. Speaking to BBC London 94.9, he predicted extensive road closures: I imagine this road will be closed a long time after this is finished because of damage the heat does to the road. It will have to remain closed until a structural engineer examines it properly and either he or she says what work has to be done and that work is completed - this is not an overnight job.Wednesday's chaos saw onlookers reporting breathing difficulties amid the emergency response. UK Power Networks reported approximately 1,000 customers remain without electricity, though power has been restored to roughly 2,000 others. The company aims to complete full restoration by Thursday's end.Matt Rudling from UK Power Networks offered apologies while explaining the technical challenges: The gas is still burning under there and until we can gain access to that particular area we won't understand what's caused it and what we can do. Emergency generators now supply temporary power while engineers attempt connecting damaged cables to functional networks.The West End entertainment district suffered significant losses Wednesday evening. Multiple prestigious theaters canceled performances, including Beautiful - The Carole King Musical, Charlie And The Chocolate Factory, Disney's The Lion King, Gypsy, Mamma Mia! The Play That Goes Wrong and The Woman In Black. Thursday matinee shows at the Novello and Aldwych theaters also faced cancellation.Westminster City Council's Councillor Richard Beddoe expressed frustration over the infrastructure failure: We are relieved to hear that there were no serious casualties but the losses to big businesses in the West End, due to poor infrastructure, is just not acceptable. We want to see action.The National Grid confirmed involvement in isolating gas supplies after the fire affected one of their transmission pipes. The company outlined the complexity of their response: This is a challenging operation due to the fire's location, access to our gas pipe and other utilities in close proximity. We cannot just turn a valve and switch off the gas because of safety reasons and [the] impact on the gas network.Transportation networks adapted to the disruption. While Holborn station remained operational, Transport for London diverted nine bus services: the 1, 59, 68, 91, 168, 171, 188, 243 and 521 routes.For the latest travel updates follow @BBCTravelAlert on Twitter and visit the BBC London Travel website.

text: US illustrator Norman Bridwell, creator of the Clifford the Big Red Dog books, has died at the age of 86 following a fall at his home in Massachusetts. Since 1963, the beloved character has captured hearts through more than 40 stories that have sold 120 million copies across the globe.From merchandise to appearances in US buildings—even the White House—Clifford's image became ubiquitous in American culture.Two additional books by Bridwell await publication next year, completing his final works.We are deeply saddened by the loss of our loyal and talented friend whose drawings and stories have inspired all of us and generations of children and their parents, said Dick Robinson, president of Scholastic, the author's long-time publisher.Norma, Bridwell's wife of 56 years, reflected on her husband's legacy: A lot of people were Clifford fans and that makes them Norman fans too.The character's name originated from Norma herself, who chose it after her imaginary childhood friend from her own youth.Throughout the decades, the bright red dog starred in numerous adventures—from Clifford Goes To Hollywood to Clifford and The Grouchy Neighbours—becoming essential bedtime reading for children throughout the US and internationally.Each story typically followed a familiar pattern: the dog would find himself in predicaments before ultimately redeeming himself through daring rescues or acts of kindness.According to Bridwell's wife, striking similarities existed between the creator and his famous creation.He's never been able to recognise that. Clifford tries to do the right thing, Norman tries to do right the thing, and he makes a mess of it. But he's the most lovable grown-up man. He's just a nice guy.During the 1950s, before achieving fame with Clifford, Bridwell earned his living as a commercial artist.Multiple attempts to enter children's publishing met with failure until a New York book editor made a crucial suggestion: develop a story around his submitted illustration featuring a child with her oversized dog.More rejections continued until Scholastic recognized the creation's potential—a decision that would generate enduring success for the publishing house.I said to my wife, 'Now don't count on there being any more. This one is just a fluke. I don't know if there will ever be another one,' Bridwell said.In recent decades, the character transitioned to animated television cartoons for US audiences, while 2004 saw the release of a feature film titled Clifford's Big Red Movie.Bridwell leaves behind his wife, one son, and three grandchildren. According to his family, both a small private funeral service and a larger public celebration honoring the author's life and contributions are planned.

text: Residents of a mid Wales village have voted on proposals to install a new train station in the area. Two potential locations for reopening Carno station are now under community consultation, following a request from the Welsh Government to Carno Station Action Group and the local community council.The campaign to restore rail services to this Mid Wales village began in 2002, targeting a stretch of the Cambrian line between Aberystwyth and Shrewsbury. One proposed site occupies the exact location of the original station, which fell victim to the 1963 Beeching cuts that devastated Britain's railway network. Following closure, this historic station site became integrated into the Laura Ashley complex in Carno.Mid Wales Transportation conducted an appraisal in 2011, working alongside the Welsh Government, and concluded there existed compelling justification for future station investment. Should approval be granted, ambitious plans could transform the development into a multifaceted hub featuring a tourist information centre and a dedicated Laura Ashley museum.Jeremy Barnes, chairman of the Action Group, confirmed the week-long consultation concluded on 22 March, with results currently being processed before submission to the Welsh government. Barnes elaborated on the comprehensive vision: We have talked to the Welsh government about the possibility of the new station including a tourist information centre, cafe, an office for the community council's clerk and a small museum dedicated to Laura Ashley should the existing site be chosen.The proposal addresses significant regional connectivity gaps. It is located on the longest stretch of railway without an intermediate station in the whole of Wales, the 22 miles between Caersws and Machynlleth, Barnes explained. He emphasized the economic potential: Carno is a growing village with a population of about 750 and this proposed development will create employment and allow residents affordable access to work further afield.Barnes stressed the community's frustration with underutilized infrastructure: There is a strong consensus that the capital asset of the railway line passing through the village is being wasted as long as the trains pass through without stopping.These consultation efforts emerged from discussions between the action group and Transport Minister Edwina Hart during an October meeting.Laura Ashley's connection to Carno spans nearly twenty-five years until her death in 1985. The renowned fashion designer established her Welsh operations base here in 1961, relocating with husband Bernard from Kent. Her final resting place remains in the village churchyard, cementing her lasting bond with the community.The former Laura Ashley headquarters, once a major manufacturing center for her products, ceased operations in 2004, leaving behind both industrial heritage and redevelopment opportunities.

text: France rounded off their Euro 2016 preparations with a classy and comprehensive victory over Scotland. The striker, who had faced criticism from French media and jeers from supporters leading into the Euros, delivered when it mattered most. His opener came via an ingenious back-heel, followed by an opportunistic close-range rebound that earned thunderous applause from the Metz faithful. Arsenal teammate Laurent Koscielny completed the first-half rout with a well-placed header.Scotland's struggles continued from their disappointing 1-0 loss to Italy six days prior, where Gordon Strachan had criticized his team's inability to retain possession and control the tempo. The goalkeeper's heroics will make him difficult to dislodge when World Cup qualifying begins in September.France's midfield trio of N'Golo Kante, Paul Pogba, and Blaise Matuidi displayed the kind of power and athleticism that makes them such an enticing prospect. text: The body set up to probe deaths during the Troubles in Northern Ireland investigated cases where the state was involved with less rigour than others, a police watchdog has found. A damning inspection report has revealed that Northern Ireland's Historical Enquiries Team operated unlawfully when handling cases involving state forces, with HM Inspectorate of Constabulary concluding that the unit's policies were founded on a misrepresentation of the law.The scathing assessment found serious shortcomings and inconsistencies in how HET approached its investigations, particularly regarding military cases from the Troubles era.Established in 2005, HET was tasked with re-examining 3,260 murders that occurred during Northern Ireland's conflict. However, the inspection determined that the team's handling of state involvement cases violated the European Convention on Human Rights.Her Majesty's inspector of constabulary, Stephen Otter, was unequivocal about the legal violations when questioned about HET's conduct: We think it was acting unlawfully in regard to state cases because it treats them differently in policy terms and in the way that then acts out in practice.So state cases were less effective as a result and effectiveness is a key test of whether it's Article 2 compliant, Otter explained.The inspection arose after Northern Ireland's chief constable Matt Baggott commissioned the HMIC review following mounting criticism. This scrutiny intensified after Dr Patricia Lundy of the University of Ulster published research claiming HET provided preferential treatment to former soldiers while failing to properly investigate military-related deaths.HET had initially rejected Dr Lundy's findings, but the HMIC report vindicated her concerns. Responding to the official validation, Dr Lundy declared: I think the HET as an organisation itself is irretrievable at this point.I think it has implications for lots of different cases, not just the army cases, because we've heard the structural problems, there's no oversight, there's no complaints procedure and really it seemed to me that it was a bit of a law unto itself, she added.Otter acknowledged that Dr Lundy's 2009 report had been unfairly dismissed and called for an official apology. I do think she deserves an apology from the chief constable on behalf of the Police Service of Northern Ireland (PSNI), he stated.What is indefensible is that she did make these findings in 2009, so for four years nothing was being done to address those findings and I do find that that is very difficult to believe.Chief Constable Baggott accepted full responsibility for the failures, announcing that all military cases would undergo re-examination. HET put in place a policy that was wrong, he admitted.A differential approach to military cases is wrong and I assure you this has ended, Baggott declared, while accepting all HMIC recommendations.The inspection examined 31 cases from HET's review of more than 150 soldier-related killings between 1970 and September 1973, focusing on whether military case reviews met current policing standards and human rights requirements.HMIC's findings revealed multiple systemic failures: - Military cases received different treatment as official policy - Standards failed to conform to current policing requirements in numerous critical areas - Explicit systems and processes were lacking - Teams operated with inconsistent working practices - No clearly defined complaints process existed - Independent oversight was absent until this inspectionA particularly troubling discovery was HET's failure to verify claims of illness when potential military interviewees claimed unfitness for questioning. HMIC condemned this as entirely wrong, noting it resulted in military cases receiving less rigour than civilian investigations.The disparity became stark when examining case referrals: since 2010, none of the 39 cases referred back to PSNI for investigation involved state forces.It is striking that not one state involvement case relating to the British Army has to date been referred to the PSNI for further investigation or prosecution, the report observed.HMIC warned that these inconsistencies threatened to undermine families' confidence in HET's effectiveness and impartiality. Otter emphasized the gravity of the situation: HMIC is concerned that the inconsistencies we found in our review may seriously undermine the capability of the HET's processes to determine whether the force used in killings during the Troubles was justified in state involvement cases, therefore potentially preventing the identification and punishment of those responsible.The inspector acknowledged the challenging environment HET operated within, describing it as an extraordinary complex social and political context presenting unparalleled challenges in UK terms.This context makes it even more important for the HET to operate to the highest standards of effectiveness and impartiality, so that the people of Northern Ireland, and the families of the victims whose cases are being reviewed, can have confidence in it, Otter emphasized.The comprehensive inspection involved interviews with over 180 individuals from various organizations, including HET staff, criminal justice agencies, and non-governmental bodies. Investigators also met with families of 13 victims across Belfast and Londonderry.Despite the serious criticisms, HMIC found widespread support for retaining HET, provided substantial improvements were implemented. Many interviewees expressed preference for an independent body separate from PSNI, yet demonstrated almost universal desire for HET's continuation with proper reforms.HET operates as a special investigative unit within PSNI, tasked with reviewing deaths that occurred in Northern Ireland between 1968 and 1998. While technically independent, the unit reports directly to Northern Ireland's chief constable.

text: Progressive music, the oft-maligned genre that had its heyday in the 1970s, is to be endorsed by the Official Charts Company (OCC). It's only 45 years too late, but better late than never, he told the BBC. text: Kenyan officials say the country is closing its borders to travellers from Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone in response to the deadly Ebola outbreak. Those arriving will face rigorous screening and potential quarantine measures if deemed necessary.Despite the flight suspension, Kenya's health secretary confirmed that Kenyans and medical personnel traveling from these states will continue to be permitted entry into the country.The epidemic, which originated in Guinea during February, has subsequently expanded to affect Liberia, Sierra Leone and Nigeria. Recent WHO data shows the death toll climbed to 1,145 on Friday, following reports of 76 additional fatalities in the 48-hour period ending August 13. Total reported cases have reached 2,127.Kenya's health ministry reported earlier that four suspected Ebola cases within the country - involving one Liberian citizen, two Nigerians who had recently traveled to Kenya, and one Zimbabwean - all returned negative test results for the virus.Kenyan Airways announced its decision to halt flights to the capitals of Liberia and Sierra Leone, effective Wednesday when the ban takes effect. The airline made this choice following guidance from Kenya's government and confirmed that passengers with bookings on cancelled routes will receive complete refunds. However, the company clarified that its Nigerian flight services remain unaffected by the suspension.The World Health Organisation has classified Kenya as being at high risk for Ebola transmission due to its status as a significant transportation hub in the region.Medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) projected on Friday that controlling the outbreak will require a minimum of six months. MSF President Joanne Liu described how the situation is deteriorating faster, and moving faster, than we can respond to.The WHO has acknowledged that the outbreak's magnitude appears vastly underestimated and emphasized that extraordinary measures are essential for containment efforts.Ebola spreads through direct contact with infected individuals' bodily fluids. The disease initially presents flu-like symptoms before potentially progressing to external hemorrhaging from locations including the eyes and gums, plus internal bleeding that may result in organ failure.According to WHO assessments, Ebola transmission risk during air travel remains minimal.

text: Leaving the EU without a trade deal would be irresponsible, the president of the CBI business group will warn. The Confederation of British Industry's director-general will deliver a stark warning against pursuing a no-deal Brexit, despite acknowledging that Prime Minister Theresa May is correct in believing an agreement remains achievable.Paul Drechsler plans to tell audiences in London that while he shares the PM's optimism about securing a deal, it would be wrong for anyone to frame the debate as a binary choice between leaving with no agreement at all. According to his prepared remarks, businesses on both sides of the Channel are deeply concerned about this worst-case scenario outcome.The speech represents the latest in a series of business warnings this week, following similar alerts from the British Chambers of Commerce and former chancellor George Osborne. Mr Drechsler will emphasize the CBI's support for the government's ambitious trade deal objectives, noting the organization's collaboration with EU business groups to advance mutually beneficial arrangements.However, he plans to deliver a pointed rebuke to no-deal advocates: But to those whose first and only choice is for Britain to walk away without a deal, I say you're not only wrong but irresponsible.The CBI chief will outline the economic risks facing British exporters under World Trade Organisation rules, warning that 90% of UK exports to the EU would encounter tariffs without an agreement. Additionally, he'll highlight increased regulatory hurdles that would damage businesses throughout the European bloc.While acknowledging that some companies are already making contingency plans for this scenario, Mr Drechsler will note that others cannot afford such preparations due to prohibitive costs.The timing proves significant as Article 50 activation approaches by month's end, as confirmed by Theresa May. Though the prime minister maintains her commitment to securing an agreement, she has repeatedly stated that no deal is better than a bad deal.Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson has expressed confidence that Britain can remain ever-more European and ever-more internationalist simultaneously, insisting a win-win EU arrangement is achievable within the two-year negotiation window.Mr Drechsler will argue that achieving a smooth Brexit serves everyone's interest, but his message faces pushback from Brexit supporters.Change Britain spokesman Chloe Westley dismissed the CBI's concerns, citing the organization's previous positions: The CBI campaigned to join the euro and warned of economic disaster if we left the EU. It has been proven wrong time and again on Europe and there is no reason to suggest that this has now changed.She added: It is overwhelmingly in the EU's interests to strike a free trade agreement with the UK. Instead of being pessimistic about our future, the CBI should support the government in getting the best deal for Britain.Patrick Minford, chairman of Economists for Brexit, challenged assumptions about no-deal consequences entirely. His research suggests removing all import tariffs unilaterally could boost GDP by 4% and treasury receipts by 7.3% compared to current arrangements, even without EU reciprococation.Our economy can and will flourish outside the single market and we do not need a trade deal with the EU to deliver that, Minford concluded.The pro-Brexit group Change Britain has accused the CBI of being proven wrong time and again on Europe, urging the business lobby to adopt a more optimistic stance toward Britain's prospects.

text: A man soldiered on after a serious and brutal hammer attack by a friend before dying five days later, a court was told. A 29-year-old man from Wisbech stands accused of murdering his friend with a hammer attack that allegedly caused fatal internal injuries, Cambridge Crown Court has heard.Mitchell Bird, of Cox Close, is charged with killing Bradley Carter, 35, following what prosecutors describe as a violent assault at Bird's flat on Valentine's Day this year. Bird denies both murder and grievous bodily harm with intent.Prosecutor Richard Christie QC told jurors that Carter had sought refuge at Bird's residence after being expelled from his mother's home for drug use in the open. Both men were described as habitual drug users.The fatal sequence of events began on February 14, when neighbors reported hearing a disturbance and commotion from the flat. According to the prosecution, Bird had accused Carter of attempting to steal from him, leading to the alleged attack.Carter later told others that Bird had beat him repeatedly with a hammer, resulting in holes in his legs. Photographic evidence of Carter's injuries, taken by both Carter and his mother in the days following the assault, was presented to the jury.The prosecution explained that Carter suffered from an enlarged spleen positioned outside his ribcage, which sustained damage during what Christie described as kicks to his body during the attack. This injury would prove fatal when the spleen later ruptured, caused him to haemorrhage and bleed internally.In the days after February 14, Carter spoke about the attack to various people, including friends, family members, a probation officer, and a housing officer, the court heard.Carter's condition deteriorated over the following days. On February 19, his mother Helen Barnes drove him to Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn for medical tests after he continued experiencing significant back pain and showed no signs of improvement.Tragically, while Barnes was away paying for parking, Carter collapsed and died at the hospital, jurors were told.Despite the five-day gap between the alleged assault and Carter's death, Christie emphasized to the jury: Although there was a delay in Bradley Carter dying, this defendant murdered him.The prosecutor added: We have clear evidence in this case that points to Mitchell Bird having perpetrated that assault.The trial is expected to continue for two weeks.

text: On Friday 11 May 2012, Derby woke up to the news there had been a fire at a house in the Allenton area. The devastating blaze that claimed five young lives within hours left a sixth child fighting for survival in hospital. By month's end, the victims' parents - Mick and Mairead Philpott - faced charges for igniting the deadly fire.What transformed this couple from grief-stricken parents, seemingly victims of arson, into prime suspects capable of murdering their own children in the eyes of law enforcement?Audio recordings presented at Nottingham Crown Court during their trial revealed chaos on Victory Road the night flames engulfed the home. Emergency service calls captured Philpott's desperate pleas: Help me! My babies are trapped inside!The parents maintained they were sleeping in the downstairs conservatory when fire erupted. Upstairs, six children - Duwayne, 13, Jade, 10, John, nine, Jack, eight, Jesse, six, and Jayden, five - were trapped. Philpott insisted he attempted rescue using a ladder, efforts Derbyshire Police characterized as apparent valiant attempts.Yet Det Supt Kate Meynell began receiving contradictory accounts from neighbors who had also rushed to save the children that evening.Within a few days they commented on how they felt they were making more effort to rescue the children and that Michael Philpott was not as instrumental as he should have been, she said.Investigation revealed the fire originated in the hallway beneath the letterbox, where petrol had been deliberately poured. Authorities discovered a petrol container near Victory Road and collected a glove as evidence. The arson was unmistakable.Police methodology involved systematically eliminating those closest to the family. Even a man Philpott allegedly assaulted was cleared. The investigation mobilized 88 officers who collected over 5,000 statements and tracked everyone purchasing petrol in containers within five miles of the residence during the days preceding the fire.Suspicion crystallized around the couple following their 16 May press conference. Assistant Chief Constable Steve Cotterill called Mick Philpott's demeanor the most extraordinary display he'd witnessed in thirty years of policing.I would have expected him to be completely and utterly destroyed, he said. Instead, Mr Cotterill observed behavior resembling an actor playing a part. It was a sham, in my view.Investigating their primary suspects required delicate handling. Mick Philpott enjoyed minor celebrity status through Jeremy Kyle show appearances. Police employed covert surveillance in the couple's hotel accommodations to substantiate their growing suspicions.Recordings captured Philpott instructing his wife: You make sure you stick to your story and They're not gonna find any evidence are they? You know what I mean?This evidence precipitated their 29 May arrest on murder charges, later amended to manslaughter. The arrests triggered a cascade effect - acquaintances felt emboldened to voice their suspicions to investigators.It gave some witnesses the confidence to come forward and talk about their concerns, said Det Supt Meynell.Forensic analysis by early November detected petrol residue on clothing belonging to the Philpotts and their associate Paul Mosley, leading to his arrest as well.The motive behind a father's decision to torch his home with children inside gradually emerged. The morning following the fire, Philpott was scheduled to confront former mistress Lisa Willis in court regarding custody of their four children together. The fire represented an elaborate scheme to frame her and secure custody rights.Despite the investigation's ultimate success, Det Supt Meynell carries lasting grief.She said: I would never lose sight of the fact six children have died in the most horrendous circumstances at the hands of their mother and father and their friend.

text: Doctors who carry out cosmetic procedures should give patients time to think before agreeing to go ahead, new guidance says. New guidance from the General Medical Council aims to enhance safety standards for cosmetic procedures ranging from facelifts and breast implants to dermal fillers and Botox injections, covering both surgical and non-surgical treatments.The GMC will now seek input from medical professionals and the general public regarding these proposed standards.According to plastic surgeons, many practitioners have already implemented a mandatory two-week cooling-off period for patients considering cosmetic procedures.Safety concerns in the cosmetic industry gained significant attention following a 2013 report from NHS England's medical director, which examined sector-wide risks. These concerns intensified after the PIP breast implant scandal affected nearly 50,000 British women. The problematic French-manufactured implants contained unauthorized silicone filler and demonstrated rupture rates twice as high as standard implants.Earlier this year, the Royal College of Surgeons released its own consultation document proposing enhanced standards for cosmetic surgery practices.As the regulatory body establishing standards for all UK doctors performing cosmetic procedures, the GMC also works to educate patients about what they should expect from their medical practitioners. The new guidance outlines several key requirements for doctors.Professor Terence Stephenson, chairman of the General Medical Council, emphasized the vulnerability of certain patients in this field and the need for their protection.We are clear that doctors must not pressure patients to make rushed decisions they may end up regretting and they must give them enough information so they can make an informed choice, Stephenson stated.The guidance received support from Rajiv Grover, a consultant plastic surgeon and former President of the British Association of Aesthetic Plastic Surgeons (Baaps), who noted that some patients lack the psychological readiness for cosmetic surgery.Cosmetic surgery has for too long been seen as a commodity but unfortunately once an operation is done - it can't be taken back to the shop, Grover explained.Baaps has maintained a two-week cooling-off period requirement for years and promotes second consultations with surgeons before patients finalize their decisions, according to Grover. The association is currently developing a screening mechanism to identify patients who should avoid surgery altogether.The GMC expects to release its final guidance in early 2016.

text: Careers services for young people in England need to be urgently improved, says a report from an advisory body set up by the government. Young people across England face a troubling postcode lottery when seeking career guidance, according to a damning report from the National Careers Council that exposes dramatic inconsistencies in advice provision nationwide.The investigation reveals massive variations in available services, with stark regional disparities highlighted by one area offering 134 careers advisory services while another provides just a single option. This geographic inequality leaves countless teenagers without adequate support for crucial life decisions.Deirdre Hughes, the council's chair, emphasized that a culture change in careers provision was urgently needed. She noted that while some advancement occurred over the past year, progress has been far too slow. Hughes warned: Meanwhile, our education and labour markets remain complex and confusing for young people, parents and teachers, and there are significant costs associated with this.The report criticizes the National Careers Service's adult-focused structure, creating a significant void in school-age advisory support. While adults receive over a million face-to-face consultation sessions, young people must rely solely on telephone helplines and digital resources rather than personalized guidance.This systematic failure has drawn widespread condemnation from education leaders and industry representatives. The council expressed being disappointed with the slow progress in enhancing youth career services and demanded immediate governmental intervention.Several high-profile critics have highlighted the crisis. Ofsted chief Sir Michael Wilshaw previously warned that the new arrangements were failing to provide good guidance, noting insufficient school expertise in delivering quality advice. The Education Select Committee similarly reported a worrying deterioration in career services last year.Neil Carberry from the CBI declared: The shift of responsibility for careers advice to schools has been a failure. Schools, government and businesses all have a role to play in fixing the problem, it cannot be shouldered by schools alone.Brian Lightman, general secretary of the Association of School and College Leaders, acknowledged schools' efforts but stressed that many are finding it extremely difficult. He described how a stark postcode lottery is putting many young people at a real disadvantage.Nick Chambers, director of the Education and Employers Taskforce charity, painted a concerning picture: Far too many young people are having to make vital and incredibly important decisions about their futures without access to good and reliable information.The council's recommendations include establishing an employer-led advisory body to oversee system improvements and ensuring all schools receive free or subsidized access to independent and impartial career development. Additionally, they propose creating an investment fund to expand successful career advice models across different schools and regions.Political criticism has been equally sharp. Labour's shadow education secretary, Tristram Hunt, stated: There is surely no other policy agenda where the government has so miserably failed our young people. Hunt pledged to reverse the decision making work experience placements optional and ensure every school has a governor dedicated to fostering local business connections for career guidance and workplace exposure.Hughes concluded with an urgent appeal: We urge government and others to take action across England to halt the rapid decline in careers services for young people.The report represents the latest in a series of critical assessments questioning the wisdom of transferring career advice responsibilities to individual schools, highlighting the urgent need for comprehensive reform to prevent further disadvantaging of England's youth.

text: A botnet which experts believe sent out 18% of the world's spam email has been shut down, a security firm said. The dismantling of Grum's command infrastructure marked a significant victory against cybercriminals, with the botnet's control servers primarily operating from Panama, Russia and Ukraine.Through coordinated efforts between security firm FireEye and anti-spam organization SpamHaus, working alongside local internet service providers (ISPs), authorities successfully eliminated this illegal network. Botnets represent networks of compromised computers, typically infected through malware deployment by cybercriminals.FireEye security researcher Atif Mushtaq emphasized the collaborative nature of the operation, stating: Grum's takedown resulted from the efforts of many individuals. He added a pointed message to spammers: This collaboration is sending a strong message to all the spammers: Stop sending us spam. We don't need your cheap Viagra or fake Rolex.The takedown unfolded across several days. Initially, Mr Mushtaq discovered Monday that Dutch authorities had disabled a server connected to Grum, which he noted at least made a dent in the botnet. By Tuesday, Panama's command and control servers (CnCs) had been eliminated.However, the cybercriminals quickly adapted. This good news was soon followed by some bad news, Mr Mushtaq explained. After seeing that the Panamanian server had been shut down, the bot herders moved quickly and started pointing the rest of the CnCs to new secondary servers in Ukraine.The cat-and-mouse game intensified as Mr Mushtaq observed: So at one point, I was thinking that all we needed was to take down one Russian server, but right in front of my eyes, the bot herders started pointing their botnet to new destinations.Ukraine's reputation as a cybercriminal sanctuary complicated matters. Shutting down any servers there has never been easy, Mr Mushtaq noted, describing the country as historically serving as a safe haven for bot herders.This victory represents one among numerous international efforts targeting botnet operations. Previously, Russian national Georgiy Avanesov received a four-year prison sentence in May for orchestrating the Bredolab botnet, which generated over £80,000 monthly. Meanwhile, Microsoft continues battling Zeus, another massive network that researchers claim has stolen millions of pounds.The international security community's coordinated pressure on local ISPs proved crucial in suspending the criminal operation. Despite more than 20,000 computers remaining infected, Mr Mushtaq explained that without functioning CnCs, these machines would become ineffective.Mr Mushtaq viewed Grum's elimination as progress in the global fight against botnets. When the appropriate channels are used, even ISPs within Russia and Ukraine can be pressured to end their cooperation with bot herders, he observed.The operation challenged cybercriminals' assumptions about geographic immunity. There are no longer any safe havens. Most of the spam botnets that used to keep their CnCs in the USA and Europe have moved to countries like Panama, Russia, and Ukraine thinking that no one can touch them in these comfort zones, Mr Mushtaq declared.His final message carried both triumph and determination: We have proven them wrong this time. Keep on dreaming of a junk-free inbox.

I was raised in this small town of Hope to believe that where you started was not where you had to stop.” He was a former Southern Baptist preacher who talked about his childhood and the BB-gun he received as a five-year-old, and spoke of abolishing the Department of Education, which has been a favorite cause of conservatives in recent years who are against federal education reforms. “I’ve always believed that children can be taught better things,” he said. And the people who had applauded the announcement shouted, “We want Mike!” He urged the securing of the border with Mexico, but he gave few details. This was a return to his presidential campaign. In the last election his campaign, which finished a surprising second to John McCain, carried the Iowa caucuses and seven other states. Four years later, the talk of a Huckabee run was already starting to stir. But the former governor, who was used to his comfortable position as a radio and television host, and despite his leading position in the Republican polls, decided not to run, saying that his heart told him not to. He also reaffirmed his unwavering opposition to gay marriage. In his speech, Huckabee referred to the advantage of being the first male in his family to graduate from high school. Now his heart has changed course. Huckabee has abandoned his media commitments and has entered the race, which is much more crowded than it was in 2012. Huckabee has some advantages: a high degree of name recognition, a pre-established system of collection and experience in election campaigns; but there is the question whether these advantages are sufficient to meet the Republican field, many of whom are evangelicals. His father was not an educated man, but he was a good man. His campaign for the presidency of the United States faces several obstacles from within his own party. Conservatives may cite the general increase in taxes and expenditures that took place during his term as governor of Arkansas. He had a father and a mother who had not much but were honest to the last drop, he thought. Although he hasn’t officially declared his candidacy, Jeb Bush is currently leading the race for the party’s nomination. Unlike in 2008, when he won eight primaries in socially conservative states, this time he must beat the likes of Senators Marco Rubio, Ted Cruz and Rand Paul, as well as former HP chief Carly Fiorina and retired neurosurgeon Ben Carson.

text: The way alcohol is sold in airports is to be examined after a number of recent incidents involving drunk passengers, the new aviation minister has said. A government minister has indicated he will examine alcohol sales restrictions and passenger screening procedures at airports, following concerns about disruptive behavior on flights, though he emphasized not wanting to kill merriment entirely.Between March 2014 and March 2016, police statistics revealed through Freedom of Information requests show that 442 individuals were detained on suspicion of intoxication either at UK airports or aboard aircraft. Despite these figures, the government maintains it has no specific plans to tackle airport alcohol issues.Recent incidents have highlighted the severity of the problem. A female passenger assaulted an Easyjet pilot by punching him in the face after being told to disembark at Manchester before takeoff. Additionally, German authorities arrested six men from a stag party in February when their mid-air altercation forced a Ryanair flight traveling from Luton to Bratislava, Slovakia, to make an emergency diversion to Berlin.Lord Ahmad addressed the balance between passenger enjoyment and safety concerns, stating: If you're a young family travelling on a plane you want to go from point A to B, you don't want to be disrupted.I don't think we want to kill merriment altogether, but I think it's important that passengers who board planes are also responsible and have a responsibility to other passengers, and that certainly should be the factor which we bear in mind, he continued.Regarding potential regulatory changes, Lord Ahmad explained: In terms of specific regulations of timings of outlets [which sell alcohol] and how they operate, clearly I want to have a look at that.The minister also emphasized the importance of pre-boarding passenger screening procedures.Some airports have already implemented preventive measures. Glasgow and Manchester airports have tested programs requiring alcohol purchases to be sealed in bags, aimed at reducing flight-related incidents.Industry representatives from UK airlines and airports acknowledge that while such disruptions represent a very rare occurrence, they can result in serious consequences. They stress that aircraft disruption constitutes an illegal offense potentially resulting in travel bans, substantial fines, or imprisonment.The scale of air travel puts these incidents in perspective - the Civil Aviation Authority's latest passenger survey recorded 238 million travelers passing through UK airports during 2014.This week saw budget airline Jet2.com introduce a disruptive passenger code of practice, developed through cooperation between airlines, airports, law enforcement, and retail establishments.The zero tolerance policy requires airport retailers to advise customers against consuming purchased alcohol before or during flights. Additionally, bar and restaurant personnel receive specialized training to restrict or halt alcohol sales when necessary to prevent or manage disruptive incidents.However, a Department for Transport spokeswoman maintained the current position: Airport security is always under review, however there are no plans to specifically address the issue of alcohol at airports.

text: Hospital beds in England may fill up with the elderly and vulnerable because of cuts to local authority social care funding, a top NHS figure has warned. NHS Confederation chief Nigel Edwards has warned that hospital patients requiring medical treatment could face bed shortages due to government spending cuts, according to a letter he sent to the Daily Telegraph.While Chancellor George Osborne's Spending Review protected health spending through ring-fencing, English councils are confronting a 27% reduction in central government funding across the next four years. Edwards acknowledged that the £2bn interim solution to social care funding announced in the Spending Review would provide welcome relief to many, though he cautioned about potential knock-on effects on health services due to the funding squeeze.The Department for Health countered by highlighting the additional £2bn allocation designed to safeguard social care.Less support from council services will quickly lead to increased pressure on emergency services and hospitals, Edwards wrote in his Telegraph letter. Hospital beds will be blocked for those who badly need care because the support services the elderly require after discharge will not be available.Edwards emphasized the critical need for collaboration: When it comes to the care of the most vulnerable in our society, it really is essential that the NHS and local authorities are in it together.The Spending Review's key measures include: • £81bn in public spending cuts over four years • 19% average departmental cuts - below the anticipated 25% • £7bn additional welfare cuts, affecting incapacity, housing benefit and tax credits • £1.8bn increase in public sector pension employee contributions by 2014 • Accelerated rise in state pension age • 7% cut for local councils beginning April next year • Permanent bank levy • Rail fares rising 3% above inflation from 2012A Department of Health spokeswoman acknowledged that social care can impact on NHS demands, explaining their response: That's why we are strengthening programmes like re-ablement and the 30-day re-admission tariff, which will integrate hospital care with care in the community.The department emphasized their commitment: We have allocated an additional £2bn by 2014-15 - this extra boost, alongside an ambitious programme of efficiency, will ensure that there is enough funding available both to protect people's access to services and deliver new approaches to improve quality and outcomes.Officials expect local health and social care professionals will work together to ensure that the funding is spent on joint health and social care priorities and improve outcomes for everyone.However, Local Government Association's Councillor David Rogers questioned the adequacy of the £2bn allocation. Of course that is very welcome, but as part of what councils said to the government before the Spending Review, there's likely to be a gap over that same time of about £6bn, he stated.Rogers added: So, there are still going to be difficulties. But I think that the important thing is to ensure that both councils and the NHS locally work increasingly closely together to provide the best service to our residents.Thursday brought additional criticism regarding whether the £2bn designated for social care would reach its intended destination, with half coming from direct local government grants.Nuffield Trust think tank chief executive Jennifer Dixon expressed skepticism: The reality is that local authority budgets will be stretched and funds for social care are not ring-fenced, so the extra £1bn per year is by no means certain.

Less support from council services will quickly lead to increased pressure on emergency services and hospitals because the support services needed for patients to be discharged will not be available. text: Antrim lost 2-06 to 0-09 to Limerick in their All-Ireland Qualifier Round 1B game at Corrigan Park on Saturday. Despite entering the match without a single competitive victory all season, Limerick transformed their fortunes through early strikes from Ian Ryan and Sean McSweeney's penalty conversion, propelling them toward triumph.At halftime, the visitors held a 2-2 to 0-6 advantage before extending their lead with additional scores from McSweeney, Ryan and Stephen Cahill. Crucially, goalkeeper Donal O'Sullivan delivered three outstanding saves that proved decisive for Limerick's cause.For Antrim, their championship journey concluded in deflating circumstances, as the Saffrons failed to capitalize on their recent promotion to Division Three of the Football League.The opening exchanges saw Antrim exploit favorable wind conditions effectively. Ryan Murphy converted a free kick after just 40 seconds, followed by Kevin Niblock's score from the right flank, establishing a 0-2 to 0-0 lead for the home team.However, Limerick received a massive lift in the fifth minute when Seanie Buckley's precise pass found Ryan positioned at the square's edge. The St Senan's forward buried a low drive past Chris Kerr to level the contest.Three minutes later, disaster struck Antrim again as McSweeney stepped up for a penalty opportunity. The spot kick was awarded after midfielder Darragh Treacy was brought down having penetrated behind Antrim's defensive line. McSweeney maintained his composure, drilling the ball into the net's bottom right corner to establish a 2-01 to 0-02 lead for the visitors.While those goals injected significant confidence into Limerick's performance, Antrim mounted a spirited response. Matthew Fitzpatrick opened his account with an excellent 13th-minute effort from the right - though a goal attempt might have been the better option. Four minutes subsequently, Patrick McBride added his team's fourth point, reducing the deficit to three.Following an injury to Limerick captain Iain Corbett, Tommy Childs entered as a late substitute and made an immediate impact around midfield. His intelligent play created space for Ryan's second score from the right after 18 minutes.Ryan nearly doubled his goal tally nine minutes before the break, rising above substitute Martin Johnson, but Kerr produced an exceptional save with his feet to deny the attempt.Antrim concluded the first half impressively, with McBride and Sean Burke both finding their target to leave Limerick holding a two-point interval advantage.Carrying their slender lead and benefiting from strengthening wind assistance, Limerick emerged energetically for the second period. Following some resolute defensive work, corner-back Cahill stretched their advantage to three points in the 44th minute.Having managed only six points across 50 minutes, Antrim desperately required a goal to mount any meaningful comeback. That opportunity materialized for Martin Johnson as he drove inward from the right, but Donal O'Sullivan produced a superb save to preserve his clean sheet.Tomas McCann's introduction provided Antrim with essential attacking pace, and he complemented a Ryan Murray free with his own score, cutting Limerick's lead to two points with nine minutes remaining.Ryan responded by extending the gap to a goal through a free kick, yet Antrim twice threatened to find the net in the closing stages. However, O'Sullivan's brilliant saves against Ryan Murray and Martin Johnson secured Limerick's progression to the next round.Limerick: D O'Sullivan; P Browne, S Cahill (0-1), S O'Dea; B Fanning, J McCarthy, P Ranahan; D Treacy, S Buckley; G Noonan, P Nash, T Childs; S McSweeney (1-3, 1-0 pen, 0-3f), I Ryan (1-2), H Bourke.Subs: E Hogan for Bourke (50 mins), P Hannon for Nash (63 mins), I Corbett for Childs (66 mins).Antrim: C Kerr; K O'Boyle, J Crozier, R Johnson; P McBride (0-2), P Gallagher, M Sweeney; S McVeigh, M McCann; J Laverty, M Fitzpatrick (0-1), K Niblock (0-2, 1f)); R Murray (0-2f), N McKeever, S Burke (0-1).Subs: M Johnson for McVeigh (20 mins), D McAleese for Laverty (30 mins), C Murray for Gallagher (h-t), P McAleer for R Johnson (h-t), T McCann for McKeever (56 mins), J Carron for Burke (66 mins).
