text: Saturday's FA Cup final between Arsenal and Aston Villa at Wembley will be watched by half a billion viewers in more than 120 countries. The world's oldest cup competition prepares for its 134th final at Wembley, where nearly 90,000 spectators will witness elite millionaire athletes compete for glory. Yet the inaugural championship in 1872 presented a starkly different spectacle.On that historic day 143 years ago, approximately 2,000 onlookers gathered to watch 22 amateur players battle on a cricket pitch without nets, as Wanderers defeated Royal Engineers 1-0 through Morton Betts' decisive strike.BBC Sport, collaborating with De Montfort University's professor of history Matthew Taylor, examines that groundbreaking final...**The Tournament's Genesis**Before 1872's FA Cup emerged, England lacked regular competitive football fixtures. Football Association secretary Charles Alcock conceived plans for the inaugural tournament, attracting 15 teams to November 1871's opening round.The participating clubs included Barnes, Civil Service, Hitchin, Crystal Palace (the original club dissolved in 1876, distinct from today's team), Maidenhead, Marlow, Queen's Park, Donington School, Upton Park, Clapham Rovers, Royal Engineers, Reigate Priory, Wanderers, Harrow Chequers and Hampstead Heathens, who received a bye.Steam-age logistics created scheduling nightmares across Britain, resulting in Scottish team Queen's Park reaching the semi-finals without playing a single match.Both semi-finals at Kennington Oval ended goalless. Royal Engineers secured their final berth with a 3-0 replay victory over Crystal Palace, while Wanderers advanced when Queen's Park withdrew, unable to afford another expensive London journey for their replay.**Historical Context**The historian's view: The general consensus is that the FA Cup was based on the knockout competitions between 'Houses' at major public schools such as Harrow. But Alcock may also have taken inspiration from existing competitions in the provinces, such as Sheffield's Youdon Cup, launched in 1867.Certainly football was equally, if not more, established and popular in Sheffield as it was in London at this time, and the elite ex-public schoolboys based in the capital knew and played against teams from Sheffield, Nottingham and elsewhere.**The Finalists**Alcock, the tournament's mastermind, played defense for Wanderers. Originally Forest Football Club in 1859, the team comprised former Harrow pupils who adopted 'Wanderers' because they played at various venues. By 1869, they settled at Kennington Oval, where Alcock served as Surrey cricket club secretary.Major Francis Marindin founded Royal Engineers in 1863—a remarkable figure who served in the Crimean war, participated in the 1872 final, became FA president in 1874, and refereed eight subsequent FA Cup finals.**The Venue**Kennington Oval hosted the 1872 final, the same ground that staged the first England-Scotland international in 1870. The venue would accommodate 20 of the following 21 FA Cup finals, with only the 1873 final held at Lillie Bridge near Chelsea's current Stamford Bridge home.The historian's view: Many football clubs played on cricket grounds in the late 19th century. Football clubs often emerged from existing cricket clubs, as a way of the players keeping fit in the winter. Purpose-built football grounds did not emerge in significant numbers until the 1880s and 1890s.**Attendance and Atmosphere**While modern Wembley crowds battle through masses of supporters, 1872's affair remained subdued. Football hadn't captured public imagination, drawing roughly 2,000 spectators to the Oval.Though much has transformed beyond recognition in football, attendance costs remain contentious...The historian's view: Attendances for football matches were not large in the early 1870s, with one reason for the relatively low attendance the price of tickets, which at one shilling (five pence in today's money) was higher than for most matches at the time.The Oval crowd was said to be 'very fashionable', so presumably made up of the well-to-do and the upper middle-class, as well as those connected with the 'old boys' public school network that ran the Football Association at this time.**Tactical Innovation**Royal Engineers resembled their era's Barcelona, employing revolutionary 'passing' tactics that contrasted sharply with conventional ball-chasing approaches.Betts scored the match's sole goal after 15 minutes, playing under pseudonym A H Chequer (referencing his Harrow Chequers membership), collecting the ball following Walpole Vidal's extended dribble before striking home.Goalkeeping remained non-specialized, with keepers frequently playing outfield positions.The historian's view: It was not unusual for teams to line up with six or seven forwards in the early 1870s. text: A gay man has won a landmark ruling which will give his husband the same pension rights as a wife would receive. Meanwhile, human rights organization Liberty proclaimed that thousands of individuals stand to gain from this ruling. Government officials indicated they would examine the decision's ramifications.According to BBC legal affairs correspondent Clive Coleman, this judgment will create a dramatic effect on the entitlement of thousands of civil partners and spouses in same sex marriages. These couples will now possess identical pension rights and benefits as their heterosexual counterparts, Coleman noted.The decision transforms Mr Walker's husband's financial future dramatically. Typically, occupational pension schemes provide surviving spouses with 50% of the pension's value for life, regardless of when the marriage occurred.However, the Equality Act 2010 contained a provision that permitted employers to deny civil partners spousal benefits accrued before December 2005. This ruling was made under EU law and is a direct consequence of the rights protection the EU gives us, Norton explained.We now risk losing that protection. text: At one of the shops serving the troops in Camp Bastion there are plenty of reminders that this war is nearly over, at least for those who have travelled from Britain and America. The merchandise racks are thinning out. Special offers mark down remaining inventory while full-price souvenirs signal an approaching finale.Drinking glasses bear the message Been there; Done that, and a mug declares Happiness is Helmand in the rear view mirror — stark reminders that departure looms.Once a thriving military metropolis rivaling Reading in scale, Bastion now transforms into something resembling a ghost town. Empty compounds that previously teemed with tents and military vehicles stand vacant. The familiar rhythm of helicopter rotors overhead has grown sporadic, while fewer uniformed personnel traverse the pathways.Most other British installations across Helmand have already vanished as Bastion continues its gradual contraction. During the conflict's peak, approximately 10,000 British military personnel operated from 137 bases throughout southern Afghanistan's province.Today, roughly 4,000 UK personnel remain at merely two locations: Bastion's main operating base and Sterga 2, an observation post offering strategic oversight of the Helmand valley.Sterga will soon transfer to Nato command as the British-led Task Force Helmand dissolves into Regional Command South West under a US Marine Corps brigadier general's leadership.Afghan forces now control Lashkar Gah, the former British headquarters and main operating base. The structures that recently housed a British provincial reconstruction team will become a health centre — a transformation no UK presence will witness.This represents Britain's complete withdrawal from one of Afghanistan's most violent regions.Camp Price, which once sheltered 2,000 troops, has been demolished over recent weeks. British soldiers now wield chainsaws and diggers as their primary tools.The saws dismantle protective Hesco walls while diggers level terrain — returning dust to dust. Even concrete barriers serving as impromptu memorials, adorned with graffiti honoring fallen comrades, have been removed.Capt David Goodman observes the final shipping containers being loaded onto trucks. Since October, 600 containers have departed Price.I am now dreaming of ISO containers, he says. We have been sending out 20 or 30 a day and it is a nightmare, waking up thinking 'did this container go?'Virtually nothing remains behind, raising questions about British forces' enduring legacy after eight years in Helmand and 448 military fatalities.Peace certainly isn't that legacy. Distant gunfire echoes as the last containers leave Camp Price.Lt Col Mike Caldicott of the Royal Logistic Corps commanded the final military convoy departing Price — likely Helmand's last logistic patrol. He maintains conviction in their impact.I only wish that people at home could see the changes I have seen through my eyes, he says. I think they would feel a lot better about the investment we have made.This perspective contrasts with soldiers who seem more focused on homecoming than their legacy.One states simply: Job done, get home. Another remarks: I will miss the sun, that is probably about it.While most soldiers believe they've made a difference, few in uniform echo David Cameron's claim last year of mission accomplished.Lt Gen John Lorimer, Afghanistan's most senior British general, acknowledges extraordinary things have been achieved across the country. However, when questioned about mission accomplished, he sidesteps the phrase entirely.There is still a lot to be done, he responds instead. One senior British officer describes Iraq as the A-level exam while Afghanistan represents the PhD.Domestic assessment proves harsher. Current reluctance toward military intervention mirrors public war fatigue.Margaret Evison, who lost her son Mark in Helmand during 2009, has processed her grief but states: There is nothing in my mind that would justify my son's death.Regarding broader achievements, she questions whether British withdrawal coincides with increased Afghan stability. Concerning Cameron's mission accomplished declaration, she responds: Well he has to say that!Brig James Woodham, Task Force Helmand's final commander, also acknowledges substantial remaining work. While believing progress occurred, he concedes that ultimately history will be the judge of what has been achieved.The peculiarity remains that after eight years of significant investment, no British military presence will remain to influence the concluding narrative.

text: Basketball's biggest star LeBron James has announced his return to the Cleveland Cavaliers - the team where he began his NBA career 11 years ago. In a Friday interview with Sports Illustrated, the 29-year-old basketball superstar revealed his decision to return home. Since July 1st, James has remained a free agent after choosing to opt out of his Miami Heat contract's final two years.I always believed I'd return to Cleveland and finish my career there, James declared.The four-time NBA most valuable player abandoned his Miami contract last month, walking away from $42.7m (£25.1m) he would have collected over the remaining two seasons. While his decision triggered intense competition among teams seeking his services, James disclosed that returning to Ohio had always occupied his mind.James, an Akron native from 40 miles outside Cleveland, explained his reasoning: After last season, free agency wasn't even a thought. But I have two boys and my wife, Savannah, is pregnant with a girl. I started thinking about what it would be like to raise my family in my home town.Though he considered other franchises, James remained resolute about his destination. I looked at other teams, but I wasn't going to leave Miami for anywhere except Cleveland. The more time passed, the more it felt right. This is what makes me happy.James's basketball journey began when Cleveland selected him as their first draft pick in 2003. Over seven seasons, he achieved superstardom before Miami lured him away in 2010, where he created a formidable trio alongside Chris Bosh and Dwyane Wade.His 2010 departure announcement came through a staged ESPN television program titled The Decision, which provoked fierce backlash from Cleveland supporters who angrily burned his jerseys. Despite forgoing $20m (£11.7m) for next season, James captured NBA championships with Miami in 2012 and 2013. The Heat also reached Finals in 2011, falling to Dallas, and 2014, suffering a crushing defeat to San Antonio.Reflecting on his Miami experience, James expressed mixed emotions: The hardest thing to leave is what I built with those guys. I've talked to some of them and will talk to others. Nothing will ever change what we accomplished. We are brothers for life.Cleveland airport loudspeakers broadcast news of James's return, while Cavaliers ticket phone lines crashed under overwhelming demand, ESPN reported.Cavaliers owner Dan Gilbert, who in 2010 penned an open letter condemning James's departure as a shocking act of disloyalty and shameful display of selfishness and betrayal, offered a dramatically different response Friday. He tweeted: My eight-year-old: 'Daddy, does this mean I can finally wear my LeBron jersey, again?' Yes it does, son. Yes it does!Meanwhile, Miami reactions proved less celebratory. According to South Florida's WPLG Local 10, vandals defaced a James mural. Heat owner Micky Arison tweeted his disappointment: I am shocked and disappointed in today's news. However I will never forget what LeBron brought us for four years. Thanks for the memories.Miami's troubles may deepen considerably. Both Wade and Bosh entered free agency this summer alongside James and could potentially follow their former teammate's exodus from South Beach.Beyond the Sports Illustrated interview, James shared an Instagram photo showing himself in a Cavaliers uniform, captioned I'm coming home.However, James cautioned Cleveland supporters against expecting immediate success. When I left Cleveland, I was on a mission, James explained. I was seeking championships, and we won two. But Miami already knew that feeling. Our city hasn't had that feeling in a long, long, long time.He tempered expectations further: I'm not promising a championship. I know how hard that is to deliver. We're not ready right now. No way. Of course, I want to win next year, but I'm realistic. It will be a long process, much longer than it was in 2010. My patience will get tested. I know that.

text: The jobs market has seen a substantial decline in people starting full-time jobs since the start of the year, according to a regular survey of recruiters. A recruitment survey covering approximately 100 Scottish employment consultants reveals the nation's job market continued its downward trajectory through January, marking the fourth straight month of declining permanent placements.The data, compiled jointly by Markit and the Recruitment and Employment Confederation (REC), painted a concerning picture of Scotland's employment landscape. While demand for both permanent and temporary positions increased during the month, the availability of candidates for permanent roles dropped sharply alongside actual placements.Kevin Green, chief executive of REC, commented: The jobs market in Scotland continued to deteriorate in January, with recruiters reporting a decline in permanent placements for the fourth consecutive month. Scotland's economy is not as strong as the rest of the UK. The energy sector has weakened, and ongoing political uncertainty is affecting business confidence.Despite these challenges, certain sectors continue driving recruitment demand. Nursing, medicine and care consistently lead hiring requirements, with engineering and construction following closely behind.The construction industry faces particular workforce pressures, according to Wednesday's Construction Industry Training Board (CITB) forecast. The sector requires 12,000 new recruits over the next five years to replace departing workers and those leaving the country entirely.However, CITB projects overall construction employment will shrink as major infrastructure projects like the Queensferry Crossing conclude their peak phases. Home-building and repair markets show modest growth prospects of just 1% to 2%.Ian Hughes, a director at CITB, said: While we have factored Brexit into this forecast, there remain many unknowns to life after leaving the EU. We will be working with our industry to understand what it means for our migrant workforce and what we must do to attract and grow more of our own.Scotland's employment metrics lag behind broader UK performance. Starting salaries rose but at slower rates than parallel surveys indicated for Britain overall. The nation's job market appears markedly weaker compared to stronger employment conditions elsewhere across the country.Temporary employment showed more positive signs, with recruitment consultants reporting the fastest hiring pace in over twelve months. Hourly pay rates for temporary workers increased, though wage inflation momentum slowed.Green added: Vacancies in Scotland remain in growth, so demand for staff is robust, despite employers showing hesitancy when it comes to investment decisions. This suggests the market could pick up again if confidence is restored.The mixed signals reflect broader economic uncertainties affecting Scottish business confidence, particularly stemming from energy sector weakness and political instability concerns.

His troubled stint at St Mary's included a training-ground altercation that led to a January loan move to Juventus.It was a difficult situation for him to come back to, Koeman explained to BBC Radio Solent. He was too late. The decision of the board was to allow him not to come back. We have to look for opportunities for him to play in a different team.Osvaldo's Southampton career was marked by controversy from the start. The Panama Papers revelations initially sparked the investigation when they connected his children to offshore entities used for purchasing London properties.These revelations intensified suspicions that the companies served as vehicles for money laundering—allegations Mr Sharif vehemently contests. While acknowledging the London properties were legitimately obtained, he maintains personal non-ownership of these assets.Opposition factions are mounting pressure, accusing his family of exploiting political positions to accumulate illegal wealth and demanding his resignation. This controversy now poses a substantial threat to his leadership.Mr Sharif remains defiant, dismissing the investigators' findings as mere allegations and assumptions while refusing to step down. Last week's federal cabinet meeting reinforced his decision to retain power.Security measures around the Supreme Court have intensified dramatically, with hundreds of personnel deployed and barbed wire fencing erected around sections of the building.The Joint Investigation Team (JIT), established in April, has identified significant gaps/disparity among the known and declared sources of income and the wealth amassed by Mr Sharif and his relatives.The team alleges Mr Sharif concealed assets and inflated his father's wealth to legitimize his family's fortune. Additionally, they claim he failed to report an exorbitant hike in family wealth during his initial decade in office (1985-93).His daughter Maryam Sharif, considered his political successor, faces accusations of being the beneficial owner of offshore companies that acquired the London flats. The JIT alleges she fabricated documents portraying herself as a trustee for her brother, the purported actual owner.A trust deed copy signed by her in February 2006 forms the basis of this allegation. The JIT contends the document used Calibri font, which wasn't commercially released until January 2007.The Panama Papers leak—11 million documents from Panama-based Mossack Fonseca law firm—exposed both the flats' existence and their connected offshore companies.According to the family, proceeds from selling their UAE-based Gulf Steel Mills funded the flats and their UK and Gulf region businesses. PM Sharif's late father, Mian Mohammad Sharif, established the mill in the early 1970s, later investing sale proceeds in Qatar-based ventures.Former Qatari Prime Minister Prince Hammad bin Jassim al-Thani provided a letter explaining the money trail, though he remained unavailable for JIT interviews. However, the JIT discovered no evidence of funds flowing from Pakistan through Dubai and Qatar to the London properties.National division over the JIT report reflects starkly in media coverage. Pro-government channels portray the report as fabricated lies, while pro-opposition outlets convince viewers of the Sharif family's corruption involvement.Complex international finance issues permeate the report, encompassing intricate financial regulations across multiple jurisdictions and regulatory authorities. While much content may reflect reality, experts identify instances where the JIT seemingly compensated for limited access or understanding, or included unfounded opinions.Controversy surrounds the Supreme Court's decision to include representatives from two military intelligence services—MI and ISI—among the six-member JIT, which ideally should comprise only financial experts. The court's choice to grant ISI exclusive secretarial services to the JIT has drawn criticism from those believing this service has actively managed Pakistan's political hierarchy since the 1980s.Many suspect ISI interference ahead of 2018 elections to preserve its political establishment influence.Three possibilities emerge: The Supreme Court faces immense pressure while handling this unprecedented situation. Establishing the JIT to examine the prime minister's wealth marked an extraordinary step—the JIT represents neither constitutional nor executive creation, but rather a Supreme Court initiative.Consequently, few anticipate complete rejection of the JIT report by the court.Should disqualification occur, Mr Sharif would face lifetime political exclusion under the constitution's honest and sagacious provision. His daughter and political heir would confront identical prospects.If disqualified, the prime minister would likely name a successor—possibly his brother Shahbaz, Punjab's chief minister—allowing the government to complete its term. Under alternative circumstances, analysts expect him to remain in position and, if necessary, fight until the end.

text: A recovering alcoholic has been jailed for four months for stealing £11,000 from a faulty Ulster Bank cash machine. At Downpatrick Crown Court, 58-year-old Peter Anthony Young from Hunter's Way, Ardglass, received a four-month custodial sentence after a judge determined he had deliberately taken advantage of a significant banking system failure nearly four years earlier.The Ulster Bank computer malfunction allowed customers to make ATM withdrawals without any impact on their account balances. Bank investigators later traced the unauthorized withdrawals to Young's account.Ms Ivers, representing the prosecution, explained to the court that Ulster Bank experienced a computer malfunction in its system on 22 June 2012. She revealed that Young, an Ulster Bank customer, had withdrawn £11,000 from his account that same day through 22 separate £500 transactions.After the bank's unsuccessful attempts to reach Young, officials reported the incident to police as fraudulent. The PSNI launched an investigation, leading to Young's voluntary attendance at a police station where he confessed to the withdrawals. He told officers he had spent the money on drink.The prosecution noted that Young, still an Ulster Bank customer, had made no effort to pay back the funds, leaving an outstanding balance of £10,908.40.Young's defence counsel characterized the situation as an unusual case, emphasizing that his client made frank admissions during his September 2014 police interview.Reading between the lines from the court papers, it appears Mr Young was in the company of other people drinking with them that day and when he was taking money out it became apparent to him and the others that there was a fault with this machine, the defence lawyer told the court. This was always going to come home to him. He is not in the least blaming others.The defence painted a picture of Young's troubled past, explaining that his life had taken a downward spiral after his mother's death in 1991. By age 34, Young had become an alcoholic, homeless, and was living on the streets of Belfast.However, the court heard that the father-of-five was now a recovering alcoholic, regularly attending Alcoholics Anonymous meetings, participating in a church group, and enrolled in a rehabilitation programme.The defence requested a community order, arguing it would leave something hanging over his head that would remind him not to stray from the straight and narrow again. The lawyer urged the court to give him a chance to continue to improve himself.The judge acknowledged that Young initially withdrew £500 on the day in question but emphasized his deliberate actions afterward. He chose to return to this machine a further 21 times to withdraw the money when he knew he did not have the funds in his account, the judge stated. He knew full well what he was doing and he deliberately took advantage of the defective ATM.Noting that Young, who survives on social security benefits, had not repaid any stolen money to Ulster Bank, the judge concluded: I don't believe I could deal with this case by way of a suspended sentence. The least sentence I can impose is one of four months in custody.

text: A primary school in Leeds has introduced a temporary ban on children playing tig during break times after clothes were torn and pupils were left upset. A school's decision to ban the playground game of tig has sparked fresh debate about educational institutions restricting traditional childhood activities across England.The headmaster justified halting the game - alternatively called tag or you're it - by explaining children needed some time to settle down a bit. This prohibition joins a growing catalogue of everyday school activities that have been outlawed by educational establishments nationwide, many triggering nostalgia for simpler times when such pursuits were commonplace.**British Bulldog Falls Victim to Safety Concerns**Perhaps predictably, many schools have already eliminated this high-energy playground staple. The game requires pupils to charge toward opponents, employing shoulder drops and swift maneuvers to evade the 'bulldogs' while racing to safety across the yard.Data from 2011, though dated, reveals telling statistics: over 25% of 653 school staff surveyed by the Association of Teachers and Lecturers reported their institutions had prohibited the activity. One secondary school educator bluntly explained the reasoning: because of the number of broken bones it generates!**Conkers Controversy Spreads Across Counties**Educational authorities in Wiltshire, Cumbria and Clackmannanshire implemented conker prohibitions, citing concerns that horse chestnuts might trigger severe anaphylactic reactions among vulnerable students.However, the Anaphylaxis Campaign advocated for a common sense approach instead, suggesting proper post-battle cleanup protocols where conkers are safely stored and participants thoroughly wash their hands.Some institutions found middle ground, permitting conker battles only when children wore protective goggles. A Carlisle headteacher defended this as a sensible precaution against flying horse chestnut fragments potentially injuring students' eyes.**Birthday Treats Become Classroom Casualties**Norbreck Primary Academy in Blackpool eliminated birthday cakes this January, with staff claiming they lacked sufficient time to verify ingredients for students with allergies. Parents received notification that any cakes brought to school would be sent home uneaten.The headteacher's message acknowledged the unpopular decision: I hate to be a killjoy... there are many reasons for this, some of them serious.**Footwear Fiasco Forces Mass Exodus**Birmingham students faced unexpected dismissal when Baverstock Academy in Druids Heath enforced new footwear regulations requiring plain black shoes exclusively. Letters detailing the compulsory rules prompted what one parent described as ridiculous and chaotic scenes, with approximately 300 children sent home.Parents later reported the school moderately relaxed these stringent requirements.**Pajama Police Target Parents**At Skerne Park Academy in Darlington, the headteacher addressed not student behavior but parental presentation. Adults conducting school runs were requested to wash each morning and avoid dropping off children while wearing pajamas.The situation reached a tipping point when parents appeared at parents' evenings and even the Christmas show still dressed in their PJs, according to the head.**Literary Limitations Over Religious Sensitivity**Barbara Harris, head teacher at Park Road Junior Infant and Nursery School in Batley, West Yorkshire, removed books featuring pig stories from key stage one classrooms to avoid potentially offending Muslim students.While the literature remained accessible in the school library, Harris explained: We try to be sensitive to the fact that for Muslims talk of pigs is offensive. The ban affected classes for children under seven.**Tinsel Triggers Safety Shutdown**Students in South Gloucestershire discovered their festive spirit curtailed when Chipping Sodbury school prohibited tinsel during a non-uniform day. Staff justified the restriction by citing litter concerns and potential dangers.Teachers warned the decorative material could cause injuries if pupils attempted to strangle each other with it. A letter sent home referenced health and safety reasons for the prohibition.The local council defended the event as being far from being against the spirit of Christmas, emphasizing its charitable purpose supporting Crisis.

text: Schools in Beijing are closed and outdoor construction halted as the Chinese capital's first ever pollution red alert came into effect. Beijing has issued its inaugural red alert for air pollution, marking a historic first since China adopted its four-tier warning system over two years ago. The maximum-level alert, announced late Monday, remains active until Thursday midday.The warning triggers significant restrictions: vehicle usage faces limitations while certain factories must cease operations entirely. This development coincides with China's participation in carbon emissions discussions in Paris, despite the nation holding the title of world's largest polluter.When the alert activated at 07:00 local time Tuesday (23:00 GMT Monday), the US Embassy's Beijing air quality monitor recorded PM 2.5 particle concentrations at 291 micrograms per cubic metre. Four hours later, readings showed a marginal improvement to 250 micrograms - still classified as very unhealthy. Suburban areas reported particle levels several times higher.The World Health Organization sets 25 micrograms per cubic metre as the maximum safe threshold.Cycling to work this morning with my smog mask securely fastened, I noticed noticeably lighter traffic. Beijing's inaugural red alert mandates that half of all vehicles remain off roads - odd-numbered license plates today, even-numbered tomorrow.Though the air appears unpleasantly grey and filthy, pollution indices actually register considerably lower than last week's levels, when dangerous particulate matter (PM 2.5) soared to approximately 40 times WHO's maximum guidelines. Today's reading represents merely 10 times that limit.Why implement red alert measures now? The absence of previous red alerts has generated increasingly vocal criticism. Last week, as children navigated through poisonous gloom to schools that remained open, citizens questioned what circumstances would finally prompt government action.Growing public pressure may have ultimately influenced this decision.Multiple factors contribute to the smog: coal-powered industries and heating systems, vehicle emissions, and construction site dust, all worsened by humidity and wind absence.The directive continues until Thursday 12:00, when an anticipated cold front should clear the smog.Beyond construction limitations and school advisories - institutions without adequate air filtration systems received closure recommendations - vehicles may only operate on alternating days based on license plate numbers ending in odd or even digits. Officials pledged additional public transportation to manage increased demand.**Analysis: Matt McGrath, BBC environment correspondent, Paris**China's air quality significantly influences its pursuit of a new global climate change agreement.Chinese negotiators emphasize continued renewable energy investments aimed at reducing coal consumption, particularly in urban centers. Approximately 58% of the country's primary energy consumption increase during 2013-14 originated from non-fossil fuel sources.While these environmental initiatives may not immediately improve Beijing's air quality, they have impacted global carbon dioxide output. Recently published figures reveal carbon levels have stagnated or slightly declined despite worldwide economic expansion.A robust Paris agreement won't instantly resolve China's air quality problems, but if it ultimately reduces renewable energy costs further, it could contribute to long-term solutions.You have to do whatever you can to protect yourself, Beijing resident Li Huiwen told AP news agency. Even when wearing the mask, I feel uncomfortable and don't have any energy.Weather conditions and geographical factors have intensified smog effects - the city borders industrial pollution-generating areas to the south and east, while northern and western mountains trap pollutants. This situation has heightened concerns that China has prioritized economic growth at excessive environmental expense.It is a sharp warning to us that we may have too much development at the price of environment and it is time for us to seriously deal with air pollution, said Beijing worker Fan Jinglong.The health consequences are enormous. According to a study led by Jos Lelieveld of Germany's Max Planck Institute and published in Nature magazine this year, air pollution has caused 1.4 million premature deaths in China.Last month, activists reported levels reaching 1,400 micrograms per cubic metre in northeastern Shenyang city, claiming it was China's worst recorded pollution.For comparison, London's December 6 PM 2.5 average measured 8 micrograms per cubic metre, according to King's College's Environmental Research Group. The group noted readings exceeding 70 during spring 2014 and 2015, with the highest recorded on November 5, 2006 (bonfire night) at 112.Last week, Greenpeace activists urged Chinese authorities to declare a red alert. Nanjing, another Chinese city, issued a red alert in December 2013.Beijing issued an orange alert - the second-highest level in the 2013-adopted four-tier system - on November 30.Capital pollution had actually improved during the year's first 10 months compared to the previous year's corresponding period, though pollution levels remained frequently elevated.Correspondents note that Chinese officials previously hesitated to commit to firm carbon emission reduction targets but now recognize the necessity of reducing fossil fuel dependence. President Xi Jinping pledged action on China's emissions during the Paris global climate change talks.Despite substantial renewable energy investments, China continues relying on coal for over 60% of its power generation.

text: An elderly woman was beheaded by a man who went on a rampage in north London, the Old Bailey has heard. Nicholas Salvador, a 25-year-old Enfield resident, stands accused of murdering 82-year-old Palmira Silva in a brutal garden attack that left her stabbed and beheaded, according to prosecutors who addressed the court.Armed with a machete and wooden pole, Salvador was eventually subdued after a chaotic confrontation requiring officers to deploy tasers six times before his arrest. The defendant has entered a plea of not guilty by reason of insanity to the murder charge.Prosecutor Jonathan Rees QC informed jurors that the fatal incident occurred just three days following Salvador's job termination. While there remains no question that Salvador killed Mrs Silva, the circumstances surrounding the September 4th afternoon attack paint a disturbing picture of mental deterioration.Living merely three doors from his victim on Nightingale Road, Salvador had been staying with a local family when his behavior became increasingly erratic. The court learned that on the day of the killing, he first turned his weapons against two cats belonging to his hosts, beheading both animals because he perceived them as demons.His violent rampage continued as he moved through neighboring back gardens, forced entry into a residence, and attacked a vehicle occupied by two family members from his temporary home. Salvador then scaled a wall into Mrs Silva's garden, where the fatal assault took place.According to Mr Rees, the defendant's distorted reality led him to believe he was confronting either a supernatural entity resembling a resurrected Hitler or a demon masquerading as an elderly woman.Following the murder, Salvador fled but was eventually cornered in another residence's front room. The ensuing arrest proved extraordinarily difficult, with officers struggling against a suspect who seemed impervious to multiple taser deployments, kicks, and punches. Throughout the ordeal, Salvador exhibited clear signs of mental disturbance, repeatedly chanting phrases including red is the colour and I am the king.Witness testimony described Salvador's pre-attack behavior as resembling a headless chicken, frantically searching for additional cats to kill. In the weeks preceding the violence, those around him had observed increasingly odd behaviour and his growing fascination with shapeshifters - mythical beings capable of transforming their appearance.Initially held at Belmarsh prison after being charged, Salvador was subsequently transferred to the high-security Broadmoor Hospital due to his deteriorating mental condition. Mr Rees indicated that psychiatric experts will testify regarding Salvador's diagnosis of paranoid schizophrenia.Mrs Silva's life story reflects that of many post-war immigrants who built new lives in Britain. Arriving from Italy in 1953, she established a cafe business alongside her husband and leaves behind two children, six grandchildren, and one great-grandchild.The defendant faces additional charges of assault causing actual bodily harm and assaulting a police officer, both contested on grounds of insanity. PC Bernard Hamilton sustained leg injuries requiring hospital treatment during Salvador's arrest.Proceedings in the case are ongoing.

text: Ahead of the general election on 7 May, BBC Radio Merseyside is holding three special debates in front of a live audience. Roger Phillips will moderate the inaugural hour-long debate at 12:00 BST in Wavertree, regarded as one of Liverpool's Labour strongholds. This constituency joins Southport and Wirral West as the three pivotal areas selected for these electoral discussions, offering voters direct access to quiz prospective representatives seeking five-year Westminster terms.Located east of Liverpool's city center, Wavertree maintains a largely residential character while housing an extensive technology park with strong university connections. The substantial student demographic significantly bolsters the area's economic vitality.Electoral concerns linger from 2010's administrative breakdown when Dunbabin Road's polling station exhausted ballot supplies just before closure. Liverpool City Council acknowledged that the problems last time at a small number of polling stations were caused by a number of people turning up at the close of polls and not all of the polling stations had a full allocation of ballot papers.Preventive measures now include ensuring all stations have a full allocation and additional training has been provided for staff. Also anyone in the queue by 22:00 BST will be given the chance to vote.Shadow health minister Luciana Berger secured Labour's position five years ago with over 7,000 votes to spare, succeeding Jane Kennedy, who represented the constituency since its 1997 creation before becoming Merseyside's Police Commissioner in 2012. Former Labour Councillor Jake Morrison briefly threatened to challenge Berger - Morrison was elected at 18 in 2011 but severed party ties last year, retiring at 22.Berger's re-election platform promises to take practical action to support people who are looking for a job, for example by holding another jobs fair to bring together employers and local people. I'll promote apprenticeships and opportunities for young people and back our fantastic small businesses.She added: I will continue to campaign for changes to law around dangerous dogs to make our neighbourhoods safer, and I will build on my strong record of standing up for the people of Liverpool Wavertree to ensure their concerns are heard where it matters and that real change is delivered for our community.The Liberal Democrats, unsuccessful in their 2010 targeting of this seat, now pin hopes on 20-year-old student Leo Evans. His agenda includes protecting green spaces like Calderstones Park, boosting NHS funding by £8bn annually with mental health emphasis, securing Liverpool's devolved power benefits - particularly HS2 and HS3 connections - and advancing the biggest expansion of apprenticeships since the 1950s.Conservative candidate James Pearson, a former Trafford councillor who unsuccessfully contested Liverpool City Council's Church ward last year, makes his parliamentary debut. This Army reserves officer, having served in Afghanistan and Cyprus, prioritizes supporting business investment, safeguarding NHS services, and advocating for armed forces families. However, his party's mere 7.5% vote share in 2010 makes victory unlikely.UKIP's Adam Heatherington, a former Liverpool mayoral candidate and supply teacher, targets disenchanted voters from both traditional parties. Citing Wavertree's below-average economic performance, he advocates increased investment in Wavertree Technology Park where there's a lot of vacant offices and retail spaces… business rates are just too high.We have a brain drain in this city - too many students are leaving to work in Manchester, Leeds and London. We need more of a focus on vocational qualifications and bring them up to equal par with academic qualifications and we need more investment in our young people, he said.Green party candidate Peter Cranie, the former election co-ordinator who narrowly missed European Parliament selection last year, acknowledges limited prospects while the party concentrates efforts on nearby Liverpool Riverside's Martin Dobson campaign. Nevertheless, he provides everyone in Wavertree the opportunity to express their support for the more radical policies against austerity.We think it is obscene that the five richest families in Britain own the same wealth as the 13 million least well-off, he said. That's why the Greens will commit to ending austerity and real redistribution of wealth for a fairer and better society.Council worker Dave Walsh represents the Trade Unionist and Socialist Coalition, seeking to get those who have been disenfranchised and disengaged in politics re-engaged while defending local services including libraries and Sure Start Centres. The party fields 130 candidates nationwide - their largest deployment - advocating £10 minimum wage and railway renationalization.Independent candidate Leo Evans, an 18-year-old Edge Hill student, discovered political engagement through Until They Kick Us Out, a Young Everyman Playhouse production exploring youth and democracy themes. His platform encompasses school leaver support, higher minimum wages, student and low-income rent caps, and social housing improvements. He maintains his campaign is more than just a protest vote.Seven candidates make Wavertree among Merseyside's most competitive constituencies. Listeners can hear candidate responses on BBC Radio Merseyside from 12:00 until 14:00.

text: Italian Prime Minister Mario Monti claimed Europe had one week to save the euro ahead of yet another crunch EU summit on Thursday and Friday. While France's president advocates for a growth pact and Tony Blair pushes for a grand bargain, with markets clamoring for a big bazooka and German voices murmuring about federalism, the eurozone crisis actually has surprisingly clear-cut economic and financial remedies.The solution? Simply examine how America - that other massive single currency zone functioning far more effectively - has tackled identical challenges.Europe's fundamental issue lies not in complex economics but in the political unpalatability of nearly every viable solution.At its core, the eurozone crisis stems from southern European economies becoming fundamentally uncompetitive. During boom years, wages escalated too rapidly, creating massive trade imbalances where imports far exceeded exports, with the deficit financed through borrowing.This toxic combination - excessive southern debt, persistent lack of competitiveness, continued borrowing needs, and Germany's hesitancy to provide funding - has triggered the financial panic making it exponentially harder for southern European governments and banks to access market financing.Compounding these problems, European financial markets have seized up while governments collectively pursue spending cuts and the European Central Bank maintains its price stability focus, threatening to plunge the entire continent into prolonged, deep recession that would only worsen debt burdens.Should the eurozone seek inspiration from the US model during this critical moment, what economic, financial, and ultimately political transformations might be necessary?**Immediate Banking Confidence**Europe's most urgent priority involves restoring banking sector confidence. All bad loans made by eurozone banks (loans to mortgage borrowers, property speculators and even governments that may not be fully repaid) may need to be cleaned up (by injecting money into the banks), with potential losses absorbed by the entire eurozone - since many national governments likely cannot shoulder these costs alone. Spain's current bailout arrangement exemplifies this problem, leaving the Spanish government bearing all losses.Deposits at all eurozone banks may need to be guaranteed in euros by the eurozone as a whole, preventing panicked investors from transferring funds from southern European banks (vulnerable to euro exit) to Germany, Switzerland, and Denmark.Additionally, all European banks may require placement under a common regime of regulation and supervision, providing troubled institutions equal rescue loan access while establishing central authority for winding up failed banks.**Long-term Government Solvency**Europe faces its greatest long-term puzzle in preventing government defaults by countries like Spain or Italy while restoring confidence in their euro commitment and ensuring future fiscal responsibility across all governments.The most contentious issue remains eurobonds. Substantial portions of eurozone government debt may require amalgamation - with governments backing each other's finances - to reinforce governmental commitment to euro membership.Long-term solutions might necessitate a US-style federal budget covering recession costs, preventing individual governments from facing bankruptcy during national economic downturns. For instance, minimum social security levels - particularly unemployment benefits - could be permanently shared across the eurozone, funded through common income taxation.**Growth and Reform Agenda**New French President Francois Hollande won election campaigning for a growth pact - reforms designed to boost European economies while mitigating pain from continent-wide government spending cuts.The European Central Bank may need mandate changes establishing explicit dual targets supporting both employment and price stability, mirroring the US Federal Reserve's approach as Hollande proposes.The eurozone might require large-scale investment in infrastructure, particularly in southern Europe, similar to West Germany's post-1990 East German reconstruction efforts. Current proposals include expanding the European Investment Bank's lending capacity and creating common project bonds for major construction financing.All Europeans, especially southerners, must implement structural reforms increasing long-term growth and strengthening government finances, despite short-term growth risks. These encompass removing market competition restrictions, raising retirement ages, reducing state employment over time, and facilitating hiring and firing processes. Hollande has resisted many such French reforms.**Economic Rebalancing**Rebalancing addresses the fundamental competitiveness problems that led southern Europeans to accumulate excessive debt initially.The ECB and German government may need to stimulate high wage inflation in Germany for several years, eliminating the country's massive competitive trade advantage over southern Europe - something that is already beginning to happen.Similar to Washington's assistance for struggling US states, southern European governments may require direct money transfers (given, not lent) from the broader eurozone via fiscal transfers, enabling them to support their economies until competitiveness returns. These transfers might ultimately become bailout loans never requiring repayment.Structural reforms, particularly labor market changes, remain crucial for rebalancing by ensuring southern European wages avoid the excessive increases of the past decade.**Political Integration Requirements**Creating a comprehensive banking, fiscal, and monetary union would require eurozone governments transferring power to a central authority (the European Commission) capable of financing and supervising all these measures, while national governments accept strictly limited future spending within their means.Since most reforms involve Germany sharing wealth with Europe while all nations surrender power to Brussels, Berlin demands no taxation without representation - essentially full federalism with spending and regulation controlled by a directly elected presidency of the European Commission.

text: And so it begins. Cardiff Bay's political atmosphere has already been charged with pre-election tension, and now the assembly's fifth electoral contest officially begins.While campaigning styles and events may seem recognizable, this election cycle brings unprecedented challenges. The EU referendum campaign creates a cacophonous environment where all parties must struggle to make their messages heard above the din.UKIP represents perhaps the most significant shift in the political landscape. For the first time, the party stands a genuine chance of securing multiple seats, potentially reshaping the assembly's entire political dynamic.Each major party confronts distinct obstacles. Labour faces a formidable triple challenge: defending their NHS stewardship record, projecting vitality after nearly two decades in power, and managing the uncertain electoral impact of UK leader Jeremy Corbyn in crucial marginal constituencies where Conservative opponents lurk.Following last year's devastating electoral performance, the Liberal Democrats must engineer a remarkable comeback from their crushing defeat.The Conservatives face the delicate task of preventing EU referendum divisions from undermining their Welsh momentum, particularly after achieving several striking general election victories.After enduring multiple disappointing electoral outcomes, Plaid Cymru desperately needs to generate meaningful campaign momentum.UKIP confronts both unprecedented opportunity and significant risk. While positioned to potentially elect several AMs—establishing their first meaningful institutional foothold across the UK—persistent internal divisions continue to plague the party.The incoming Welsh Government will wield greater authority than any predecessor, yet the NHS—devolved since 1999—is expected to dominate campaign discourse.Future policy-makers must navigate the complex challenge of supporting a financially strained health service while simultaneously maintaining investment in education and economic development.Despite broad inter-party agreement on initiatives like apprenticeship programs and small business rate relief, deeply divisive issues including the proposed M4 relief road and council reorganization present voters with stark choices.Turnout remains unpredictable after reaching 42% previously. While the EU referendum threatens to overshadow assembly politics, sustained media coverage of NHS issues over recent years has simultaneously elevated public awareness of devolution's significance.

text: Mfon Udoh scored a hat-trick as Nigeria's Enyimba beat visitors Etoile du Sahel of Tunisia 3-0 in the first leg of their last 16 African Champions League tie on Sunday. Enyimba's striker Udoh delivered a masterclass performance, netting a hat-trick that positioned him as the tournament's leading scorer with seven goals. His opening strike came nine minutes into the match, followed by a second goal after the interval, before sealing his treble with a thunderous effort in the dying moments.The Nigerian side's victory was aided when Etoile du Sahel were reduced to ten players. Ghazi Abderazek received his marching orders after collecting a second yellow card for dissent, leaving his team to battle through the final 19 minutes a man down.This encounter marks a rematch of the 2004 final, where Enyimba ultimately triumphed on penalties following 2-1 home victories for both sides across the two legs.Meanwhile, in Kinshasa on Sunday, AS Vita Club of DR Congo secured a crucial 1-0 victory over South Africa's Mamelodi Sundowns. Uganda's Dennis Onyango produced several outstanding saves to keep Sundowns competitive, repeatedly thwarting Vita Club's Ghanaian sensation Bernard Morrison.The decisive moment arrived during stoppage time when Morrison, afforded excessive space once more, saw his effort parried by Onyango. However, the rebound fell kindly to Kule Mbombo, who made no mistake with the finish.The winners of these ties will advance to the group stages, while the defeated teams will receive another opportunity in the Confederation Cup.Defending champions TP Mazembe, Vita's compatriots, face an uphill battle following Saturday's 2-0 defeat to Morocco's Wydad Casablanca in Marrakech. Abdellatif Noussir opened his tournament account just before the break, while Reda Hajhouj doubled the advantage from the penalty spot midway through the second period.Under the guidance of former Real Madrid manager John Toshack, Wydad seeks their second continental triumph, having previously conquered the competition in 1992. Mazembe, meanwhile, pursues a sixth title that would establish them as the second most decorated club behind Egypt's Al Ahly, who boast eight championships.Saturday also witnessed record holders Al Ahly secure a 1-1 stalemate away to Young Africans in Tanzania. The Cairo Red Devils, now managed by ex-Tottenham boss Martin Jol, struck early through Amr Gamal's 11th-minute header, claiming a valuable away goal. Young Africans responded eight minutes later, leveling through an unfortunate Ahmed Hegazi own-goal.Al Ahly's fierce rivals Zamalek, directed by another former English Premier League manager Alex McLeish, comfortably dispatched Algerian newcomers Mouloudia Bejaia 2-0 in Cairo. Mahmoud 'Kahraba' Abdel Moneim broke the deadlock approaching the hour mark, before Ahmed Hamoudi sealed victory eight minutes from full-time.Ivory Coast's Asec Mimosas capitalized on home soil to defeat Al Ahly Tripoli of Libya 2-0. Dao Youssouf opened the scoring after 59 minutes, with Aka Serge adding the insurance goal ten minutes before the final whistle.Al Merreikh of Sudan and Algeria's Entente Setif battled to a 2-2 draw in their second consecutive seasonal meeting. Saturday's encounter saw Merreikh fall behind to Eude Dagoulou's 15th-minute opener. Raji Abdalati restored parity five minutes later, only for Abdelmoumene Djabou to restore Setif's advantage within three minutes. However, Abdalati's second strike of the evening ensured the first leg concluded level at 2-2.Mali's hopes of securing their first-ever qualifier suffered a severe blow as Stade Malien succumbed to a shocking 3-1 home defeat against Zambia's Zesco United. Despite Moussakoye Diallo's early opener providing initial optimism, Mwape Mwelwa equalized before the interval, setting the stage for Idris Ilunga's decisive late double.

text: The HS2 link between Birmingham and Crewe marks a sad day for Stoke-on-Trent, Tristram Hunt has said. Transport Secretary Patrick McLoughlin's suggestion to build a junction in South Staffordshire serving Stoke-on-Trent comes as the HS2 Birmingham to Crewe section prepares for its 2027 opening.The 43-mile HS2 stretch connecting Birmingham and Crewe will now launch six years ahead of the original timeline under revised plans. This development forms part of the broader HS2 project designed to enhance transport connections with northern England, while the government targets completion of the London to Birmingham route by 2026.Crewe's selection over Stoke-on-Trent as the crucial staging point toward Manchester has sparked significant debate. The city had previously submitted a bid for an HS2 railway station within its centre.City MP Mr Hunt criticized the decision, arguing the London to Manchester line could have been achieved more quickly and cheaply with a route through the Potteries. Addressing Crewe's selection over his city, Labour MP Mr Hunt stated: With Crewe rather than Stoke benefitting from this massive investment, plans for a northern gateway partnership between Stoke-on-Trent and east Cheshire become more important.Mark Winnington, who represents economy, environment and transport on Staffordshire County Council, condemned the current route as environmentally destructive and damaging to local communities. HS2 will cut through 45 miles of Staffordshire countryside and from the outset we have been concerned about the impact a project of this scale will have not only on the environment but also on residents living close to the proposed route, Mr Winnington explained. He characterized the route as cutting through extensive countryside areas, calling it a big blow to affected communities.Crewe's six-year monopoly as the North West's sole HS2 connection theoretically positions Cheshire to fulfill its self-proclaimed role as gateway to the Northern Powerhouse. However, this outcome hardly surprises observers, given that the government-owned HS2 company consistently recommended Crewe for a station stop.The decision undoubtedly disappoints Stoke-on-Trent, which mounted a competitive bid for hub status and even threatened legal action upon potential failure. Government officials and Cheshire representatives now pledge to ensure North Staffordshire experiences high-speed rail benefits.Cheshire East Council leader Michael Jones hailed the HS2 Birmingham to Crewe connection as a game-changer for Crewe and surrounding areas. It's a real once-in-a-generation opportunity, the like of which Cheshire East has not seen before, he declared.Environmental concerns persist among local representatives. Conservative MP for Lichfield, Michael Fabricant, branded the announced route environmentally damaging to beautiful parts of Staffordshire.Distance remains a practical concern for constituents. Labour MP for Stoke-on-Trent South, Robert Flello, highlighted accessibility issues: Crewe might look on a map [as if it is] next door to Stoke-on-Trent but the reality is it's a good hour by car from my constituents.Conservative MP for Stafford, Jeremy Lefroy, urged Mr McLoughlin to look again at the proposed route.Further updates on this story and others on Stoke and Staffordshire continue to develop as the project advances.
dipper: The HS2 link between Birmingham and Crewe marks a sad day for Stoke-on-Trent, Tristram Hunt has said. But there is also a certain question of the value of the connection between London and Manchester. The choice of Crewe instead of Stoke-on-Trent as the strategic hub for the route to Manchester has led to much controversy; the city had previously bid for an HS2 station in its centre; and the MP for the city, Mr Hunt, criticised the decision, arguing that the London-to-Manchester line could be completed more quickly and at less expense if it passed through the Potteries. The 43-mile HS2 section from Birmingham to Crewe will now be completed six years ahead of the original timetable, and the government expects to complete the route from London to Birmingham by 2026. Mark Winnington, a member of the county council for economy, environment and transport, called the current route "ecologically destructive" and damaging to the local communities. He said the route would cut through an extensive area of countryside and be a great blow to affected communities. In connection with the choice of Crewe over his city, the Labour MP, Mr Hunt, said: With Crewe instead of the city benefiting from this huge investment, the plans for a northern gateway partnership between Stoke and east Cheshire are becoming more important. The decision undoubtedly disappoints those from the city of Stoke-on-Trent, which made a bid for a hub and threatened to sue if it failed. However, this is hardly a surprise for those following the process, because the government-owned HS2 company has always recommended that a station be established in the town. Government officials and Cheshire representatives have now pledged to ensure that North Staffs benefits from the HS2 project. The Conservative Member of Parliament for Lichfield, Michael Fabricant, has branded the route proposed as a blight on the natural beauty of parts of Staffordshire. The Conservative Member of Parliament for Stafford, Jeremy Lefroy, has urged the Transport Secretary to think again about the route. Distances remain a practical problem for constituents; Robert Flello, the Labour Member of Parliament for the southern district of the city, pointed out that while it looks as though the railway station at Crewe is just next to the town, in reality it is a good hour’s drive from my constituents.

text: An own goal from goalkeeper Ryan Clarke in the 95th minute denied Neal Ardley's AFC Wimbledon their first win of the season as Rochdale earned a share of the spoils at the Crown Oil Arena. Rochdale's late equalizer through an unfortunate own goal denied AFC Wimbledon a crucial victory that would have lifted them from League One's relegation zone.The visitors appeared destined for three vital points after Andy Barcham's first-half header, but goalkeeper Clarke's misfortune in the dying moments - punching Jamie Allen's corner into his own net - left Wimbledon rooted to the bottom of the table.Wimbledon seized the initiative early, capitalizing on Rochdale's defensive miscommunication after just 12 minutes. The breakthrough came from an unlikely source when Donal McDermott's corner was inadvertently returned to him by Matt Lund. McDermott's subsequent attempt to beat Chris Whelpdale ended in dispossession deep within Wimbledon's half.Whelpdale seized the opportunity brilliantly, surging the full length of the pitch down the right flank before delivering a precise cross. Barcham met the delivery perfectly, directing his header beyond Conrad Logan to give the Dons an early advantage.The second half saw Rochdale intensify their pursuit of an equalizer. Jamie Allen came agonizingly close when his thunderous effort crashed against the crossbar, while Clarke twice thwarted Calvin Andrew's attempts to restore parity.Rochdale's comeback hopes appeared to diminish when Callum Camps received his marching orders for a second bookable offense, reducing the home side to ten men. However, Clarke's earlier heroics counted for nothing when he inadvertently diverted Allen's corner kick into his own goal deep into stoppage time.The dramatic finale leaves AFC Wimbledon still searching for the points needed to escape League One's bottom four, while Rochdale will feel satisfied with salvaging a draw despite their numerical disadvantage.Report supplied by the Press Association. text: A schoolgirl has become the first child in Wales to be given an official hearing dog. Among the UK's 45,000 children living with deafness, 14-year-old Poppy represents a remarkable success story. Her profound hearing loss, paired with a yellow Labrador companion, has transformed from a source of isolation into a pathway toward greater confidence and peaceful nights.Through the charity Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, Poppy became one of just 27 children across the UK to receive a specially trained hearing dog. Her journey to this partnership began when subtle behavioral shifts caught the attention of her parents, civil engineer Richard and housewife Rebecca, when she reached nine years old.She was turning the volume up on the TV, Rebecca recalled. When she was in the car she wouldn't hear me when I was talking to her, even though her brothers and sister could hear in the back.These concerns prompted a referral to an audiologist, who made a startling discovery about the Cwmbran, Torfaen schoolgirl. Poppy was profoundly deaf and could barely detect sound, yet had masterfully concealed this through lip-reading skills that fooled everyone around her.Her academic performance remained unaffected, masking the early warning signs of her condition. Rebecca explained: What we realised when she was diagnosed was that she had become quite proficient in lip reading, which was how she had managed to wing her way through school. No-one had noticed as there was no change in her schoolwork.Medical professionals diagnosed Poppy with Autoimmune Polyendocrine Syndrome type 1, a rare disease. While hearing aids for both ears provided some assistance during waking hours, nighttime brought particular challenges. Without her hearing aids, complete silence left her anxious and unable to sleep peacefully, constantly worried about unexpected intrusions into her room.Social situations became increasingly difficult. Simple tasks like shopping alone seemed insurmountable, and Poppy grew more withdrawn despite her hearing aids. This isolation persisted for three years until Rebecca discovered hearing dogs—canine companions that assist deaf individuals much like guide dogs help the visually impaired. Currently, 850 deaf people throughout the UK, predominantly adults, benefit from these partnerships.Due to her profound hearing loss, Poppy achieved a historic milestone as Wales' first child to receive a hearing dog. The specially trained companion was christened Tanni, honoring Baroness Tanni Grey Thompson, and represented one of only 12 dogs distributed that particular year.One year later, Poppy credits Tanni with revolutionizing her daily existence.Having her has built my confidence, Poppy explained. She gives me more independence. Before when my mum went out I would be left at home, now I can go with her and go into shops. Before I was very reluctant to go into a shop and pay by myself. I was worried as they wouldn't know I was deaf, but now they can see from Tanni that they need to speak clearly as she wears a special harness when we're out.The partnership extends beyond practical assistance. Another good thing is that people ask questions about Tanni and I feel happy talking about her. It has made me more confident answering questions in general, Poppy noted. I have got a best friend.Tanni accompanies Poppy everywhere except school, having received specialized training to alert her owner to fire alarms and maternal summons. Morning wake-up calls and message delivery represent core aspects of Tanni's duties.She wakes me up in the morning, if my mum wants to let me know we are going out or it is tea time she will write a note and put it in a purse which Tanni then brings in her mouth to me. So she will come up to get me and then nudges me, Poppy described.Future training possibilities include responses to doorbells, phone calls, and text messages as Poppy matures and gains independence.Perhaps most significantly, Tanni has restored Poppy's ability to sleep soundly. I used to sleep with the door open as I didn't know who was coming in to the room, I had the bed so I could see straight down the landing with the door open, she revealed. Now Tanni wakes me up if someone comes in, so I can sleep with the door shut.Andrew James, National Client Services Manager for Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, expressed enthusiasm about the program's expansion. We have now placed 27 hearing dogs with deaf children across the UK, and we are so pleased that Poppy and Tanni are the first child partnership in Wales.Since launching in 2012, the Hearing Dogs for Deaf Children project has demonstrated remarkable success, with growing annual interest prompting plans for further expansion. Hearing dogs have an important influence on a deaf child's life, and we couldn't be happier with the positive difference that Tanni has made to Poppy and her family, James concluded.Wales currently hosts 29 deaf individuals partnered with hearing dogs, with Poppy and Tanni representing a pioneering achievement in pediatric hearing assistance.

text: Six years ago Yingluck Shinawatra, a novice who had only been in politics for two months, led the Pheu Thai party, founded and funded by her older brother Thaksin, to a resounding election victory. The verdict against Yingluck Shinawatra represents a remarkable turn of events for a political party that had previously witnessed two administrations toppled through military intervention and disputed judicial rulings. Just a year earlier, her supporters had occupied Bangkok's streets in protests that culminated in violent confrontations.Central to Yingluck's electoral victory was an ambitious pledge to Thailand's rice farmers - a promise that now forms the crux of her legal troubles.The controversial rice subsidy program committed the government to purchasing the nation's entire rice harvest at 15,000 baht (£350; $450) per tonne, substantially exceeding the previous administration's guarantee of 11,000 baht. Farmers embraced the policy enthusiastically.However, economists and agricultural specialists immediately raised concerns about the scheme's feasibility. Thailand held the position as the world's leading rice exporter, yet the guaranteed price of 15,000 baht far exceeded global market rates. Experts predicted that competing nations like India and Vietnam would capitalize on Thailand's pricing disadvantage, capturing market share by offering rice at prices well below what the Thai government could match without sustaining massive financial losses. Corruption warnings accompanied these economic concerns.Now, six years after implementing the program, Yingluck confronts potential imprisonment of up to 10 years on malfeasance charges - specifically dereliction of duty regarding the rice scheme. While not directly accused of corruption, she faces allegations of failing to prevent it during her tenure as prime minister and chair of the National Rice Policy Committee.A conviction would result in a permanent political ban, adding to the five-year prohibition imposed following her 2015 impeachment.Predictably, Yingluck and her political allies have denounced the proceedings as unfair.The same military officers who orchestrated her government's 2014 overthrow now control Thailand. They justified their coup as necessary for restoring stability, yet notably withheld support as sustained Bangkok protests paralyzed her administration. The military's impartiality remains questionable, particularly given its authoritarian influence extending into judicial matters.The rice program proved extraordinarily costly and inefficient. Precise figures for losses from rotting grain, theft, and improper sales remain contested. Government estimates place state losses at minimum $8bn, though some calculations reach $20bn - figures that encompass both corruption-related losses and overall subsidy expenses.While the scheme improved farmers' living conditions, its long-term sustainability appeared doubtful.Corruption evidence exists anecdotally, though few cases have reached court. The most prominent case involves a former commerce minister and 27 co-defendants accused of fraudulent government-to-government rice sales to China - with verdicts scheduled for the same day as Yingluck's judgment.During court proceedings, Yingluck maintained she bore no responsibility for daily scheme operations and argued that canceling a key electoral platform exceeded her authority. She identified what she considers numerous procedural irregularities in her case.Regardless of the case's legal merits, observers widely believe the military government seeks to diminish Thaksin Shinawatra's political influence before permitting democratic restoration.Yingluck remains highly popular and politically effective. With Thaksin approaching his tenth year in exile, his party struggles to identify successor leadership.Her fate presents Thailand's current leadership with complex challenges.An acquittal might embolden Thaksin, who fiercely protects his younger sister, to demand greater post-election power sharing than the military would tolerate. Such an outcome would infuriate conservative hardliners and former anti-Yingluck protesters.Imprisonment would satisfy Shinawatra opponents and completely eliminate her from politics. A conviction would also provide retrospective justification for the generals' coup as anti-corruption action.Yet conviction risks transforming the photogenic Yingluck into a resistance symbol for the red-shirt movement supporting her.Red-shirt leadership acknowledges that organizing large-scale protests under military rule would prove difficult. They've rejected repeating the central Bangkok occupation that ended disastrously seven years ago.However, they would interpret conviction as the opening salvo in renewed military conflict, ending reconciliation pretenses. Localized demonstrations by Yingluck supporters remain possible.This prospect concerns the government, which desires tranquility preceding October's elaborate cremation ceremony for late King Bhumibol Adulyadej. Officials must also consider King Vajiralongkorn's preferences, as his coronation ceremony will likely follow the cremation.A suspended sentence might offer compromise, possible if Yingluck receives less than five years. Even with custodial sentencing, legal experts note appeal options exist - though this depends on her decision.Underlying these proceedings is maneuvering for new power arrangements once generals permit elections.Polling suggests Pheu Thai will emerge as the largest party, maintaining its position since 2001, though new electoral systems will likely prevent lower house majorities.Political parties must contend with a 250-seat military-appointed senate and a military-drafted 20-year reform blueprint that legally binds all future governments.In this environment, the next prime minister's identity remains uncertain. Previously, elected Thai governments concentrated significant power and patronage - an arrangement that will no longer exist.Some Pheu Thai members believe opposition status might benefit the party, arguing that the first elected government will face such constraints from courts and generals that power isn't worth pursuing.The military itself contains factions, and current leadership dominance isn't guaranteed. King Vajiralongkorn's intentions represent another crucial unknown.Thailand's lese majeste laws prevent domestic discussion of his role, but he has already demonstrated his desire for consultation on major decisions and willingness to exercise influence differently than his father.He may emerge as among the most significant forces reshaping Thailand's future.

text: The medical director of the UK hospital where Pakistani girl Malala Yousafzai is being treated has said doctors are impressed with her strength and resilience. A 14-year-old Pakistani schoolgirl who was targeted by Taliban gunmen for advocating girls' education continues her recovery at a Birmingham hospital, though medical officials warn her journey to full health remains uncertain.Malala, who gained international recognition through her educational activism, arrived at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on Monday night via air ambulance, nearly a week after the devastating attack in Pakistan's Swat Valley. The assault occurred as she and two classmates returned from school in Mingora, when a gunman boarded their van, specifically asked for her by name, and fired three shots at her head.Dr David Rosser, overseeing her care, expressed cautious optimism about the teenager's condition. There's a long way to go and she is not out of the woods yet... but at this stage we're optimistic that things are going in the right direction, he stated, noting that while progress has been encouraging, significant challenges lie ahead.The hospital has implemented stringent security measures following Taliban threats to target Malala again. West Midlands police maintain a visible presence to manage unauthorized visitors, having already turned away well-wishers on Monday evening who hoped to see the young activist. Dr Rosser acknowledged the situation as irritating but confirmed that hospital administrators and security partners remain comfortable with security arrangements.Pakistan's President Asif Ali Zardari, speaking from Azerbaijan on Tuesday, condemned the attack in stark terms. The Taliban attack on the 14-year-old girl, who from the age of 11 was involved in the struggle for education for girls, is an attack on all girls in Pakistan, an attack on education, and on all civilised people, he declared, characterizing the assault as targeting civilised people everywhere.Malala's reputation as an education advocate stems from her early courage in challenging Taliban restrictions. In 2009, at just 11 years old, she began writing an anonymous diary for BBC Urdu, documenting daily life under Taliban rule after the militant group banned girls from attending school in her region.Medical specialists anticipate that her recovery will require extensive neurological intervention and surgical procedures to repair or replace damaged skull bones once her condition stabilizes sufficiently for such complex treatments.
